docs.title: Trials at the Shore: Mutiny, Missing Papers, and a Race Against the Tide
Events and Actions
docs.text:
The session began with Werner recapping the previous night's successful, albeit risky, smuggling operation for Knick Nab, who was absent. The recap turned up a couple of loose threads worth chewing on: every barrel they'd carried down the tunnel — even the ones packed with ordinary luxuries like preserved quail eggs — had held a slip of paper scrawled in some unreadable script, which the party took for a cipher of some kind, and Burlyman admitted the black powder among the goods wasn't his usual cargo but was fetching an unusually high price with the war on. They also noted that the guard rotation they'd slipped past looked to be new standard practice now that the coast was being watched, meaning the trick that worked once wasn't one they could simply repeat — though the replacement pair, Evans and Fursa, had seemed noticeably less disciplined than the first watch and might be worth cultivating if Burlyman needed the run done again. After the recap, most of the exhausted party went to rest in their room at The Crow's Nest. Mani, however, stayed awake to train with Randolph the Chronicler, who brought out a pair of wooden fighting sticks — a cruder, more brutal Navy training weapon than the rapier Mani was used to — and explained that a blade's elegance sometimes has to give way to practicality in close quarters. Mani insisted on saluting him formally before the bout despite Randolph's warning that such courtesy wasn't customary among fighters of this style, then fought well enough despite his exhaustion to land a solid strike on his tutor's knee. Randolph, impressed but wary of pushing him further while so tired, called an early halt. Mani confided that he and his friends had taken on Burlyman's night work because he couldn't otherwise afford his room and board, but promised he would show up for training every day regardless of how tired or beaten he was.

Around noon, the party awoke. Mani, Cosimo, and Werner headed down to their hidden clubhouse (the "Batcave") to offer prayers of thanks for their recent success, while Knick Nab and Riu stayed behind in the bustling common room to eavesdrop. Sitting with their own thoughts for a moment, the group reflected that as long as they stayed close to The Crow's Nest, they were safe — Knick Nab from the Handler he'd fled, Cosimo from the church, Noddy from tax collectors. In the common room, Knick Nab and Riu overheard sailors discussing the unexpected return of the warship HMS Advance, previously thought lost. Its captain, Maynard, was missing, and the first lieutenant, Barrows, was under suspicion, with a public court-martial scheduled for four bells that afternoon. Satisfied he'd learned what he could for now, Riu headed down to join the prayer, crawling into the clubhouse so quietly that Mani — still jumpy after an earlier scare with a rat — very nearly ran him through with sword and knife before recognizing him. In the clubhouse, Cosimo led the group in a short invocation to the Mother and Father, thanking them for allowing the party "to step without sound, to touch without being felt, and to succeed without loss," and threw a pinch of gunpowder onto the braziers for a dramatic flare that visibly impressed everyone present. As the flare died down, Mani capped the ceremony with a small verse of his own — "success without loss, forge friendship through adversity, sunrise bestowed grace" — half prayer, half boast.

Knick Nab remained upstairs, gathering more details. His first attempt to question a sailor was brushed off, but buying a grizzled old sailor a drink loosened his tongue: the Advance had been part of a major northern offensive meant to crush a gathering of the Southern Navy in its home waters, an operation the North's admirals were confident of winning outright. Instead, the Southern fleet out-sailed and out-maneuvered them at every turn, scattering the northern ships and inflicting a defeat that has badly shaken confidence in the war at sea. It was in the wake of that battle that the Advance vanished, presumed lost, before limping back into port starving and without her captain.

The party regrouped, and Knick Nab shared the news. They decided to attend the court-martial. Werner purchased some commoner clothes and a small backpack, changing out of his finer clothes and stowing them away, since dockside work had already ruined his good outfit. Weighing what to carry, the party judged daggers and throwing knives were unremarkable enough to pass, but a sword or a set of harpoons on a child would draw stares, and a pistol would have to stay hidden entirely to avoid worse trouble. Along the way, Werner walked the others through what he knew of naval discipline: minor offenses earn a flogging — anywhere from a handful of lashes up to being lashed around the fleet — but anything warranting more than twenty-four lashes, including a death sentence, requires a formal court-martial attended by two ranking captains and a pair of priests, whether the accused is a common sailor or a captain. Keelhauling, he noted, was a pirate practice the Northern Navy didn't use; talk of mutiny in particular is treated so severely it almost always ends in death regardless. The group (Mani, Cosimo, Werner, Riu, and Knick Nab) then headed to the shore in Low Town where the tribunal was taking place. Noddy was not mentioned as accompanying them and was presumably resting or elsewhere in the inn.

The scene at the shore was crowded, with gallows erected in the middle of a cleared space between an official stone building — fine steps, pillars, a walled garden — and the dock and rocks marking the waterline. Guarded grandstand-style seating had been set up along the garden's edge, and the crowd was thick enough that sailors and ordinary townsfolk had settled into their own separate clusters, with more people still filing down from the town above. Present were Admiral Denys, Vice Admiral Codemar, Prelate Frederick, Prince Piers, Mistress Mary (seated near the Prince), and Randolph the Chronicler, watching through a looking glass and jotting notes in his book. Knick Nab spotted other young pickpockets working the crowd, including Stick Stab, who recognized him at once, seemed startled he'd gone independent, and — after being handed a couple of bronze coins to keep quiet — promised not to mention having seen him, adding that Knick Nab could always find him if he ever wanted to go independent himself.

Admiral Denys opened the tribunal, announcing it was held under the authority of the Crown as witnessed by Prince Piers, and had the prisoners brought out in irons — six sailors of the Advance, plus Lieutenant Barrows, unshackled and carrying his sword and satchel, walking in of his own accord behind them. Each accused sailor was read the same charge — an article against uttering any words of sedition or mutiny, or making mutinous assemblies, on whatever penalty the court-martial saw fit to inflict — and Barrows testified against them in turn as the tribunal's chief witness. Nearby, two boys in the crowd took up gleeful chants of their own, one crying "Hang him!" and the other "Chop off his head!" — a reminder that not everyone present saw this as anything but a show. The first sailor claimed the lieutenant "had no cause to be in command" and was endangering the ship; found guilty, he was hanged the old-fashioned way, hoisted and left to strangle and kick rather than dropped, a slow death that visibly unsettled the watching party and drew a low groan from the crowd as he finally went still. The second sailor accused Barrows of abandoning Captain Maynard and endangering the ship; he was found guilty and beheaded cleanly in a single stroke by the executioner, who checked the kill with his knife before the body and head were tossed into a waiting cart and sawdust thrown down over the blood. Throughout, Riu kept one eye on Mistress Mary near the Prince, unable to shake the sense that her presence there meant something — he noted that she barely watched the first man's slow strangulation, looking away, and that she averted her eyes again at the second man's beheading, no closer to an explanation either way. Noddy, who had apparently followed the party or attended separately, chose to leave after the second execution and head back to The Crow's Nest, growing steadily more fatigued on the walk. A third and fourth sailor were tried and executed in turn, each giving much the same account — that Barrows had no right to command, or had abandoned the captain — though the details shifted slightly from telling to telling.

When a young cabin boy, about fourteen, was brought forth, Mani and Knick Nab tried to start a "Let Him Live" chant among the crowd, but it failed to catch on. Cosimo tried a different tack, offering a quiet prayer invoking the Mother's mercy on the boy's behalf, but that appeal fared no better. The cabin boy was found guilty. Werner and Mani, unwilling to witness the execution of a peer, left the proceedings. Riu, meanwhile, had grown fixated on an old woman with a horse cart at the edge of the crowd, certain her presence there meant something. As the boy was dragged to the block, Riu strode over and slapped the horse's rump, hoping to spook it into some kind of intervention — the horse barely reacted, and the old woman only looked at him and said, "I can only influence the fates of so many, and the little boy is not one of them," before turning her cart and driving away. The cabin boy was then beheaded.

Before anyone knew a word about missing papers, Knick Nab tried to whip up a "Hang him!" chant of his own against Barrows, purely for sport — it went nowhere, unlike the boys' earlier chants, and he would reverse his position entirely within minutes. Finally, Lieutenant Barrows himself was called forward to answer for deserting his duty and Captain Maynard. His charge was read separately from the others': that he had basely deserted his duty and station and run while the enemy was engaged, or enticed others to do so, an offense punishable by death or whatever lesser sentence the court saw fit. He testified that Maynard, before disappearing ashore with a landing party, had left him written orders — countersigned by the ship's second lieutenant — to sail on without him if he did not return within two days, and that he'd had those papers in his satchel when he arrived that very afternoon. When pressed to produce them, he found his satchel empty. He tore through it in mounting panic, at one point pulling out nothing more useful than a chart covered in navigational figures, before admitting the orders were simply gone; the ship's logs, he said, had likewise gone missing after the captain's disappearance, and he could only presume Maynard had taken them. Riu spotted a street urchin bolt away from the area moments after Barrows had stepped aside earlier to wait his turn, and quietly told Knick Nab what he'd seen. Knick Nab worked his way closer and confirmed Barrows still had his purse and sword — ruling out an ordinary pickpocketing — then stepped forward as a witness, testifying that he'd seen a boy of his own trade lift something other than a purse from the lieutenant's satchel. Barrows seized on this, but without the papers themselves the tribunal found him guilty regardless.

Given the chance to speak with Prelate Frederick before sentencing, Barrows apparently requested his own manner of death — a considerable gamble — and the tribunal granted it: he was to be suspended by the ankles above the water at the bridge, to drown only once the tide rose far enough to reach him. The party's own knowledge of tides and the sea (confirmed by several Survival and Sailor rolls) put that at roughly twelve hours away. The big executioner stripped Barrows of his jacket, sword, and belongings, tied the rope to his ankles, and hauled him up over the water with a guard posted to make sure no one cut him down early. As he was led off, Barrows begged Knick Nab directly to find the papers and clear his name, while Mistress Mary was seen tugging at Prince Piers' sleeve and gesturing toward Knick Nab, clearly troubled by what she'd witnessed.

Werner, upon returning to the inn, also felt unusually fatigued. The remaining party members (Knick Nab, Cosimo, Riu, and Mani) sprinted back to The Crow's Nest to regroup with Werner and Noddy. They agreed the theft had to be deliberate — no street thief goes for papers over a full purse — and debated two threads to pull: track down whoever had actually taken the papers, or figure out who stood to benefit from Barrows hanging, be it a rival noble house or someone within the Admiralty itself. They judged the papers the more perishable lead and resolved to start with Stick Stab and Knick Nab's old safe house, while being wary of storming in outright — since Knick Nab had deserted that crew and risked punishment for returning, they preferred to send a known face in first rather than walk into a den of his former associates uninvited. They also discussed asking Mistress Clara what she might know, though decided that could wait, and agreed the party's common fund — which Riu had taken it upon himself to track, and confirmed at fifty silver — could be used to buy the papers back if it came to that, rather than force.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• The party learned that the HMS Advance had been part of a major northern naval offensive meant to crush a gathering of the Southern Navy in its home waters — an operation the North was confident of winning outright, until the Southern fleet out-maneuvered and scattered them, badly denting northern confidence in the war at sea. It was in that battle's aftermath that the Advance vanished, before returning much later without her captain and starving.
  • In recapping the previous night's smuggling run, the party recalled that every barrel — even ones holding ordinary luxuries — had contained a slip of paper covered in an unreadable script, seemingly some kind of cipher; Burlyman admitted the black powder among the goods was unusually profitable given the wartime shortage, though he denied any involvement in an insurrection.
  • The party recognized that the previous night's ruse of drugging the guards likely can't be repeated, since the coast watch appears to be a new standing wartime procedure; they noted the newer pair of guards, Evans and Fursa, seemed less disciplined than the first watch and might be worth cultivating if a further run is ever needed.
  • Werner explained naval discipline to the others: minor offenses earn a flogging, but anything warranting more than twenty-four lashes — including a death sentence — requires a formal court-martial with two ranking captains and a pair of priests in attendance, regardless of the rank of the accused. Keelhauling was a pirate practice, not something the Northern Navy used; talk of mutiny in particular is treated so severely it almost always ends in death regardless.
  • They witnessed the brutal process of a naval court-martial, including hangings, beheadings, and the differing (and not entirely consistent) accounts each mutineer gave for turning against Lieutenant Barrows.
  • Riu slapped the old woman with the horse cart's horse hoping to spook it into intervening for the cabin boy; it didn't work, and she told him only, "I can only influence the fates of so many, and the little boy is not one of them," before driving off.
  • Riu grew increasingly convinced that Mistress Mary's presence beside Prince Piers meant something more than coincidence, watching her reactions throughout the proceedings without reaching any conclusion.
  • Lieutenant Barrows claimed his orders from Captain Maynard were written down but stolen by a young thief; he also testified that the ship's logs had gone missing after the captain's disappearance, and he could only presume Maynard had taken them himself.
  • Knick Nab corroborated seeing a theft from Barrows' satchel, having confirmed first that Barrows' purse and sword were untouched.
  • Barrows apparently requested his own manner of execution — suspended over the water to drown with the tide — buying himself roughly twelve hours rather than a swift death; the party's own Survival and Sailor knowledge confirmed the tide's timing.
  • The party discussed the likelihood that the papers were deliberately stolen to ensure Barrows' conviction, weighing whether a rival noble house or the Admiralty itself might be behind it, but judged that lead less time-sensitive than tracking down the papers directly.
  • The party decided to attempt to find the stolen papers within the 12-hour deadline to save Lieutenant Barrows, planning to approach Knick Nab's old crew cautiously — sending a known face in rather than walking into the safe house uninvited, given the risk of punishment for his having deserted them — and to use their common fund of fifty silver to buy the papers back if necessary rather than resorting to force.
  • Initial plans involved seeking out Stick Stab, investigating Knick Nab's former safe house, and possibly speaking with Mistress Clara.
  • Noddy and Werner both experienced unusual fatigue on their way back to the inn from the court-martial.

docs.title: The Grunge Lane Gambit: Stolen Papers and a Mysterious Map
Events and Actions
docs.text:
Following the public executions at the docks, which ran long into the afternoon, the party gathered at the Crow's Nest as evening fell to plan the recovery of papers stolen from Lieutenant Barrows during his trial. Knick Nab identified the thief as Stick Stab, a knife-specialist from his former gang, run by Nigfa out of a hideout beneath a bakery and chandlery on Grunge Lane. Knick Nab warned the others that Nigfa was an unpredictable, scraggly man with long, filthy yellow fingernails, who carried little more than a stick but kept a few older toughs on hand and was known to punish underlings by cutting off their toes. As they weighed whether to get involved at all, Cosimo argued it strained belief that a pickpocket would pass over a purse for paperwork unless directed to, and reasoned that someone must have hired Nigfa for the job — a theory Noddy waved off as beside the point and Werner worried might expose them to whoever's guards were footing the bill. Undeterred, the party reasoned that clearing Barrows' name — and exposing that his papers had been deliberately targeted — might win them a valuable favor from a naval officer who could help arrange passage out of the city. Cosimo went further, framing their unlikely freedom as the grace of the Father and Mother and the recovery of the papers as a call to adventure the party was bound to answer. With night falling and the gang due to retreat into the hideout to sleep, the party knew they had only a narrow window to catch Stick Stab in the open before any raid grew far more dangerous.

The party formulated a plan: Werner De Rendal and Manuel de Barret (Mani) would enter the bakery, and Infurious Montesigna (Riu) the chandlery, posing as ordinary customers buying bread and candles to provide cover and a distraction. Riu played the part of a sailor freshly ashore, browsing the chandlery's stock of tallow and beeswax candles for his reading, while Werner and Mani lingered over the bakery's leftover morning loaves. Meanwhile, Knick Nab, recognizable to the gang, would lead Cosimo Cellini Scivio, posing as a prospective recruit, in through the bakery's back entrance and down into the hideout itself. Noddy positioned himself across the street to keep watch, directing his bird familiar, Pocket, to orbit overhead and peer into upper-floor windows.

Grunge Lane proved to be an unremarkable block of three shops — a chicken butchery, a stone-built bakery, and a wooden chandlery — separated by narrow, little-used alleys. Beneath the bakery and chandlery lay Nigfa's true hideout: a damp, cave-like basement reachable by a staircase behind either shop, with no other way in or out, and fed by a foul stream the gang's children used as their only water source and latrine alike. A perception sweep on the approach turned up no sign of Stick Stab in the open, so the party moved ahead with the plan as arranged.

Knick Nab and Cosimo descended into the hideout, where they found Stick Stab and two other young pickpockets playing dice around a table. Stick Stab was startled to see his old crewmate — doubly so when Knick Nab let a hidden rapier show beneath his coat. Confronted, Stick Stab admitted Nigfa had already taken the stolen papers upstairs, and revealed that Nigfa had told him beforehand to watch the trial for anyone carrying important-looking papers and steal those instead of a purse if the chance arose — Barrows had simply been the one person there who looked worth targeting. The detail only deepened the party's suspicion that someone had hired Nigfa for the job. One of the other pickpockets bolted upstairs to warn Nigfa; Cosimo's attempt to intimidate the second into staying put failed, and he too fled.

Knick Nab and Cosimo pursued up the back stairs, where they found the door to Nigfa's room in the bakery locked. Cosimo's attempt to pick the lock failed, so Werner — waiting nearby with Mani after their own alarm was raised — set to breaking it down with a chisel and stone-mason's hammer. As the door gave way in pieces, an older teenage gang member came pounding up from the basement to raise the alarm; Werner's shouted order to stop cracked halfway through in his adolescent voice and did nothing to intimidate the boy, but a follow-up kick caught him square in the head, sending him tumbling unconscious down the stairwell. Moments later, another young pickpocket — a boy named Al — burst past them shouting a warning up toward Nigfa's room before Werner finally forced the door open.

Inside, Nigfa — armed with a knife and flanked by two sailor associates — was already trying to escape, having thrown a bed frame across the alley to bridge the gap to an open window of the chandlery's upper floor. Combat erupted as Werner hurled his harpoon across the room, catching Nigfa low in the body and opening a grievous wound while he was still crossing the makeshift bridge. Mani kicked at the bed-frame bridge to collapse the escape route; his first attempt only left it more precarious, but a second knocked it loose. By then one of the two sailors had already tried to leap the gap and was left hanging by his fingertips from the chandlery's window ledge — dropping his knife in the process — until his grip finally gave and he tumbled roughly twelve feet into the alley below, landing on his feet. Nigfa, badly wounded and with nowhere left to run, chose to jump from the window himself rather than keep fighting, and landed in the alley in a bloody heap.

In the alley, Cosimo leapt from the window to press the attack on the fallen Nigfa, though the blow went wide; Mani followed close behind, vaulting out after him with rapier drawn in one hand and his half-eaten baguette still in the other, landing beside the sprawled bodies with a triumphant flourish before searching the unconscious sailor. In the chandlery, the second sailor — unarmed — came down the stairs after them and advanced on Riu, who leveled his pistol at the man's face and warned him off with a flat "not today." Noddy jammed the door shut with his scimitar to buy time, but when the sailor tried to bolt past them and flee, Werner caught him from behind with a sweeping blow that wrenched his arm from its socket and dropped him. The party stripped him of 12 bronze pieces — he carried no weapon — and let him go. Werner then went down into the alley, found Nigfa still clinging to life, and made sure of him, recovering his harpoon in the process.

With the fight over, the party gathered the loot: a small chest of papers from Nigfa's room, a sack of 64 silver coins, a second sack of valuable goblets and chalices, and the dagger the dangling sailor had dropped. Rather than heading straight back, they doubled around through side streets to make sure they weren't followed before returning to their secret cubbyhole beneath the Crow's Nest.

There, by lantern and candlelight, the party laid out what they had taken. Among the papers was a sealed letter from Captain Maynard to Lieutenant Barrows, a stack of assorted naval orders and correspondence — some sealed, some not — and one item that matched none of the rest: a very old, fire-damaged map on skin-like parchment, marked with Elven-style runes and the name "Gildenhome," apparently depicting a door. Riu, drawing on his bookish knowledge of old documents, judged the map to be at least twenty years old, made from some kind of skin or parchment rather than paper, and clearly a fragment of a larger original. None of the party could place the name Gildenhome or make anything further of the runes, despite attempts at history, regional lore, and what little Elvish anyone in the group could muster.

The party weighed the risk of carrying so many naval documents into the Admiralty, reasoning that the stack alone could expose the fleet's movements if it fell into the wrong hands or if they themselves were searched — and wondered aloud whether the theft was less a coincidence than evidence of an established spy operation feeding fleet intelligence to the North's enemies. They agreed to leave the map and the bulk of the recovered papers hidden in the cubbyhole, taking only the sealed letter to deliver, and to hold what they'd found in reserve as potential leverage once Lieutenant Barrows was free to advise them. With Mistress Mary away for the day with the Prince, they went upstairs to consult Mistress Clara instead, framing their questions as concern for a friend of Mary's rather than revealing the full truth. Clara examined the sealed letter and advised them to present it directly to someone in authority at the Admiralty, or, failing that, to Lieutenant Barrows' own guards at the docks, reasoning that Barrows himself would know whom to trust. The session ended with the party setting out for the docks to attempt exactly that, while Werner stayed behind briefly to give the remaining unsealed naval papers a sailor's once-over for anything of obvious value, careful not to break the seal on anything still closed.

docs.title: Events and Actions
docs.text:
The party, possessing Lieutenant Barrows' stolen letter and a cache of other documents — including an ancient map inscribed on a scrap of skin and at least two decades old — first went upstairs at The Crow's Nest hoping to find Mistress Mary, whom they had seen with the Prince at the trial, but she was out; a companion of hers could offer little beyond suggesting they take everything straight to the Admiralty. Weighing that advice, they decided to approach the Admiralty directly to prove Barrows' innocence. Before setting out, they weighed the risk of turning everything over: presenting Naval papers that pointed to a spy ring could easily end in torture or worse. Some voiced real fear of the consequences, but Knick Nab argued they had already been seen and named at the trial and could not simply walk away now, and volunteered to make the approach himself. After leaving their other spoils (money and valuables) in their clubhouse at The Crow's Nest, they changed out of the clothes bloodied in the fight at Nigfa's safe house and took a few minutes to clean themselves up before heading to the Docks, with Werner accompanying Knick Nab to the door and the others hanging back to prepare for a possible rescue.

At the Docks, Noddy first hailed one of the patrolling guards to ask where proof of Barrows' innocence should be brought if found; the guard, unaware of any such arrangement, told him to clear off. Noddy then tried calling directly to the still-dangling Lieutenant Barrows, but Barrows could only manage a strangled noise in reply — enough to show he was alive, but nothing intelligible. Knick Nab and Werner De Rendal then approached the Admiralty building itself, where two guards barred the way. When a suspicious guard demanded proof by asking the Admiral's name, Knick Nab recalled it correctly — Admiral Denys — and claimed he had been personally tasked by the Admiral to find proof of Barrows' innocence. Werner, using the alias "Simon de Say," supported this, claiming to be a client of the noble de Marel family.

After a lengthy wait, an officer, Vice Admiral Codemar, emerged. Knick Nab explained he had retrieved the letter from the pickpocket, Stick Stab. Codemar warned that if this proved to be deceit, their fate would be far worse than Barrows'; he then read the sealed letter and ordered Knick Nab and Werner into custody. They were taken into a waiting room inside the Admiralty building.

Meanwhile, the other party members (Noddy, Cosimo, and Manuel de Barret) watched from outside. Manuel, who had held back a portion of the recovered documents rather than hand everything over, quietly looked them through — orders, ship movements, provisions, postings, letters of introduction, some already opened — confirming they were clearly recent and valuable, and resolved to keep them in reserve in case the moment called for more evidence, though it never did. Out of the mist, an old woman ("Good Mother") came clip-clopping up the street with a horse and cart. Noddy and Cosimo spoke with her; she gave them each a small bag containing twigs and roots, telling them it would help them "find the truth." When Noddy asked about the Medallion symbol, she cryptically replied, "That's what I told you to do."

Inside, Knick Nab and Werner heard a commotion, and soldiers rushed out to rescue Lieutenant Barrows — a messy, brutal business from what those outside could see, as the guards cut the rope, Barrows fell into the water, and they hauled him out and half-carried him back across the courtyard. He was brought into the building looking in bad shape, and groans could be heard from time to time as he was assessed. Later, Vice Admiral Codemar returned and questioned Knick Nab and Werner. Knick Nab explained he had confronted the pickpocket, Stick Stab, at Nigfa's safe house on Grunge Lane, and that Nigfa had specifically ordered his boys to steal documents; pressed on how he knew this, he admitted the pickpockets had been roughed up until they talked. He then presented the additional stolen Naval documents, flabbergasting Codemar, and admitted under questioning that he had been taken from the hills as a small child and had no memory of his true name or family.

Knick Nab and Werner were then moved to a cell in the basement, their possessions (Knick Nab's knives, Werner's lockpicks and wooden spoon) temporarily confiscated. Knick Nab unsuccessfully attempted to telepathically contact Noddy.

The remaining party members outside coordinated. Manuel de Barret kept watch at the Docks. Noddy and Cosimo returned to The Crow's Nest and informed Randolph the Chronicler of the situation. Randolph counseled patience, reasoning that Barrows' rescue meant the guards believed their story, though he warned that Nigfa's death — even in self-defense — could still count against Knick Nab and Werner if it came to light. He confirmed that Mary had left with the Prince that morning and had not returned, and added that even if things went badly, the Admiralty building was not a jail, so their friends would not be held there for long. Cosimo then spoke with Mistress Clara, showing her the bag of twigs and, at her prompting, recounting the whole story of the Old Woman who had given it to him. Clara admitted the tale did not sound like anything from the teachings of the Mother and Father, though she allowed it was not unreasonable to suspect their hand in it. Unable to reach Mary herself, Clara guessed she would be back within a day or two, matching how long her calls from the Prince usually lasted, and promised to pass along their request. Clara identified the contents of the bag as Bitterroot, a rare plant from the islands used by pygmies for pain relief — the notes she consulted described chewing two roots for the effect — and agreed to observe Cosimo if he decided to try it.

Through the night, the party kept watch over the Admiralty building in shifts, with Burlyman's wife supplying food and, for whoever drew the cold outdoor watch, a small flask of spirits to keep warm. Passing back through The Crow's Nest, Noddy noticed A'Wood — the sailor who had guided them through the smuggling tunnels — drinking with a group of unfamiliar sailors, and quietly studied their faces in case he needed to recognize them again.

The next day, Knick Nab and Werner were brought up from the cell to an office to meet with Vice Admiral Codemar again. He told them Lieutenant Barrows was young and strong and recovering well, and had urged that they be treated as friends rather than prisoners or suspects — a request Codemar said he felt bound to honour, given his own sense of debt to Barrows. He pressed them to be entirely forthright, then returned to the confrontation at Grunge Lane: they admitted to the violence, explaining they had been defending themselves, that Nigfa had died falling from a window, and that two other sailors present had fled or been badly hurt, one with a dislocated shoulder. On hearing that the safe house's upper rooms held barrels and crates of goods, Codemar concluded the bakery and chandlery fronting it must have been complicit in some smuggling operation. Satisfied, he confirmed Barrows had vouched for them, expressed gratitude for the returned documents and the information about the spy ring, and said he would need to speak with them again — noting that if he needed to find them, he already knew they were staying at The Crow's Nest. Asked where they were from, Werner claimed they had formerly been clients of "the De Rendal" — a once-great northern family fallen on hard times — without admitting the name was in fact his own. Werner then inquired about a Naval commission, and Codemar advised him to have his father's factor make a formal request.

The party reunited and, at Knick Nab's suggestion, resolved to sit down together for a proper meal rather than scraps, using the time to talk through everything that had happened. Comparing notes, more than one of them found that trying to leave the group's company brought on nausea and fatigue — evidence that the medallions somehow bound their fates together — though none of them recalled feeling anything the night before, when the group was split three-and-three between the cell and the street outside, even allowing that everyone had simply been too exhausted to notice. They connected the nausea to an earlier, cryptic remark from the Old Woman that she could not change everyone's fate, concluding she must be deliberately shaping theirs. Cosimo searched his knowledge of the Divinity of Two for anything resembling her instruction to "seek the truth," but found nothing tying it to established church teaching. Mindful that Randolph recorded everything he was told, the party agreed to keep him in the dark about the medallions and the Old Woman, sharing with him only what they judged safe. Someone also pointed out that the Admiralty's coming visit might not be their only worry: Knick Nab had told Stick Stab where they lived before the fight at Nigfa's, so Nigfa's surviving associates in the underworld could come looking for them as well.

Turning to the map, the party worked out that the long straight line across its center — which they had first taken for a road or canal — was more likely a wall, since it bore a door and a small structure and was flanked by roads on both sides. The cryptic script scattered across it resembled a degraded, corrupted form of Elvish, unreadable even to Infurious Montesigna (Riu), who had a little training in the language. Besides Gildenhome, the map marked several other "homes" — one to the east, one partway down a path, and one at its southern edge — along with an X, a notable clearing, a stretch of coastline complete with what looked like a sea monster, and cardinal direction points, though the party cautioned themselves against assuming the compass arrow followed Northern convention without confirming which end was north. They reasoned the map likely postdated the Great Change, since whoever made it had evidently gone out exploring and returned with what they'd found; Riu also noted that measuring longitude at sea remained difficult in this world, with sailors still navigating largely by landmarks, ice patterns, and dead reckoning, which meant the map's markings were unlikely to be true coordinates. Judging Gildenhome their best lead, the party decided to make a faithful copy of the map — with Riu, whose vocation as a librarian included map-making, taking the lead — before doing anything else with the fragile original. They planned to research Gildenhome and the map's origins through libraries and cartographers, quietly ask around about anyone offering a reward — as much as 50 gold, they guessed — for a stolen map, and consider whether the loot recovered from Nigfa's gang could reveal who the documents were stolen from in the first place, reasoning that whoever stole them had likely been targeting people in naval uniform specifically, since papers passed between officers directly were unlikely to have gone missing by chance. Someone wondered aloud whether any of this connected to the walled-off chamber they had found beneath the Capitol's cathedral, with its manacles and the immured body wearing several concealed medallions of which only one had ever been visible — the two mysteries felt related, though nobody could say how. For now, they set aside the idea of questioning a church of the Two directly, mindful that even hinting at some power behind the Old Woman could be read as blasphemy, though disguising the question as a devout northern boy's idle curiosity about old stories was floated as a safer approach to try later.

Besides Gildenhome, the map also marks several other "homes" to the east, along a path, and at its southern edge, along with an X, a notable clearing, a stretch of coastline with what looks like a sea monster, and cardinal direction points of uncertain orientation. The party guessed the map postdates the Great Change, and Riu noted that reliable longitude is still beyond this world's navigators, who rely on landmarks, ice patterns, and dead reckoning.
  • Randolph confirmed Mistress Mary left with the Prince that morning and had not returned, and noted that the Admiralty building is not a jail, so even a bad outcome would not have kept Knick Nab and Werner there for long.
  • Vice Admiral Codemar suspects the bakery and chandlery fronting Nigfa's hideout were complicit in smuggling, based on the barrels and crates found stored in its upper rooms.
  • The party planned to:
    • Make a copy of the ancient map.
    • Research "Gildenhome" and the map's origins through libraries and cartographers.
    • Quietly ask around about anyone offering a reward — as much as 50 gold, by their guess — for such a map.
    • Consider whether the loot recovered from Nigfa's gang could reveal who the documents were originally stolen from, on the theory that the thieves were likely targeting people in naval uniform specifically.
    • Explore the use of the Bitterroot.
    • Speak to Burlyman about payment for the earlier smuggling job.
    • Hold off on questioning a church of the Two directly about the Old Woman, for now, given that even hinting at some power behind her could be read as blasphemy; disguising the question as a devout northern boy's idle curiosity about old stories was floated as a safer approach to try later.
    • Say as little as possible to Randolph the Chronicler about the medallions and the Old Woman, since he records everything he is told.
  • The Admiralty knows the party is staying at The Crow's Nest.

docs.title: Items Lost
docs.text:
• Knick Nab's large knife and one throwing knife were temporarily confiscated by Admiralty guards (returned upon release).
  • Werner De Rendal's lockpicks and a large wooden spoon were temporarily confiscated by Admiralty guards (returned upon release).

docs.title: Bitter Truths, Pointed Ears, and Golden Goblets
Events and Actions
docs.text:
The party, gathered at the Crow's Nest after securing Lieutenant Barrows' release, debated the nature and purpose of the pouches of sticks (Bitterroot) given to Cosimo and Noddy by an old crone. Riu initially believed they were meant for Lieutenant Barrows to alleviate his pain, and proposed presenting himself and Noddy to the lieutenant directly: claiming a hand in his rescue, offering him the pouch, and asking for a commission as a ship's healer, reasoning that Barrows would need to replace crew he had lost — a boy and five men hanged, with others left behind on the island. The rest of the party judged this premature and preferred to experiment with the Bitterroot themselves first. The party learned from Mistress Clara's research in a book that the roots were likely Bitterroot, a plant used by pygmies for sustenance and its calming and pain-relieving properties. The old crone had cryptically stated the roots would help them "find the truth."

Following Noddy's suggestion, most of the party retired to their basement clubhouse to experiment with the Bitterroot, lighting the braziers and offering a prayer to the Mother and Father for guidance before diving in. Noddy chewed his stick first, sucking on it slowly like licorice, and found his thoughts sharpening and organizing with unusual clarity — he could recall past events, such as the party's first descent into the smugglers' cove, with vivid precision, down to the color of the sky and the pattern of the clouds that day. He offered a taste to his familiar, Pocket, who pecked at it and lost interest. Cosimo, Werner, Knick Nab, and Mani also partook, toasting to clarity and truth as they chewed. Cosimo reported similar effects of clarity and enhanced reasoning. Werner found it helped mitigate pain after he experimentally punched a charred door. Knick Nab felt "pumped" with organized thoughts. Riu abstained.

Under the influence of the Bitterroot, Cosimo and Noddy began to perceive the smuggler A'Wood in his true form: a tall, thin Elf with pointed ears, long flowing golden hair, and fine leather clothing quite unlike a sailor's rough garb. They also saw an unsettling, unhealthy "taint" or "aura" around most other people, including themselves and their companions and even Burlyman and his wife — an unwholesome, sickly impression rather than any visible glow. A'Wood alone appeared the opposite way — unnervingly, deliberately ordinary — a plainness that struck Cosimo and Noddy as strange even before they had chewed the root. Curious about the nature of the taint, Cosimo tried to draw some of it out of A'Wood and into himself, but the attempt came to nothing; drawing on his own arcane knowledge to study it, he sensed no trace of actual magic in the taint, unlike A'Wood's disguise, which plainly was magical. The others did not perceive any of these phenomena.

Outside, Cosimo and Noddy separately whispered their descriptions of A'Wood to Knick Nab and Mani — tall, gaunt, pointed ears, long flowing golden hair — and the two accounts matched exactly, convincing the rest of the party that something uncanny was really going on. Knick Nab impulsively rushed back into the Crow's Nest common room to confront A'Wood, with the rest of the party following. A'Wood, after some convincing by Knick Nab, agreed to a private conversation in the party's curtained-off room; Mani ducked in partway through with a tray of drinks so the huddle of boys around A'Wood wouldn't look out of place to the rest of the tavern. There, A'Wood revealed his Elven nature, explaining he had spent about a week in the Capitol — having come from a castle and then another town before that — using the smuggling run as a convenient way in, and spending his days simply listening to gossip in the tavern. He said he was in disguise to observe the Northern Kingdom's military buildup, watching whether its forces were bound east toward Elven lands, and reported that the buildup looked substantial on both land and sea — heavy naval preparation alongside a large mobilization of cavalry, with rumor in the tavern pointing toward a coming war against the South. He hinted that there were others like him nearby whom he refused to risk exposing — any further help, he said, would have to come from outside the city. Hearing that the roots had come from an old crone, A'Wood reacted with visible unease, explaining that in Elven tradition such crones are tied to fate, luck, and happenstance — as though he suspected something more than chance was behind his exposure.

Riu questioned A'Wood about "Gildenhome," a name he'd encountered. A'Wood recognized it as a fabled city from ancient Elven myth but could not translate the old Elven script Riu presented, noting its archaic and unusual forms. When Cosimo pressed him to explain how he achieved his disguise, A'Wood first demonstrated a bit of mundane sleight-of-hand — palming and vanishing a coin — before conceding that what he truly did was something more, and that Cosimo showed genuine aptitude worth teaching. Intrigued by Cosimo and Noddy's ability to see through his glamour (which they attributed to the Bitterroot), A'Wood offered to teach them how to access their own innate "power" (Mentalism/Illusionism), with lessons to begin the following morning.

The party then discussed their next steps, agreeing to present themselves to the authorities as a group rather than risk their hard-won goodwill by sending only a couple of representatives. They decided to inquire about Lieutenant Barrows at the Admiralty Building. The guard on duty rebuffed them with open contempt, repeatedly dismissing Cosimo as "little boy," but Cosimo talked his way past the guard's dismissal and secured a promise that he'd check inside. After a twenty-minute wait, the guard returned to report that Barrows had already been sent to the infirmary in High Town — a place none of them could simply walk into.

Returning to the Crow's Nest, the party asked Burlyman whether there would be more smuggling work. He explained that increased vigilance at sea meant the next shipment would be delayed, and that resuming runs through the tunnel would require an inside arrangement with guards — building on the party's earlier dealings with Fursa and Evans — a matter he was still working on. He expressed continued interest in employing the party once conditions allowed. The party then had Burlyman appraise the valuable goblets they had acquired; after weighing and evaluating the items, he paid them 12 gold pieces. This wealth was distributed among the party members.

The next morning, A'Wood commenced his instruction with Cosimo and Noddy, remarking that most people were too weak-minded for this kind of training and that their aptitude — young and untrained as they were — genuinely surprised him. Cosimo selected the "Overlay" spell (Open Mentalism - Seemings list), while Noddy chose "Blur" (Open Mentalism). Riu sought out Mistress Clara for healing training; with no wounded patients to treat since her original offer, she instead had him practice on a regular patient's minor complaint and told him the man would be back weekly. Mani practiced his knife-throwing skills, and Werner also engaged in training.

Later, while the party was having lunch, Stick Stab entered the Crow's Nest, made eye contact, and quickly departed. Knick Nab and Mani immediately pursued him outside, onto the road that runs past the tavern toward the cliff edge and the crow-haunted tree that gives the Crow's Nest its name. They found Stick Stab with five other youths — older toughs rather than grown men, but armed with knives, swords, an axe, and a hook, and ready to fight regardless. Stick Stab demanded the return of the papers the party had previously recovered, warning that worse than him was coming for them if he didn't get them back. The ruffians drew their weapons, and Werner, watching from the doorway, held a knife ready to throw the instant anyone moved against Mani. Mani attempted to de-escalate by offering to sell the papers back, but Stick Stab was unyielding. Mani lit a sheet of paper on fire and threw it out the door to pressure him, then burned a second sheet soon after when the bluff didn't land, claiming the party would rather destroy the recovered documents than hand them over. As the situation intensified, three sharp whistles sounded from outside — a signal among Stick Stab's crew — and the ruffians drew pistols alongside their blades. Burlyman's wife slipped out of sight while Burlyman quietly armed himself with a blunderbuss inside the tavern. The session concluded as Stick Stab began to enter the Crow's Nest and Riu moved to close the door, only to find it blocked by one of Stick Stab's accomplices; Riu leveled his pistol at the man's foot and demanded he move it, but the door remained open as the confrontation reignited.

docs.title: NPCs & Creatures
docs.text:
• A'Wood: Revealed to be an Elf in disguise, observing the North's military buildup on behalf of his people in the East — reporting substantial land and naval preparations and tavern rumor of a coming war against the South. Spent about a week in the Capitol — having come from a castle and then another town before that — using the smuggling run as cover and spending his days simply listening to gossip in the tavern. Unsettled to learn the Bitterroot came from an old crone, tying the encounter to Elven notions of fate. Hinted that other Elves were nearby but refused to risk exposing them, saying further aid would have to come from outside the city. Demonstrated some mundane sleight-of-hand before agreeing to teach Cosimo and Noddy, remarking that most people are too weak-minded for such training and that their aptitude genuinely surprised him.
  • Stick Stab: Confronted the party, demanding the return of stolen papers.
  • Ruffians (5 youths): Accomplices of Stick Stab.
  • Burlyman: Proprietor of the Crow's Nest. Fenced the party's goblets for 12 gold. Armed himself during the confrontation with Stick Stab.
  • Mistress Clara: Provided information about Bitterroot. Began training Riu in healing.
  • Pocket: Noddy's familiar spirit, inhabiting a seagull. Offered a taste of the Bitterroot out of curiosity; pecked at it and showed no interest.
  • Randolph the Chronicler: Present in the Crow's Nest, observing and taking notes.
  • Vice Admiral Codemar: Mentioned.
  • Lieutenant Barrows: Mentioned; confirmed to be in the infirmary in High Town.
  • Old Woman: Mentioned as the source of the Bitterroot, given to the party as "an old crone."
  • Pygmies: Mentioned as the original cultivators of Bitterroot.
  • Dr. Wynken: Mentioned as a physician who researched Bitterroot.
  • Fursa and Evans: The dock guards from the party's earlier smuggling run, mentioned again by Burlyman as the inside contacts he needs to arrange before resuming shipments.

docs.title: Locations
docs.text:
• The Crow's Nest: The primary location, including the common room, the party's private curtained room, and their basement clubhouse. Outside, the road running past the tavern leads to a high cliff edge and a tree favored by a murder of crows — the tavern's namesake.
  • The Admiralty Building: The party visited the exterior to inquire about Lieutenant Barrows.
  • High Town: Mentioned as the location of the infirmary where Lieutenant Barrows is.
  • The East: Mentioned by A'Wood as the location of Elven lands.
  • Gildenhome: Mentioned by A'Wood as a fabled ancient Elven city/myth.
  • Bitterroot Isle: Mentioned as the origin of the Bitterroot plant.

docs.title: Conflicts
docs.text:
• A brief, quickly resolved disagreement between Riu and Cosimo/Noddy regarding the Bitterroot pouches.
  • A tense, non-violent confrontation with A'Wood, leading to the revelation of his Elven identity and his mission.
  • A major confrontation with Stick Stab and his five ruffian associates outside the Crow's Nest. This escalated to drawn weapons (knives, swords, an axe, a hook, pistols) and threats of death from Stick Stab if the papers were not returned. The conflict was ongoing at the session's end.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• Bitterroot Effects: Chewing Bitterroot can induce heightened focus, mental clarity, and provide some pain relief. For Cosimo and Noddy, it uniquely allowed them to perceive A'Wood's true Elven form and a strange "taint" or unhealthy aura around most other individuals.
  • A'Wood's Identity and Mission: A'Wood is an Elf from the East, using a magical disguise (glamour) to spy on the Northern Kingdom's military buildup, ensuring it poses no threat to Elven territories. He indicated there are others of his kind operating nearby but refused to risk exposing them, saying any further help would have to come from outside the city.
  • The Northern Kingdom's Military Buildup: A'Wood reported that the North's preparations are substantial on both land and sea — a large naval mobilization alongside a significant buildup of cavalry — with tavern rumor pointing toward a coming war against the South.
  • Elven Relations: Elves are generally isolationist and wary of the North due to negative historical interactions.
  • Elven Views on Crones: A'Wood reacted with unease on learning the Bitterroot was a gift from an old crone, explaining that in Elven tradition, crones are associated with fate, luck, and happenstance.
  • Elven Magic/Abilities: A'Wood offered to teach Cosimo and Noddy how to access their own innate powers, suggesting a connection to Mentalism or Illusionism.
  • The Old Women and the Amulets: Turning over their unsolved mysteries, the party speculated again about the old women who periodically appear to them and the medallions that let them see one another, debating whether the crones are tied to the Mother and Father, why the number of old women encountered has varied between one and three — Werner recalled encountering more than one crone in a wagon while stowing away to escape the upper city — and whether the party might have been drawn from different points in time into the same moment. No firm conclusions were reached.
  • Abominations and the Two: Confronted with a possible non-human in their midst, the party briefly weighed whether A'Wood's Elven nature made him a target under the Two's teachings against the unblessed, but agreed that being an Elf was not the same as being born of an unblessed union.
  • Gildenhome: The name refers to a legendary city from ancient Elven lore. The script Riu found related to it is archaic Elven, difficult for A'Wood to translate.
  • Lieutenant Barrows' Status: He has been moved from the Admiralty Building to an infirmary in High Town.
  • Fencing Goods: Burlyman is a viable contact for selling (fencing) valuable items.
  • Future Smuggling Work: Burlyman indicated the next shipment is delayed due to heightened vigilance at sea, and that resuming the tunnel operation will require an inside arrangement with the dock guards, Fursa and Evans. He remains interested in employing the party once this is settled.
  • Stick Stab's Threat: Stick Stab is determined to retrieve the papers the party recovered and is backed by a gang and apparently more powerful, unseen figures.
  • Character Advancement: With the session's action concluded, the party discussed finishing the transition from their adolescent-era characters to full first-level characters, but ran out of time to complete it and agreed to handle it as bookkeeping before the next session.

    • Cosimo Cellini Scivio and Noddy began training with A'Wood to develop their mental/illusionary abilities.

• Bitterroot Sticks (5): One stick each consumed by Noddy, Cosimo Cellini Scivio, Werner De Rendal, Knick Nab, and Manuel de Barret during their experimental tasting.

docs.title: A Captain's Offer and a Captive's Secret
Events and Actions
docs.text:
(Note: The video and transcript for the session immediately preceding this one, which detailed the initial confrontation with Stick Stab and his gang, have unfortunately been lost. This summary begins with the events following that confrontation, filled out where possible by a recap the party gave partway through this session for a player who had missed the fight.)

The session began with the player characters comparing the level 1 abilities they had just gained. Cosimo demonstrated his growing command of illusion — stationary images and sounds solid enough to hide the party behind a false wall or disguise a stretch of terrain — along with a new knack for sensing illusions others couldn't and a minor ranged strike of his own to fall back on in a pinch. Riu described his lay healer training: stopping bleeding, mending broken bones, easing fatigue, diagnosing what ailed a patient, and the beginnings of study into prosthetics. Riu also mentioned investing further in his family's trade, taking skill with hoofed mammals as a nod to the Mona family's long history of horse breeding on the Plains.

Recapping the fight for their returning companion, the party reconstructed some of what had happened before the transcript was lost. Brief argument over whether Stick Stab should live or die collapsed almost immediately into fighting. The party barred the tavern door with a boarding harpoon while Stick Stab's companions tried to force their way in from outside. Knick Nab's opening blow swept Stick Stab's legs out from under him, leaving him stunned enough to surrender on the spot. The gang outside then opened fire through the window, forcing the party to board it up; the only casualty was a graze from flying glass. Listening past the barred door, the party made out that a separate group had arrived down the street and opened fire on the attackers in three volleys. In the confusion, Knick Nab slipped outside and recovered two pistols from the fallen before Stick Stab was dragged down into the cellar.

The main part of the session picked up in the aftermath of that confrontation. Stick Stab was taken down into the cellar, where Noddy shoved him against the wall and drove a blow into his kidneys before he and Mani searched him thoroughly: boots, socks, pockets, coat, and shirt all turned out, yielding two proper fighting knives and a coin purse, but no papers or anything else that might identify who he answered to. It was Mani who found something more — an invisible weight resting against Stick Stab's throat — and worked it free: a second Medallion, just as unyielding to remove as their own had been. Stick Stab seemed relieved to be rid of it, calling it nothing but pain and thanking Mani for taking it off him. Under further questioning, dagger drawn, a battered Stick Stab admitted he had found the Medallion weeks earlier while sneaking into the cellar looking for food — the same cellar where the party had found their own. Noddy then tried a bluff, claiming to know of another kid who'd once had a similar invisible necklace, and pressed Stick Stab on whether that kid had long red hair; Stick Stab took the bait, confirming the kid had red hair, though he couldn't say for certain whether it was long — it may have been tucked under a cap or wrap. Before handing him over to Captain Barrows, Knick Nab pulled Stick Stab aside for one last try at getting a name, but Stick Stab would say only that they were all dead regardless of what happened to him, and he never gave one up.

Soon after, Lieutenant Barrows arrived with a contingent of Marines — leaning on a cane, visibly favouring an injury, but composed and properly turned out. Knick Nab greeted him warmly, the two having history from an earlier rescue, and Werner was recognised alongside him. Stick Stab was brought up from the cellar and presented to Barrows for formal questioning. Mani, seemingly eager to impress the officer, kept up the rough treatment — striking Stick Stab hard enough to leave him stunned — until the boy broke down sobbing without giving up anything further; Mani then softened, fetching water and a rag and offering a gentler hand once the harder approach had run its course.

Barrows explained he had come looking for Knick Nab and Werner personally, and asked the party to recount what had happened. Knick Nab laid it out for him: they had traced the stolen documents to a cavern beneath a bakery and chandlery in Grunge Lane — the former hideout of the very gang Knick Nab himself had once run with before leaving it behind, which was how he'd known where to look. Alongside Barrows's papers, they had also turned up an unrelated parcel of documents, apparently by chance. Knick Nab admitted he had once told Stick Stab he'd be welcome at the Crow's Nest if he ever wanted out of the gang — an offer that, in hindsight, had only pointed Stick Stab and his armed companions toward where the party was staying. As Stick Stab was led away, Knick Nab pulled Barrows aside for one last urgent word: whoever had sent the boy might well be watching them even now. Barrows ordered Stick Stab and the recovered papers taken to Vice Admiral Codemar for further questioning, and thanked the party for their trouble. Stepping outside afterward, they found four of the attackers' bodies laid out where the Marines had collected them, a fifth having apparently fallen from the cliff while fleeing; a separate contingent of city guards could be seen approaching from down the street to help secure the scene.

He then turned to the party itself, asking what skills they could bring to bear. Werner stepped forward first, formally introducing himself and explaining his family's seafaring history and his hope of securing a Navy commission, his letters of introduction having been lost along the way. Cosimo followed, describing himself as a rigger and rope operator, well used to cranes and cargo work. When Barrows asked whether the party wished to join the Navy, Knick Nab pushed back — he wanted the personal satisfaction of hunting down whoever was really behind Stick Stab, not simply escaping the city. Barrows argued that the party wasn't yet equipped for that fight, and that leaving for a time — training, gaining experience, letting their trail go cold — would put them in a far better position to return and finish it later; he promised that if the mastermind were ever caught, the party would be informed and invited to witness the trial or execution. Mani spoke next, describing his family of sailors and merchants, his knowledge of keeping a ship quiet on a smuggling run (down to wrapping oars in cloth so they wouldn't splash), and his ongoing study of swordsmanship. At that, Randolph the Chronicler, who had been quietly taking notes throughout, stepped forward to vouch for the real martial skill beginning to show in him.

Captain Barrows then drew Randolph aside for a private word. Riu strained to catch what was said but made out only talk of dates and times, with Randolph repeatedly emphasising "one week" — a span that seemed to line up with how long the party had actually been in the Capitol. Returning to the group, Barrows asked after the two he hadn't yet heard from: Noddy offered little beyond knowing which way was north and admitting he could dance a little and cook a bit, while Riu introduced himself as a scholar who had lately picked up medicine, healing, and woodworking — including a claim he could build exoskeletons — and named his family, the Monas, the horse-breeding Plains nobility Barrows recognised at once for their loyalty to the Crown.

Satisfied, Barrows made his offer: passage out of the city and positions aboard his new command, the "Advance," for anyone willing to join the King's Navy. He admitted plainly that he currently had no crew of any kind, having lost his previous one to a mutiny, and that he felt he could trust this group after what he'd seen of them. He singled out Knick Nab for something more — a personal position as his steward — in gratitude for once having saved his life. Mani answered first, saying he was interested but would need to check with his current master — an unmistakable nod to Randolph, standing right there — before giving a firm answer. Knick Nab answered carefully in turn, saying he'd need time to settle a few small obligations in the city first, including with Burlyman, who had given the party room and board in exchange for labour; Barrows could spare him no more than until the tide turned the following evening. Knick Nab also asked about bringing personal possessions — permitted, and he was promised a footlocker — while Werner pressed about formalising his commission despite his lost papers; Barrows agreed to make inquiries on his behalf. As he took his leave, Barrows warned the party plainly that neither the tavern nor the city was safe for them any longer — whoever wanted them dead clearly knew where to find them.

With the Marines gone, the party turned to practicalities. They agreed it was worth telling Burlyman about the Navy's offer, and discussed slipping out of the city the next day through the smugglers' tunnels rather than risking the streets, reasoning that leaving a presence behind at the tavern would keep any watchers looking in the wrong place. Cosimo, familiar with the tunnels from his construction work, favoured that route and offered his skill at disguise if it came to that. Knick Nab was tempted to spend one last night out in the city but was talked out of it given the danger. They also sent Noddy's familiar, the seagull Pocket, to fly down and check on the gang member who had fallen from the cliff during the fight; Pocket found the body wedged halfway down the rock face but couldn't confirm whether a pistol — worth some two gold — had gone down with him. Searching Stick Stab's purse turned up eight silver, split among the party with two shares set aside for the group's shared fund, now standing at forty-four. With a little time and money left before the deadline, they discussed shopping for gear — weighing whether to venture into the city themselves or have goods brought to them at double the price. Knick Nab asked for a custom leather coat doubling as light armour, meant to be worn only when trouble threatened rather than as everyday wear, with concealed pockets sized for tools like throwing knives.

docs.title: NPCs & Creatures
docs.text:
• Stick Stab: Captured and interrogated. Roughly the same age as the party and more street urchin than mastermind despite his authority over the gang, he wore a second Medallion — found weeks earlier while scavenging for food in the same cellar the party knew, and one he seemed relieved to have taken from him, calling it nothing but pain. He confirmed the "red-haired kid" had red hair, though its length was uncertain. Broke down under pressure but never named his handler, and no papers or other identifying items were found on him. Taken into custody by Marines to be seen by the Vice Admiral.
  • Captain Barrows: Formerly Lieutenant Barrows, now visibly injured but composed. Arrived with Marines, took charge of Stick Stab, and offered the party positions on his ship, the "Advance" — admitting he currently has no crew at all, having lost his last one to a mutiny. Made a personal offer of stewardship to Knick Nab in gratitude for a past rescue, and agreed to look into Werner's Navy commission.
  • Marines: Accompanied Captain Barrows, secured the area around the Crow's Nest, and took Stick Stab into custody.
  • City Guards: A separate contingent seen approaching down the street as the scene wound down, distinct from Barrows's Marines.
  • Randolph the Chronicler: Present in The Crow's Nest, quietly taking notes throughout. Vouched for Mani's emerging martial skills to Captain Barrows and had a private conversation with him about "one week," partially overheard by Riu.
  • "Red-haired kid with long hair": Mentioned by Stick Stab as someone who might also have a Medallion. Confirmed to have red hair; whether it is truly "long" is unconfirmed, since Stick Stab only ever saw it possibly tucked under a cap or wrap.
  • Burlyman: The Crow's Nest's proprietor, who has given the party room and board in exchange for labour. The party resolved to tell him about the Navy's offer before deciding.
  • Pocket: Noddy's familiar spirit, inhabiting a seagull. Sent to fly down the cliff face and check on the gang member who fell during the earlier fight.
  • Vice Admiral Codemar: Mentioned as the person Stick Stab would be taken to. (The party heard his name during the trial.)

docs.title: Locations
docs.text:
• The Crow's Nest: The primary location for the session's events, including the interrogation of Stick Stab and the meeting with Captain Barrows.
  • The cellars beneath the Crow's Nest: Where both the party's own Medallions and Stick Stab's were found.
  • Grunge Lane: The cavern beneath a bakery and chandlery, the former hideout of the gang Knick Nab once belonged to and where the party first recovered Barrows's stolen documents.
  • The "Advance" (ship): Captain Barrows' new command. The PCs were invited to join its crew and report there before the tide turns.
  • The Capitol: The city where all events took place, including its network of smugglers' tunnels the party considered using to leave unseen.

docs.title: Conflicts
docs.text:
• Knick Nab's attempt to talk Stick Stab into naming his handler failed, forcing the party into intimidation instead.
  • Stick Stab was roughed up during the cellar search — Noddy shoved him against the wall and struck his kidneys before the search began — and again in front of Captain Barrows, mostly at Mani's hand, until he broke down sobbing without ever giving up a name.
  • The aftermath of the previous session's fight was evident, with Stick Stab's gang members confirmed deceased outside The Crow's Nest (four bodies seen, one reportedly fell off the cliff).
  • Recapping the fight, the party recalled that a separate group had opened fire on Stick Stab's gang from down the street in three volleys before Captain Barrows and the Marines ever reached the door — presumably connected, though the party never confirmed whether it was the same force.
  • Captain Barrows warned the party as he left that the tavern, and the city more broadly, was no longer safe for them.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• PCs shared details of their new level 1 abilities: Cosimo's illusions, Riu's healing (and a new interest in hoofed mammals, echoing his family's horse-breeding background).
  • Another Medallion was discovered, worn by Stick Stab. He claimed to have found it weeks earlier while scavenging for food in the same cellar the party found theirs, and seemed relieved to have it removed, calling it nothing but pain to wear.
  • Aside from two knives and a coin purse, no papers or documents were found on Stick Stab that might identify who he answered to.
  • Stick Stab confirmed the "red-haired kid with long hair" has red hair, though its length couldn't be confirmed.
  • Knick Nab revealed to Captain Barrows that he had once belonged to the same gang that operated out of the Grunge Lane cavern, and that his own past offer to Stick Stab of a way out had inadvertently led the gang to the Crow's Nest.
  • Captain Barrows was promoted and given command of the ship "Advance," which he currently has no crew for after losing his previous crew to a mutiny.
  • Captain Barrows offered the party a way to leave the city by joining the Navy, citing the danger they were in and his own need for crew.
  • Captain Barrows made a separate, personal offer to Knick Nab: a position as his steward.
  • Mani said he was interested in the Navy offer but wanted to check first with his current master — Randolph, standing right there — before committing.
  • Captain Barrows promised that if Stick Stab's handler is ever captured, the party will be informed and invited to witness the trial or execution.
  • The party discussed the pros and cons of accepting Barrows' offer; Knick Nab wanted to stay and hunt down the people responsible rather than leave.
  • The deadline to join is before the tide turns on the next day.
  • Randolph the Chronicler vouched for Mani to Captain Barrows.
  • Riu overheard parts of a private conversation between Captain Barrows and Randolph the Chronicler, where the phrase "one week" was repeatedly mentioned by the Chronicler, seemingly tied to how long the party has been in the Capitol.
  • Werner asked about formalising a Navy commission despite having lost his papers; Barrows agreed to make inquiries.
  • The party discussed leaving the city the next day via the smugglers' tunnels rather than the streets, with Cosimo offering his familiarity with the tunnels and his skill at disguise.
  • The party discussed purchasing equipment before leaving, including whether goods could be brought to them at the tavern (at double the price) rather than risking a trip into the city; Knick Nab requested a custom leather coat doubling as light armour, for wear only when trouble threatened, with concealed pockets for tools.
