docs.title: Volunteers for the King's Navy and a Fiery Night at the Docks
Events and Actions
docs.text:
The session began with the party, now Level 1, discussing their next steps after Captain Barrows' offer to join the crew of the "Advance." They debated the fate of Stick Stab, with Riu advocating for his redemption and proposing that his taken Medallion be returned to him, believing Fate had chosen Stick Stab as it had chosen them; Riu voiced concern that removing the Medallion in the first place might have interrupted Fate's design. Cosimo, while no less wary, pointed out that Stick Stab had only done what his boss ordered him to do in hunting the party down — a choice several of them might once have made themselves in his position. Others remained wary of trusting Stick Stab — Knick Nab pointedly noted that one of Stick Stab's own associates had shot him — though the party agreed that if he could not be reached, the Medallion might instead be given to Randolph the Chronicler or one of the Crow's Nest's mistresses. Mindful of Stick Stab's earlier warning that his associates would come for them regardless of his own fate, the party resolved to stay together and keep watch through the night rather than split up. Knick Nab investigated a mention of a "red-headed" associate of Stick Stab but found no leads within his former gang.

The party then turned to preparations before joining the ship, taking stock of the 44 silver and 3 gold they held in common. They were advised that a warship offered little privacy and no shortage of gambling among the crew, and that valuables were best left behind — a caution that shaped their decision to keep only essentials aboard. Mani arranged to buy spices from Burlyman as a gift for the ship's cook, hoping to win favor with the crew; Burlyman warned him that such gifts tend to end up with the officers rather than the cook, and suggested routing the gift through the captain instead. Riu planned to buy a surgeon's kit and a herb reference book. Werner De Rendal decided to procure a Midshipman's uniform and a bottle of alcohol for the Quartermaster. Cosimo planned to purchase a mandolin, while Knick Nab planned to replace the fiddle that had been stolen from him since arriving in the city. The party decided Mani would carry the original Gildenhome map, sewn into the lining of his notebook and protected within an oilskin bag, while Cosimo worked a brick loose in the mortar of the Crow's Nest common room wall to hide the paper copy of the map behind it.

That evening, the party said their farewells. Mani visited Randolph the Chronicler, who gifted him a fine dagger (a main gauche) and delivered an almost valedictory farewell, warning that Mani might not find him still posted in the Capitol even a year hence and telling him to ask after his whereabouts at the Academy if he wished to find him again. Overjoyed, Mani immediately took the blade to a corner of the room to practice his fencing, too elated to sit still. Mani had discussed arranging flowers for Mistress Clara through Burlyman, but that errand went undone; instead, he personally delivered her a sealed, wax-stamped poem asking her permission to write to her of his adventures and dedicate his future glories to her, which she granted. The poem, left for her to read afterward, read: "Clarity in dawn, leave a youth, return a man, to earn love's first kiss." Riu received a gift of herbs from Mistress Clara during the same visit.

Back at The Crow's Nest, Mani's singing captivated the common room — quieting a nearby brewing fistfight and revealing an unexpected talent — while Knick Nab slipped out unnoticed to confront a remnant of his old gang. Finding the hideout's ground-floor windows barred and shuttered and failing to pick the lock on its back door, he climbed a tree behind the neighboring butcher's yard to reach an open second-floor window — the same one through which the party had first broken in to find Nigfa — and let himself in that way. The room beyond had clearly been searched, its crates broken open and contents strewn about, evidently since the party had reported the hideout's location to the Admiralty. Descending to the basement, he found a young, frightened boy from his former gang sleeping alone; the boy startled awake and rolled off his sleeping plank in terror. Knick Nab gave his own name and warned the boy to tell his bosses that they would pay when he returned, then let him go unharmed. The excursion left Knick Nab unusually tired by the time he slipped back into the inn undetected.

The next morning, Cosimo led the party in a morning prayer, building his sermon to a flourish — weighing the trials of yesterday against the glories still to come — before breaking into tongues and manifesting an illusion of light, falling stars, and choral music. The vision astounded his companions and confirmed for Mani that their path was divinely guided; Burlyman blearily wandered out mid-vision, mistook it for the lingering effects of drink, and went back to bed without ever registering what he had nearly witnessed. Mani rushed outside afterward half-expecting to find the mysterious old woman who had once guided the party to the Crow's Nest, but the street was empty.

The party then proceeded to the docks to report to the "Advance," interacting with an officer manning a table set up dockside. Riu dictated a written note to Captain Barrows arguing that Stick Stab could be convinced to cooperate fully with the Navy, and requesting permission to see him and offer him a place aboard in exchange for his cooperation rather than a death sentence. Bosun Burton carried the note to Second Lieutenant Conrad to relay to the captain; after roughly an hour's wait, word came back that Captain Barrows had no authority over Stick Stab and that he could not be seen — a sign he was being held elsewhere, presumably the Admiralty. The party agreed that pursuing the matter further would mean petitioning the Admiralty directly, but decided their remaining time was better spent finishing preparations, and let the matter rest for now. Werner De Rendal confirmed his Midshipman status with the officer at the table, who remarked that he looked old for the rank; Werner explained he had spent his life aboard a whaling ship before earning his commission.

The party then went shopping. Werner acquired his uniform from a tailor named Abercrombie & Fitch, haggling the price down from twelve silver to ten. Riu bought his surgeon's kit, and Cosimo and Knick Nab their instruments. Because Knick Nab and Cosimo were both wanted men, they judged it too risky to enter High Town themselves, so Riu went alone to purchase his herb reference book — an excursion that left him unusually tired by the time he returned to the group. Before boarding, one of the party lingered near the High Town gate hoping the mysterious old woman might appear to see them off, recalling how she had once appeared unbidden outside the Admiralty, but she did not show.

Upon returning to the "Advance," each member was formally assigned their roles. Mani was assigned to the Marines under Master of Arms Bors, presenting himself as a swordsman trained by several masters of arms and boasting he could hit a target at a hundred metres with a musket — a claim he quietly walked back once pressed for specifics; Bors ordered that he be issued a proper sword, an order not yet fulfilled by the session's end. Riu was assigned as Surgeon's Mate to Dr. Forester and immediately put to work measuring bulk medicinal herbs into jars; he asked whether there had been any injuries aboard he might treat to prove himself, but found the ship's first day mercifully quiet — little worse than a hangnail and a bleeding nose. He later secured Dr. Forester's permission to keep his pet squid, Squidly III, in the infirmary. Werner De Rendal was assigned as Midshipman under Second Lieutenant Conrad, who tested him by having him diagnose a broken hasp on the ship's compass housing — which Werner correctly identified — before ordering him to marshal a group of idle sailors led by senior hand Hal into coiling loose rigging; on his own initiative, Werner also worked out the state of the tide to gauge the urgency of the task. Cosimo, reporting aboard, was recognized by the boarding officer from a wanted notice bearing a reward for his capture, but was processed and sent on regardless; he was assigned to assist Quartermaster Mr. Crispin with rigging and cargo, and shortly afterward leapt into action when a rope gave way and a loaded cargo platform swung out over the water — he clambered across the suspended rigging, reached the platform, directed its retrieval by crane, and re-secured the load, impressing the watching crew. Knick Nab was assigned as Captain Barrows' Cabin Boy; Barrows personally recognized him, thanked him for speaking up on his behalf at the court-martial, and called him brave before handing him off to Third Lieutenant Gunter, who toured him around the ship's officers — Sailing Master Styles, Quartermaster Crispin, First Lieutenant Clugny, Second Lieutenant Conrad, Dr. Forester, and Master of Arms Bors. Returning to the captain's cabin afterward, Knick Nab was sent off again, this time to the galley, to tell the ship's stewards that the captain would take dinner at five. That evening, Werner personally delivered his purchased bottle of alcohol to Quartermaster Crispin, formally introducing himself in the process and earning a word of approval for the gesture.

Knick Nab later sought out First Lieutenant Clugny to ask why the ship had not left on the tide as planned; Clugny explained that the ship was several hundredweight short of its expected gunpowder and that departure was now expected first thing the next morning.

As night fell, while Werner De Rendal and Noddy were on watch, two separate attempts were made to bomb the "Advance" and a nearby warship using rowboats laden with explosives — a professionally-made device rigging a barrel of gunpowder to a water-clock timer and a flintlock mechanism poised over a tray of loose powder. Noddy first spotted the rowboat drifting toward the ship out of the darkness; Werner called the alert to the officer of the watch and challenged the boat's occupant, who slipped overboard and swam off before the boat drifted alongside. Werner swam out, stripping off his jacket, hat, and sword first, boarded the rowboat, and tried to snatch the pistol free of the rigged mechanism, but found it fixed in place; failing to make sense of the device otherwise, he simply tipped the boat after a tense pause, dumping it into the harbor before pushing the sealed powder barrel ashore as evidence. A boat crew of Marines and sailors put out with oars to search for the saboteur, but he was never caught. Werner and Mani then rushed to the second rowboat as it approached the other warship; after several failed attempts to tip it, they succeeded on a last try that Mani credited to divine favor, capsizing the device and claiming the recovered boat as Werner's prize. The session concluded with the threat unresolved — no one could yet say whether further devices lay hidden elsewhere along the docks — with alarms ringing and the crews of both ships on high alert.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• The party is now officially Level 1.
  • Cosimo's successful and dramatic illusion spellcasting demonstrated his magical abilities to the group, and confirmed for Mani that their path is divinely guided — his zeal has only grown since, and he now looks for omens in small coincidences.
  • Because both Knick Nab and Cosimo are wanted men in the Capitol, they judged it too dangerous to enter High Town themselves, a reminder of how exposed they remain even as they prepare to leave the city.
  • The party members were assigned various roles and duties aboard the "Advance," beginning their integration into naval life, and learned the names and roles of several key officers in the process.
  • The "Advance" carries a complement of roughly two dozen Marines and about six midshipmen, all more experienced than Werner despite his age — a reminder that the party, now naval personnel, remain thoroughly green.
  • The ship's posted regulations forbid gambling and unauthorized drinking among the crew, with mutiny punishable by death, underscoring the strictness of naval discipline.
  • The ship's departure was delayed from evening to the next morning due to a shortage of gunpowder.
  • Both Knick Nab and Riu experienced unusual fatigue after their respective solo excursions — into the old hideout and High Town — possibly related to their Medallions.
  • The infirmary keeps a running count of days since the ship's last injury; it stood at zero after a day of minor mishaps amid all the loading and provisioning.
  • Life on a naval vessel is hierarchical, with strict protocols and constant activity.
  • The "Advance" is being heavily provisioned with supplies, including gunpowder and livestock, indicating preparations for a significant voyage or military action.
  • The party chose to hide the paper copy of the Gildenhome map behind a loosened brick at the Crow's Nest, keeping only the original — sewn into Mani's notebook — with them aboard ship.
  • Mani speculated, without confirmation, that the dockside saboteurs might be working for the South.

docs.title: Bombs in the Night, a Stowaway, and a Secret Mission
Events and Actions
docs.text:
The evening after the party boarded the "Advance," while still docked in The Capitol, the planned departure was delayed — provisioning a newly-assembled crew for the ship's first cruise under this complement proved a multi-day job. Later that night, an alarm was raised. Noddy, on watch in the crow's nest, and Werner De Rendal on deck, spotted a small rowboat approaching the "Advance" with what turned out to be a barrel of gunpowder and a trigger mechanism. Werner swam out and capsized the boat, neutralizing the threat. Shortly thereafter, Mani spotted a second, similar boat heading towards another nearby ship. Werner rowed the recovered first boat over while Mani swam to intercept; Mani, using a Coin of Fate, helped capsize this second bomb-boat — righting and bailing out the recovered boats afterward proved its own struggle for the two of them.

During the ensuing alarm and commotion, Knick Nab, attempting to climb up into the rigging to see what was happening, lost his footing and fell into the harbor water but was quickly rescued by Cosimo Cellini Scivio and other sailors who threw him a rope. Werner De Rendal and Mani reported the bombing attempts to Lieutenant Gunter, and subsequently to Captain Barrows, describing the mechanism they'd found behind the barrel in the first boat: a pan slowly filling with water that would eventually tip a fixed pistol lock into the powder, evidently assembled with care rather than haste. Werner, invoking naval tradition, formally described the two rowboats as prize captures, a claim the Captain indulged with some amusement. Following these events, the Captain ordered the "Advance" to make ready to sail immediately. Midshipmen were dispatched from the ship with messages.

Getting underway from the dock took real effort: with no room to raise sail so close to shore, sailors poled the ship clear with long oars, then rowed her out using oars run through the gunports normally used for the cannon, since the "Advance" has no dedicated oar deck. Only once clear of the harbor did the crew release the main, top, and top-gallant sails and bring the oars back in, catching the wind and picking up speed. The "Advance" set sail, heading in a general west-southwest direction. Once underway, the new crew members received their initial assignments: Riu was assigned to assist the ship's surgeon as one of several mates, not yet the senior one; Knick Nab became the Captain's steward; Cosimo, with his knowledge of ropes, was put to work with the sail maker and organizing rope stores; Mani joined the Marines, initially tasked with cleaning weapons; and Noddy was sent aloft to learn about the rigging and sails. Werner, already a midshipman with a small crew of sailors under him, was set to work adjusting rigging alongside them — despite having sailed before on his family's own ships, he had never held any official authority aboard one until now.

As the "Advance" departed the docks, Knick Nab was sent to fetch the Captain's morning meal and, later, his looking glass; offered a look through it himself, he swept it from the horizon back over the retreating coastline and was the first to spot two priests and a red-haired youth watching from the dock — but chose to say nothing of it to the officers. Noddy, separately, sent his seagull Pocket flying at speed toward the dock for a closer look, and confirmed the same sight: the youth pointing directly at their ship, and the two priests visibly armed, one with a sword and the other with what looked like a broken flail or mace. Noddy reported the sighting to a midshipman, who brushed it off as unimportant. Later, the party members discussed this, with Riu and Cosimo sharing their knowledge about different types of priests, including the militant "Censures," and agreed to keep watching for the red-haired youth in the future.

After the ship was well at sea, all hands were summoned to the quarterdeck, where Lieutenant Gunter read aloud all thirty-seven articles of the "Rules and Regulations of the King's Navy," covering blasphemy, drunkenness, the limits of flogging, theft of ship's stores or powder, mutiny, and murder. Afterward, Knick Nab was handed a printed copy and ordered to post it by the main hatchway below decks. In the days that followed, word spread among the crew that Werner and Mani were behind the foiling of the bomb boats, earning them a measure of quiet respect.

During a shared off-watch discussion about their unusual abilities, Cosimo shaped a length of rope into a hook to raise and lower Pocket — a demonstration noticed by a passing sailor, who marveled aloud at "that strong seagull" before walking off, underscoring the risk of being seen. The party agreed it would be prudent to keep their abilities relatively secret for the time being, perhaps revealing them at a more critical juncture to greater effect, while always attributing such powers to the blessings of The Two.

Off duty, Mani began training in earnest — pestering the Marines for boarding-action instruction, only to learn their discipline was built for musket volleys rather than individual swordplay, before seeking out older sailors skilled in rough, improvised fighting and sparring with them, all while startling onlookers by invoking dueling terms, such as a "Bonati's defense," that nobody else aboard recognized. Knick Nab, meanwhile, had been quietly developing his own scrappy, self-taught fighting style in his off hours, sparring with whatever came to hand — belaying pins, sacks, and the like — which caught Mani's attention and interest as another source to learn from.

About a week into the voyage, Noddy was in the hold when he noticed a flash of light. Casting Blur to move unseen, he investigated cautiously and discovered a marine guard grievously wounded in front of the ship's magazine, with an unknown assailant armed with a knife standing over him. Noddy flooded the corridor with a burst of Projected Light — blinding to himself as much as the attacker — and immediately raised the alarm, shouting for help as he drew his cutlass and closed to engage, clouding the assailant's mind with a spell of Confusion while holding him off. Cosimo Cellini Scivio, Mani, and Knick Nab were among the first to respond. In the confrontation that followed in the tight, dark corridors, Cosimo cried out "Father, strike my foe, protect my friend!" and cast a spell ("Strike One") that incapacitated the assailant — an invisible blow that, to everyone watching, looked exactly like an answered prayer rather than the working of any hand. The man refused to surrender and had to be beaten into submission before the others could bind him. Riu arrived that night and, through what seemed a miraculous and unseen intervention, staunched the grievously wounded marine's bleeding — by morning the marine had made a full recovery that struck everyone who heard of it as nothing short of a miracle.

The captured assailant was found to be an unrecognized man who had apparently been hiding in a crate within the hold for a week or more, having built it so it could be opened from the inside, with a small barrel of water stored alongside him. He carried a cutlass, a dagger stained with the marine's blood, a set of lock picks, and a small supply of dense, unfamiliar food, and bore three anchor-shaped tattoos in various places on his body. Wary after their own experience with hidden Medallions, the party checked him for a hidden or invisible necklace and found none, and Cosimo cast Detect Illusion over him to rule out any disguise — he proved to be exactly what he appeared. Mani, who had spent days cleaning the ship's weapons, examined the cutlass and dagger but couldn't say for certain whether they were the "Advance's" own naval-issue arms or something the stowaway had brought aboard himself, and the crate bore no maker's mark to reveal where it had been built. Nothing found on him or in his hiding place revealed who he was or who had sent him. He was hauled off to a holding space below even the ship's ordinary brig, chained directly to the keel.

The party members directly involved in dealing with the stowaway (Noddy, Cosimo, Knick Nab, Mani, and Riu for his life-saving actions) were summoned by Captain Barrows to recount what had happened. When the Captain pressed Noddy on how the assailant had been struck down and asked outright whether he was a man of the cloth, Noddy explained he had served in the church as an altar boy but held no clerical office, crediting the gods for the decisive blow — an answer Barrows accepted without further question, and which kept the party's true abilities safely hidden behind the Two. The Captain then praised their repeated bravery and resourcefulness, noting this was not the first time they had saved him — Knick Nab's testimony had once helped clear his name at his own court-martial, and Werner and Mani had already foiled the bomb plots in port. He then confided in them the true nature of their voyage. Many of the crew's identity papers, he revealed, had been stolen while the ship was in port, and the "Advance" had left alone rather than with the fleet — both signs, to the more senior hands aboard, that something beyond a routine patrol was underway. Barrows admitted he had personally witnessed the Southern Navy's ability to command wind and sea in battle, a power no amount of Northern discipline or skill could counter, and that Captain Maynard's own logs and writings had never been recovered after his disappearance — an absence he called "extremely unusual." When Mani, turning on his charm, asked directly why their ship in particular was so important that enemies would go to such lengths against it, Barrows — visibly moved by how many times they had already saved him — answered plainly: guided by the Admiralty, which knew only that Maynard had learned something before he vanished, Barrows had been tasked with retracing that doomed voyage. The "Advance" was on a secret mission to return to the uncharted island where Maynard was lost, to investigate and understand the Southern Navy's mysterious capabilities, and was under orders not to seek out an engagement with the South along the way. He mentioned he intended to announce the broad outline of the mission to the rest of the crew within the next day or so, and that its more seasoned hands — unlike the newer recruits, who had only heard rumors — remembered all too well the North's unexplained defeats whenever the two navies had clashed, in fleet actions and single-ship duels alike. Captain Barrows expressed his growing trust in the young recruits, believing their presence on his ship might even be a blessing from The Two, though he confessed himself no man of the cloth — merely a fervent admirer of the Two.

  • Various unnamed sailors and midshipmen.

docs.title: Locations
docs.text:
• The "Advance": A frigate of the King's Navy. Events occurred while docked in The Capitol and later at sea.
    • The Orlop Deck: The deck immediately below the main deck, above the hold.
    • The Capstan: A large mechanism on deck used to raise the anchor, hoist sails, and bring the ship's boats aboard.
    • The Hold: Lowest storage deck of the "Advance," packed mostly with barrels and defined by the ship's structural ribs. Barrels served as the standard unit of cargo here — apples, salt pork, water, gunpowder, and ship's biscuit were all stored this way, with crates comparatively rare and live animals kept further aft. The stowaway was discovered here, hidden in a crate among ordinary cargo, stocked with a small barrel of water and bearing no maker's mark to reveal its origin.
    • Magazine Entrance: Location of the attack on the marine guard, at the end of a narrow corridor off the hold.
    • The Bow: Chosen by the party as their regular meeting spot during shared off-watch time to share information, partly because it draws fewer people — despite standing right by "the head," where the crew relieves themselves.
    • The prisoner's holding space: Below even the ship's ordinary brig; the stowaway was chained directly to the keel.
  • The Capitol Docks: Initial location where the bombing attempts occurred.

docs.title: Conflicts
docs.text:
• Attempted Bombings: Two rowboats carrying barrels of gunpowder and trigger mechanisms targeted the "Advance" and another nearby ship. Both were thwarted by the actions of Werner De Rendal and Mani, though righting and bailing out the recovered boats afterward took real effort.
  • Knick Nab Overboard: Knick Nab fell into the harbor water while climbing into the rigging during the alarm and was rescued.
  • Stowaway Attack:
    • An unnamed marine guard at the ship's magazine was attacked and severely wounded by a stowaway.
    • Noddy used Blur to approach unseen, Projected Light to reveal the scene, and Confusion to hamper the assailant while holding him off with his cutlass. The PCs (Noddy, Cosimo, Knick Nab, Mani) confronted and subdued the stowaway. Cosimo's "Strike One" spell was critical in incapacitating the assailant, who refused to surrender and had to be beaten into submission before being bound.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• The party experienced their first night and day aboard a sailing vessel, including the routines and assignments, and quickly learned that flame is tightly restricted below decks, with severe penalties for careless use of lanterns or candles.
  • Mani successfully used a Coin of Fate to aid in capsizing the second bomb-laden rowboat. Immediately after the attack, Captain Barrows wondered aloud whether the boats had been deliberately aimed at the ship's magazine — a remark that would prove prescient a week later.
  • The "Rules and Regulations of the King's Navy" were formally read to the crew — thirty-seven articles in all, covering blasphemy, drunkenness, flogging limits, theft of the ship's stores, powder, or arms, mutiny, and murder. Magic, pets, gambling, and relations between crew members were all noted as topics the Articles did not address.
  • The party began to notice that command and raw skill are different aptitudes aboard the "Advance": Werner, despite having authority over a small crew of sailors, often found himself directing veteran hands who could simply do the job better than he could himself.
  • Mani's inquiries with combat-experienced Marines revealed that boarding actions bear little resemblance to musket-line drill — once the volley is fired, it reportedly devolves into a close-quarters free-for-all of stabbing and struggling rather than any organized formation.
  • The party sensed cliques among the crew, including hands who had served under the ship's previous captain, Maynard, before Barrows took command.
  • A stowaway had been living in a crate in the hold for approximately a week, armed and with tools (lock picks), posing a significant threat to the ship's magazine.
  • Word spread among the crew that Werner and Mani were behind foiling the bomb boats, earning the pair a measure of quiet extra respect.
  • Captain Barrows revealed the secret mission of the "Advance": to sail to an uncharted island where Captain Maynard was lost, to investigate the Southern Navy's unexplained power over natural elements like wind and sea. He disclosed that many crew members' identity papers had been stolen while the ship was in port, that the "Advance" had left port alone rather than with the fleet, that he had personally witnessed the Southern Navy command wind and sea in battle, and that Maynard's own logs and writings were never recovered after his disappearance — all of which the Admiralty, which ordered this mission, could not explain.
  • Days into the voyage, with nothing but open ocean in every direction, the party realized none of them knew their heading; Werner, drawing on his own navigation background, confirmed the ship was sailing west-southwest.
  • The PCs discussed the nature of magic in their world, generally understanding it as miracles bestowed by "The Two." A bystanding sailor's surprised reaction to a small demonstration of Cosimo's power underscored the risk of being seen, and the party decided to be cautious about revealing their own magical abilities, preferring to wait for a critical moment.
  • Riu and Cosimo shared knowledge about different orders of priests, including militant "Censures" — smaller, more fiery clerics tasked with enforcing righteousness and rooting out anathema, historically renowned as elite fighters in battles for the kingdom. Priests are not normally seen armed except while traveling between postings, and typically travel and officiate in pairs.
  • The party noted the presence of two priests and a red-haired youth observing their departure from The Capitol, with the youth pointing directly at their ship, and connected the sighting to Stick Stab's earlier mention of a red-haired youth, whom Stick Stab had shown open hostility toward, saying it wouldn't trouble him if harm came to them. They speculated the bombing attempts were likely the work of a Southern sabotage cell targeting Northern shipping broadly, since a second, unrelated ship had also been targeted.

docs.title: Items Gained
docs.text:
• Knowledge of the "Rules and Regulations of the King's Navy," including a printed copy handed to Knick Nab to post by the main hatchway below decks.
  • A set of lock picks (taken from the subdued stowaway, subsequently handed over to an officer).
  • A packet of dense, unfamiliar food rations (taken from the stowaway, given to Riu for examination).

docs.title: Items Lost
docs.text: • One Coin of Fate (expended by Mani).

docs.title: Events and Actions
docs.text:
Following a recap of the previous session's events (including the capture of the saboteur, Ben, and Riu's healing of an injured marine), the "Advance" continued its voyage. Some crew members, including Cosimo Cellini Scivio, experienced seasickness, though his iron stomach spared him the worst of it; one of the newer midshipmen fared far worse, seen hanging over the rail and quietly ribbed by the crew for it. The party learned more about the ship's crew structure, including the officers, other midshipmen (Cedric, Giles, Wulf), and their own assigned crewmen (Burton, Hal, Odo, Mark).

Captain Barrows personally questioned Ben in the hold, where Lieutenant Conrad had already been beating him for information. Ben would admit only his name and that he had stowed away to sabotage the ship, offering nothing further even when the captain pressed him about the crate he had used to board — a question the captain punctuated with a pointed glance at the party, doing nothing to allay his suspicions of them. When the beating left Ben too battered to continue, Riu volunteered to tend him, diagnosing broken ribs, soft-tissue damage, and a concussion, and worked until he had restored much of Ben's stamina; the captain, impressed, began referring to him as "the surgeon's mate." Afterward, Knick Nab shed his marine jacket, covered his face, and talked his way past the guards to see Ben alone, wiping the blood from his face and murmuring a few words of Sanspeak in an attempt to pass himself off as a fellow agent. Ben gave no reaction, leaving Knick Nab unsure whether the message had landed; he later dropped a hint to the marines that Ben might be a Southern spy who would only open up to one of his own, though nothing came of it. A ship-wide search followed the sabotage attempt, with three teams escorted by marines combing the "Advance" stem to stern while Pocket flew reconnaissance overhead.

Riu, tasked with keeping the ship's sick-bay records for his neat penmanship, discovered that records from the "Advance's" previous, disastrous voyage were locked away and inaccessible to him. Seeking answers elsewhere, he asked Dr. Forester what had befallen the ship's earlier crew; the doctor, who had not sailed on that voyage himself, explained that the previous ship's doctor had died in a mutiny brought on by dwindling food and fresh water, after much of the crew lost faith in then-Lieutenant Barrows for what they saw as abandoning Captain Maynard. He added that the ship had been given up for lost for months before her unexpected return, and that while some reprovisioning had evidently taken place along the way, only Captain Barrows knew the particulars.

After approximately two weeks at sea, Pocket spotted a haze of land on the horizon before any lookout did, and Noddy's call carried down the length of the ship; sighting land after so long at sea always draws a crowd, and sailors crowded the forecastle to see for themselves. It was the Channel Islands — the edge of the known sea, home to scattered Islander settlements with some islands abandoned outright, and a stretch of water that would have been extraordinarily difficult to reach at all before the Great Change. Captain Barrows addressed the crew, revealing their mission was to venture past the Channels to find the previously lost Captain Maynard. He spoke of the dangers of the previous voyage and the fate of those who had mutinied.

Soon after entering the Channels, Noddy spotted a distant masthead astern and reported it to Midshipman Cedric, who confirmed the sighting himself and passed word up to Lieutenant Gunter; as the pursuer closed, her two masts, white sails, and blue pennant became visible from the crow's nest. She was identified as a Southern Navy vessel of similar size and armament to the "Advance", and Pocket flew out for a closer look to confirm she was a genuine warship rather than a mere boat. With the crew never having fired the ship's stern chasers, Captain Barrows ordered a live gunnery drill: Midshipman Giles's crew fired wildly and clipped their own ship's stern in the process, while Werner De Rendal's crew got a clean shot away, though neither had a target in range. Captain Barrows then laid out his plan to Werner: land a shore party on a nearby island with a stern chaser, hide until the pursuer passed, and open fire from the shore just before the "Advance" swung back into view to catch the Southern ship between them. Werner asked for enough elevation to sweep the enemy's decks with canister shot and was told to bring a block and tackle to manage it.

The PCs, Marine Hicks, and Werner's assigned crew were landed on the island — flat and scrubby, with rocky outcrops and marshy ground behind the sandy beach where they came ashore — and split into three groups: one hauled the boats clear and hid them, one manhandled the cannon up to a firing position among the rocks, and one scouted for cover, piling up sand and driftwood and rehearsing pistol reloads while they waited. Cosimo concealed the gun position with an illusion (Light Mirage). The Southern ship passed by unaware, but as the "Advance" began her return run, Noddy's seagull, Pocket, spotted the enemy launching a boat with four men toward the PCs' position.

When the Southern ship rounded the island's point again, Cosimo renewed the illusion and Werner ordered the cannon to fire. The first shot went wide; the second struck home, causing splinter damage; the third, canister aimed at the rigging, did little; and the fourth misfired and jammed the gun outright — the crew doused the barrel with water for fear it would explode, and Werner judged it could only be properly repaired back aboard ship. To draw the enemy's return fire away from the real gun, Cosimo also conjured a second, illusory cannon crew farther down the beach; when the Southern ship answered with a broadside, the grapeshot sailed high overhead, well wide of the actual position. Simultaneously, Cosimo created a fantasm of a musketeer further down the beach to distract the approaching enemy landing party. The "Advance" engaged the Southern ship with a broadside, scoring hits and notably killing an officer on the enemy's forecastle. The enemy ship also returned fire.

As the four-man landing party closed in, Cosimo's illusory swashbuckler — taunting them with cries of "Varlets, you have drawn but a pint of blood... your cowardice does you discredit, fie on you!" — drew their opening volley of musket and pistol fire away from the real party. With their weapons spent and reloading, Werner threw a javelin at the nearest sailor, catching him in the forearm and disrupting his reload, while Mani put a crossbow bolt into a second. Noddy cast Confusion on the same sailor Werner had javelined, and Riu wrapped Werner in a Blur to sharpen his defenses. The session ended there, with one sailor still closing on the shore party with a drawn saber as the naval battle continued offshore.

docs.title: Conflicts
docs.text:

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• The party learned more details about the "Advance's" crew, hierarchy, and armament, confirming she carries twelve guns, plus two stern chasers, two bow chasers, and four swivel-gun mounts (two currently fitted).
  • Captain Barrows elaborated on the mission to find Captain Maynard and the perils of the previous voyage, including a mutiny; Dr. Forester separately told Riu that the previous ship's doctor had died in that mutiny, brought on by a lack of food and fresh water and the crew's loss of faith in then-Lieutenant Barrows.
  • Riu discovered that the "Advance's" sick-bay records from her earlier, disastrous voyage are locked away and inaccessible to him.
  • Asked casually by a curious Cedric about Captain Barrows's history, the party stuck to their agreed official story crediting Knick Nab (the "cabin boy") for the recovery of the stolen papers that led to Barrows's acquittal, omitting the killings they were involved in during that earlier affair.
  • Cedric explained that only two routes lead back from the seas beyond the Channels: a southern route currently hostile and inadvisable, and a longer, harder northern route — the one the "Advance" used to limp home from her previous voyage, made worse by the crew not knowing their own position. He also mentioned a northern-held port within the Channels used mainly as a freshwater stop for ships heading further west.
  • The party discussed tactics for the shore ambush, including the use of Cosimo's illusion magic.
  • Werner De Rendal was placed in command of the shore party.
  • The PCs learned about the capabilities and limitations of their cannon and Cosimo's spells in a combat scenario.
  • Noddy's seagull, Pocket, proved useful for reconnaissance and impressed a skeptical crewman with obedience tricks that convinced him it truly was a trained pet.
  • The Channels see enough legitimate naval and commercial traffic that piracy is a dangerous trade there in wartime, and the Southern Navy is not known to employ privateers, which made the shadowing ship's purpose puzzling.
  • The party observed that the ship's two priests, Jacque and Nicolas, lead two prayer services a day attended by most of the crew who are not on duty.

  • The PCs in the shore party were issued pistols, rifles, a cutlass, a rapier, and a main-gauche, along with shovels, rope, a bag of rations, and a block and tackle from the ship's armory and stores.

docs.title: Items Lost
docs.text: • The cannon used by the shore party became jammed after a misfire; the crew doused it with water to prevent it exploding, and Werner determined it could not be repaired without proper shipboard tools.

docs.title: Marooned and Menaced: A Light in the Dark
Events and Actions
docs.text:
The session began with a recap of the party being deployed from the "Advance" onto a small, flat island in the Channel Islands. Their mission was to set up a cannon to ambush an enemy ship that had been shadowing them. As the plan unfolded, Cosimo drew on his newfound powers, apparently granted by the Mother and Father, first casting a protective Blur on Riu, then conjuring a static illusion of an empty shore to mask the party's true position, followed by an animated phantasm of a cannon crew firing to draw the enemy's attention — all of it kept entirely secret from the crew still aboard the "Advance." Werner opened fire on the approaching ship, blowing the head off a senior officer with a lucky shot before the cannon jammed.

As the "Advance" engaged the enemy vessel, four enemy soldiers who had been dropped off from their ship advanced on the party's position, drawn in by the phantasmal cannon fire on the beach. Cosimo conjured a second apparition, the flamboyant "Handsome Gulliver Gold," to taunt and duel the approaching soldiers; his opening insults successfully drew all four enemies' first volley harmlessly onto himself, and he even flinched and bled convincingly when struck to sell the illusion, holding their attention throughout. A fierce fight ensued. Noddy's sleep spells proved highly effective, putting two of the soldiers to sleep, while a Distraction spell left another confused after Werner wounded him with a thrown harpoon. Mani, Knick Nab, and Werner engaged the remaining enemies directly, with Werner inflicting notable wounds with his javelins and dagger. Mani fought Dieter, the enemy leader, who held the advantage of higher footing; Mani tried to disarm him outright, but the higher ground blunted the attempt, and it took several more exchanges of footwork and steel to wear Dieter down until he was outmatched and taken. Knick Nab, meanwhile, traded blows with the soldier still duelling Handsome Gulliver Gold, eventually landing a solid knee strike that staggered him and knocked him back, interrupting his attack on the illusion. Cosimo delivered a fatal dagger strike to one of the sleeping soldiers. A second soldier — Hans — was left bleeding badly from several of Werner's smaller wounds; he survived, but only after Riu worked to stabilize him once the fighting ended. The remaining soldier, put to sleep unharmed in the bushes, was taken without further struggle. Before releasing his concentration, Cosimo gave Handsome Gulliver Gold standing orders to finish the fight on his own: the illusion capped the encounter with a final flourish, rising into the air with a booming proclamation that there would be no survivors before vanishing in a poof of light — a display that rattled the marine Stanley more than either of Cosimo's earlier illusions had. Stanley himself had held his fire through the melee, unable to find a clear shot with his allies so entangled with the enemy.

After the combat, the party found that the "Advance" had continued its pursuit of the fleeing enemy ship, leaving them stranded. Werner tried signalling the "Advance" with flags, spelling out "Have three prisoners. Will you return?" but got no response; Noddy's familiar, Pocket, confirmed no one on their ship was looking back or paying attention. Both ships passed out of sight around a headland with no visible damage to either, though the party had heard screams during the earlier cannon exchange and reasoned that the enemy ship, having been forced to divert some of its guns toward the beach, had been unable to fully man both broadsides against the "Advance" — their diversion had done its job.

The party took stock of their situation. They had three prisoners: Dieter, the leader; Hans, badly wounded; and a third soldier, unharmed. They secured them methodically, one at a time, keeping weapons trained on each while he was tied so none could bolt, then looted the fallen enemies, recovering weapons and provisions, but no coin. Cosimo then climbed to the highest point nearby and gave a dramatic speech, proclaiming that Handsome Gulliver Gold was a guardian angel sent by the Mother and Father — a declaration made in complete sincerity, as Cosimo genuinely believes his powers to be divinely granted rather than his own. The prisoners looked on with what seemed to be either awe or terror, and Stanley, though less shaken by the earlier illusions, was visibly unsettled at having watched a man fly into the sky and disappear.

Before setting off, Werner spent roughly half an hour with the gun crew clearing the jammed cannon so it would be ready to fire again. Werner, Mani, Knick Nab, and the three NPC gun crew members then set off to retrieve the enemy's boat from the other side of the island. During their trek, Pocket discovered a source of fresh water. They found the boat abandoned, with no provisions aboard save drag marks in the sand and a single set of footprints leading off into the brush. After a strenuous three-and-a-half-hour row, they brought it back to the main camp. Meanwhile, Riu, Cosimo, Noddy, and Stanley set up a small camp in a depression concealed from view of the sea, gathered firewood, and debated what to do with the fallen soldier's body. A proper burial at sea was ruled out for lack of sailcloth and any water deep enough nearby; after briefly considering tying the body to a boat instead, they buried him in a crevice weighted down with stones. Asked if anyone present could act as clergy for the rites, Riu demurred that he was "only an altar boy," but it was nonetheless Riu — as the party's closest thing to a follower of the Two — who said a few words over the grave, alongside Dieter, who spoke for his fallen man.

Riu attempted to stabilize the badly wounded prisoner, Hans, combining his healing abilities with his medical training: he used magic to halt the worst of the bleeding outright, then stitched one wound closed properly and bound a second as best he could. The stitched wound held, but the bound one remained precarious — Hans was stable, but still too fragile to be moved without risking it reopening. As an experiment, Mani placed the Medallion (which he had previously taken from Stick Stab in the Capitol) on Hans.

As night fell, a fire was built. Riu tried fishing without success, while Cosimo foraged, gathering edible cattails and a handful of berries along with an unfamiliar plant he suspected might be nightshade, hoping to confirm it later against the herbalism book he had left aboard the "Advance." Beyond what could be foraged, their provisions amounted to the plain fare they'd brought off the ship: salt pork and biscuit. With ten people between the party, the gun crew, and Stanley, the party weighed shorter watches against fewer, longer ones before settling on the traditional four-hour rotation; three-person watches were established, with one watcher covering the prisoners, one the sea, and one the island's interior. During their watch, Werner and Cosimo observed a mysterious, faint flicker of light in the distance across the island, appearing and disappearing a few times in a way that suggested a hooded lantern. Werner climbed a nearby tree to get a better bearing and confirmed the light came from an unexplored part of the island, away from both the ships' route and where the enemy's boat had been found. Wary of tipping off whoever was out there, the party chose not to wake the prisoners, instead leaving the gun crew and Stanley to guard them along with the cannon and boats, arming one sailor with a captured pistol and setting the password "Advance" to guard against friendly fire. Werner then woke Riu, Noddy, and Knick Nab; Knick Nab also glimpsed the light before the session ended, with the party discussing how to scout or flank the source of the potential new threat.

docs.text:

docs.title: Conflicts
docs.text:
• Shoreline Ambush: The party engaged in combat with four enemy soldiers who landed on the island.
    • Cosimo's apparitions ("empty shore," "phantom cannon crew," "Handsome Gulliver Gold") played a significant role in distracting and taunting the enemy; Handsome Gulliver Gold ended the fight with a theatrical levitating exit as Cosimo's concentration lapsed.
    • Noddy's sleep spells put two enemies to sleep; a Distraction spell confused a third after Werner wounded him with a harpoon.
    • Werner, Mani, and Knick Nab fought directly, inflicting and receiving wounds; Mani wore down Dieter's advantage of higher ground before taking him, while Knick Nab staggered his own opponent with a knee strike that interrupted his attack on Handsome Gulliver Gold.
    • One enemy soldier was killed: by Cosimo's dagger while asleep.
    • Three enemy soldiers were captured: Dieter (leader), Hans (badly wounded from Werner's javelin and dagger wounds), and one other (asleep and unharmed).
  • Mysterious Light: At the end of the session, a mysterious light was spotted on the island, indicating a potential new, unknown presence. The party set a guard password ("Advance") and left the prisoners asleep and guarded while preparing to investigate.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• The party is stranded on the island, as the "Advance" has left in pursuit of the enemy ship and did not respond to signals. The party reasoned their diversion had worked, since the enemy ship had been unable to fully man both broadsides while some of its guns fired at the beach.
  • The island has a source of fresh water and little else of value; the neighboring island may be a better source of resources if needed. Aside from foraged cattails and berries, the party's food is limited to the salt pork and biscuit they brought off the ship.
  • The party now possesses three small boats (their two, plus the enemy's) and their cannon.
  • A discussion was held regarding the proper disposal of a fallen enemy soldier: burial at sea was ruled out for lack of sailcloth and sufficiently deep water nearby, so the party buried him ashore instead, with Dieter (enemy leader) and Riu both saying a few words over him.
  • Riu asked Dieter about the South's religious practices; Dieter was unsure whether the Divinity of Two extends to the South; it does exist there, but unlike in the North, it is not mandated.
  • Cosimo's public declarations attributing events to divine intervention by the Mother and Father were made in complete sincerity and were noted by the prisoners and Stanley.
  • Mani placed the Medallion (previously taken from Stick Stab) on the prisoner Hans as an experiment.

docs.title: The Pygmies of Bitterroot Isle and Hans's Escape
Events and Actions
docs.text:
The party, stranded on a small, flat island in the Channel Islands (Bitterroot Isle) after a naval battle, spotted mysterious lights flickering in the dark on two separate occasions during the night, prompting speculation that it might be a hooded lantern. Werner De Rendal had his men load their captured muskets and pistol and position the cannon, charged with canister, to cover the beach, while Knick Nab slipped out alone to investigate; his approach was noisy at first, and though he pressed on more carefully, a thorough search of the surrounding scrub turned up no trace of the light or whoever carried it. Werner tried to recall any island legends of wandering lights, but nothing came to mind. At dawn, before setting out again, Riu treated the badly injured prisoner Hans so he could be moved without bleeding, and the party fed and watered all three captives. Werner De Rendal, Mani, and Knick Nab then followed a faint, low-lying game track inland — the kind of trail worn by small, wary animals rather than anything larger — to a hidden burrow entrance; an attempt to call out reassurances to whoever was inside went unanswered. Tied by the ankles with a rope and carrying a candle and knife, Knick Nab crawled down into it, finding a small junction roughly twenty feet in with three passages.

Gunfire erupted from their camp. Noddy's seagull, Pocket, observed Stanley, the Marine, firing at an unseen target. Some PCs rushed back, learning Stanley had seen a "man." Werner De Rendal was struck by a small stone projectile, the blow driving his forearm hard into his own chest; once he recovered, he charged toward where the shot had come from, gun raised, shouting for whoever it was to drop their weapons and surrender, but found no one there. Mani investigated, found another burrow close to the camp, and fired his rifle down it; Noddy then tried to smoke it out by packing the entrance with brush and grass and lighting it with a firebrand from the camp, though the fire caught poorly and achieved little. The party then sealed the hole with rocks to keep whatever lived there from reaching the camp unseen. Searching the area, Cosimo recognized their attacker might be connected to the Bitterroot sticks the old woman had given him and Noddy back in the Capitol. He recalled lore from a herbalore book he had once read about pygmies using Bitterroot and their extermination by the Divinity of Two roughly a hundred years ago, and the party debated whether the culprit deserved to be exterminated as an "abomination" or given the benefit of the doubt — it might even be a shipwrecked child. Cosimo ultimately deferred, agreeing to attempt peaceful contact first while reserving the option to capture the creature and hand it to the Two for interrogation and reward if that failed. With Hans teaching them a few halting words of Islander — "we mean no harm" and "here's some food" — they left an offering of food and Bitterroot at the first burrow, calling the phrases down into the dark.

Later, Werner De Rendal caught a massive Marlin — after nearly settling for a minnow — and butchered it expertly into two flawless fillets, earning the nickname "Marlin" and keeping its spike as a trophy. Someone suggested smoking the meat to preserve it, but the party settled for simply eating their fill before it spoiled; the catch fed the whole camp, including the prisoners, and some was wrapped in leaves and left as a further offering at the burrow entrance. Cosimo interrogated the prisoners Hans, Dieter, and the unnamed sailor about the Southern Navy's uncanny seamanship, probing whether their recent victory came from leaked battle plans or some mystical command of the waves — wondering aloud if Southern officers wore ceremonial robes and chanted to summon it — but learned nothing solid beyond the sailors' own sense that the Southern ships had simply outsailed them at every turn. The party also agreed to treat the prisoners more humanely, loosening their bonds during meals and giving them turns of comfort, reasoning that defeated men deserved better than to be treated like animals. As evening fell, they fortified the camp by hauling the cannon inside the perimeter, flipping the ship's boats for cover to form a small corral, and gathering in the oars.

Near dawn, while Werner and Mani were on watch, sling bullets whistled past them. Werner called the Islander phrase for peace into the dark even as he raised his gun, while Mani charged towards a spotted light, followed by Knick Nab. In the ensuing confusion, Cosimo accidentally shot Stanley in the foot, severing a toe. Riu stopped the bleeding and gave Stanley a piece of Bitterroot to chew, which visibly eased his pain. Mani and Knick Nab found the assailants had vanished into another hole. The party resolved to seal the tunnels the next morning with a smoky fire of brush and a trickle of gunpowder — a plan overtaken by events before it could be carried out.

During this commotion, the prisoner Hans cut himself free and escaped, aided by an old Islander lady rowing a small, one-man skiff with a tiller; Cosimo's knife was found missing afterward, presumably taken by Hans in the escape. The PCs gave chase in their own larger, four-oared boat despite the enemy's head start. Cosimo conjured a hideous, troll-like sea monster — scraggly hair tangled with seashells, a wide mouth full of shark-like teeth, mottled green skin, and long clawed arms — to rear out of the water in their path, roaring that it would eat them if they didn't turn back, but Hans and the old lady rowed on without flinching. After several missed rifle shots and two missed cannon shots, Hans and the lady reached the shore of the adjacent, larger, forested island (Totem Isle) and fled into the woods. The party weighed whether it was wise to follow onto unfamiliar ground where they might be badly outnumbered, but decided that recovering Hans and learning how he'd made contact with the Islanders was worth the risk. Knick Nab, Werner De Rendal, Riu, Noddy, Cosimo, and Mani beached beside the enemy's boat, tied it to their own so it couldn't be used again, and pursued inland, leaving Stanley, the gun crew, and the remaining two prisoners on Bitterroot Isle.

On Totem Isle, Noddy sent Pocket to track the fugitives while remaining with Cosimo at the boat. Mani, Knick Nab, Werner, and Riu chased into the forest, finding broken undergrowth where the pair had crashed through before the trail split; Mani and Werner went right, Knick Nab and Riu went left. Knick Nab and Riu misread the disturbed ground, wrongly concluding their quarry had doubled back toward the coast, and returned to an empty beach. Mani and Werner also lost the trail on their side. Partway up the hill beyond the treeline, Werner found a tall tree on a rocky outcropping and climbed it; from its height he could see down to the beach and along the shoreline in both directions but found no trace of habitation anywhere — no roads, buildings, or other sign of people — before spotting birds bursting from the canopy further up the slope, suggesting their quarry's direction. He and Mani decided to continue the pursuit towards that area as the session ended.

docs.title: Events and Actions
docs.text:
The party, having pursued Hans and an old Islander woman onto Totem Isle, split to follow two diverging paths leading up from the beach. Knick Nab and Cosimo took the left-hand path but lost the trail after a while and doubled back toward the beach. Mani and Riu took the right-hand path, and when the ground itself stopped giving up clues, Mani climbed a tree to scan the canopy for any disturbance among the birds that might betray someone moving through the forest below — and spotted exactly that, further up a prominent hill, Blackstone Peak. Feeling a strange pull in the same direction, Mani led Riu up toward the summit. Knick Nab and Cosimo, having lost their own trail, chose to climb the hill as well, reasoning it would offer the best vantage point over the island. Werner De Rendal and Noddy remained with the boats, with Noddy sending his seagull, Pocket, to scout for their ship, the "Advance" (which was not sighted).

At the peak, the party reunited. Mani's strange attraction intensified. They discovered a small, seemingly abandoned observation post, complete with a hammock, a writing desk, and two small chests. One chest contained a remarkably high-quality spyglass, and the other held writing materials and three small books. Two books were blank, while the third was a logbook whose front pages — some twelve to fifteen leaves, by their estimate — had been torn out, leaving only a single legible entry dated approximately seven months prior, detailing an unremarkable day's observations from the lookout. Riu used the new spyglass to survey the surrounding country, confirming a clear view down to the beach, out across the channel their ship had passed through, and along a chain of hills further inland of comparable height to Blackstone Peak, marking this as a genuinely large island; the dense forest below, however, hid whatever lay beneath its canopy. Cosimo sensed a source of power at the peak. Certain the pull had led him to something at the post itself, Mani searched the area and turned up nothing more mystical than an old latrine pit — a sobering reminder that not every strong feeling points to treasure.

Refocusing, Mani realized the pull was coming from beneath him and began digging, uncovering a large, perfectly flat, black, stone-like surface with a subtle shimmer. The party worked together to clear more of it, determining it was a large, circular or oval object. Cosimo, meanwhile, attempted a magic ritual to cast "Detect Magic" — a spell three levels beyond his ability — with Mani kneeling in prayer beside him and Knick Nab reluctantly joining in to help; their support narrowed the ritual's steep penalty considerably, and the casting succeeded on a partial success. Directed at the surface, the chests, and everything else nearby, it detected no active magic anywhere. While Cosimo prepared his ritual, Riu cast a "Detect Power" spell of his own across the post's ordinary belongings — the ground, the hammock, the makeshift table, the surrounding trees — and found nothing magical among any of them either.

The breakthrough came when Mani knelt to listen to the surface and his Medallion brushed against it, sticking fast like a magnet. All party members found their Medallions exhibited the same property, while other metals did not. Mani's own attempt to attune to the surface fell short, but Riu then succeeded (after an initial failure and spending a coin), learning that the surface was an immense source of "pure power," though not of a type he could directly use himself. Cosimo came agonizingly close to drawing nine power points directly from the surface through channeling, but fell just short; when he later cast his ritual using only his own reserves, he was left convinced the surface really could be drawn from, if only he understood it better. Werner's stonemason's eye and knowledge of stone lore found nothing familiar in the material either — it took no tool marks, would not scratch or chip even under a chisel, and rang like solid stone when struck, unlike anything he had ever encountered. Recalling the old Islander women's claim back on Bitterroot Isle that chewing the plant could reveal hidden truths, the party also tried a pinch of their dwindling store of Bitterroot on the mystery; it left them feeling soothed, but taught them nothing more about the surface. During these events, attempts were made by Werner De Rendal, Cosimo, and Knick Nab to remove Mani's Medallion, but all failed (often due to distractions), while Mani demonstrated he could remove both Werner De Rendal's and Knick Nab's — so far the only PC able to do so, and notably also the first of the Mani/Cosimo pair to have acquired his Medallion in the first place.

Piecing together what his channeling and his ritual had each told him, Cosimo concluded that the surface itself, not something hidden within or beneath it, was the source of power — this was no vault or artifact-with-contents waiting to be opened, but a solid mass of the stuff, which meant there was no door or entrance to be found no matter how thoroughly they searched.

With evening coming on, the party made camp at the peak rather than risk the descent in darkness. Werner dug a shallow, screened fire pit at the crossroads clearing, positioned so its light couldn't be seen from either the main channel or further inland, while the others continued digging and posted watches through the night. The party debated whether to relocate their whole camp — cannon included — from the smaller island to Totem Isle, but reached no firm decision. In the morning, they made one last push to understand the buried surface: mathematics suggested the shape was most likely a true circle rather than a square, so they dug a trench to what should have been its center and cleared a wide arc of one edge to compare for evenly spaced "slots," but both efforts turned up nothing — no seams, markings, or means of entry of any kind. Judging that reburying the site wasn't worth the effort, since the disturbed ground would give it away regardless, they resolved to mark its location and leave it as found.

Deciding to investigate further inland, the party followed a path leading down from the peak. Knick Nab's tracking confirmed the path had seen no real traffic in the roughly seven months since the peak's logbook fell silent, but partway down he picked up much fresher sign — a broken branch, a smeared footprint on a log — from someone who had passed within the last day or two. Backtracking the trail, he found it led all the way up to the observation post itself, meaning whoever left it had been at the peak very recently, not simply passing through months ago. Following the path onward, the party came to a small, abandoned camp by a lake.

The camp contained several tents, partially constructed buildings, and signs of a hasty departure (a third boat missing, with drag marks in the mud less than a couple of days old). Searching the camp, they found approximately ten bodies of sailors, dead for about seven months, apparently killed by spear-like weapons. Several had fallen behind makeshift barricades or overturned supplies, suggesting they had been defending the camp when they died; the recovered spearheads and javelins were notably small, not standard shipboard weapons, raising the same suspicion of a small-statured attacker that Bitterroot Isle had already planted in the party's minds. The bodies and the camp seemed largely unlooted of personal valuables, and the number of hammocks strung between the trees roughly matched the number of dead, suggesting few if any had escaped besides whoever fled in the missing boat. However, they discovered a crate of muskets, a crate of gunpowder and shot-making materials, a crate filled with Southern Navy uniforms of various ranks (including officer regalia for naval and ground forces, though tellingly none of the dead were dressed as officers), and waterproof bags containing more log entries (dated 8-7 months ago, with nothing older) and a folder of documents written in a cipher. None of the crates bore any maker's stamp, ship's name, or other identifying mark. Another crate of gunpowder had already been broken open and spilled across the ground, ruined; Knick Nab, using his knack for finding what others try to hide, checked the camp for concealed caches but turned up nothing beyond what already lay in plain sight.

As they were processing these discoveries, the party debated how to bring their haul back — hauling it up and over the peak, or loading it into one of the camp's own boats and risking the unknown river that drained the lake — and settled on the boats for now. Werner argued that if the muskets couldn't be gotten out safely, he'd sooner sink them in the river than leave them for hostile hands, while Knick Nab held that recovering Southern orders and intelligence was their duty as Navy men regardless of the risk. A distant "boom," sounding like their cannon from the other island, interrupted the discussion; the party couldn't agree whether it meant their crew was signalling them home or fighting off an attack. Cosimo then used a "Guess" spell to try and locate the cipher, guessing it was in the "left tent."

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• The Black Surface: A large, circular/oval, black, stone-like surface was discovered buried at the top of Blackstone Peak. It is a source of immense "pure power" and magnetically attracts the PCs' Medallions. Mathematics suggested the buried shape was likely a true circle. The material defied every attempt to identify it: it took no tool marks, could not be scratched or chipped even with a chisel, matched no stone Werner De Rendal had ever encountered, and showed no seams, slots, or markings anywhere the party exposed; neither a Detect Power spell nor a chewed pinch of Bitterroot revealed anything further about its nature. Cosimo concluded from his channeling and ritual that the surface itself was the power source, not a container hiding something within — meaning there was no door or entrance to find, only the substance itself.
  • Medallion Properties: Further details about the Medallions were revealed/confirmed: they stick to the black surface. Attempts by Werner De Rendal, Cosimo, and Knick Nab to remove Mani's Medallion failed. Mani was able to remove Werner De Rendal's and Knick Nab's Medallions, leading to the understanding that only Mani has so far demonstrated this ability. Mani was also confirmed as the first of the Mani/Cosimo pair to find his Medallion.
  • Attunement: Riu successfully attuned to the black surface (after an initial failure and spending a coin), gaining an understanding of its nature: it is pure power, but not of a type he can use. Mani's own attempt to attune fell short. Cosimo separately attempted to draw power from the surface directly; though unsuccessful, he came close and believes it could work with a better understanding of the source.
  • Abandoned Southern Camp: The party discovered a 7-month-old abandoned camp that belonged to Southern forces. This suggests a Southern presence on the island around that time. None of the dead were dressed as officers, despite officer regalia being present among the crated uniforms, and none of the crates bore any identifying mark.
  • A Small Attacker: The camp's dead bore wounds from unusually small spears and javelins, not standard shipboard weapons, and several had died behind makeshift barricades — consistent with the same small, hostile presence the party already suspects from Bitterroot Isle.
  • Logbooks & Cipher: Log entries from the peak and the camp indicate activity 7-8 months ago. The peak's own logbook had roughly 12-15 leaves torn from its front; based on the party's rough estimate of two pages per month, this represents several prior months of entries, though the exact span is unknown. Ciphered documents suggest covert Southern operations.
  • Recent Activity: Someone was at the peak observation post as recently as the last day or two, then travelled inland towards the abandoned camp — this was fresh activity, not simply an old, undisturbed trail.
  • Mani's Connection: Mani feels a strong, unexplained pull to Blackstone Peak and the black surface.
  • Cosimo's Power Sense: Cosimo can sense sources of power that could aid his magic.
  • Distant Cannon Fire: A "boom" from the direction of their other camp interrupted the search of the abandoned camp; the party couldn't agree whether it meant their crew was signalling them to return or fighting off an attack.
