docs.title: Abominations, Accusations, and a Ship Ahead
Events and Actions
docs.text:
The session began with a recap of the party's discoveries on Totem Isle: a Southern spy post, and a mysterious, large, black, circular, and incredibly hard surface (referred to by the party as a "strange black rock") near the top of Blackstone Peak, which both Mani and Cosimo sensed strongly. Mani recalled having felt drawn toward the hill from the very start of the chase, independent of tracking the escaped prisoner, and that when he had lain against the rock, his Medallion gave a small click and briefly clung to its surface as though pulled by a lodestone. For Noddy's benefit, since he had missed the previous session, the party replayed their investigation of the surface: Knick Nab was the only one able to successfully attune to it, and neither Cosimo's detect magic nor Riu's own divination could find any trace of active magic in it at any range. Despite this, both Cosimo and Riu felt strongly that power could be drawn from it, though neither could actually manage to do so. Noddy then attempted his own attunement and succeeded, gaining the same sense the others had: that the surface was a massive source of power he might one day learn to use, though he had no idea how. Cosimo's "Item Lore" spell confirmed it as a "giant chunk of power" with no discernible purpose and no active magic of its own. Werner De Rendal's attempt to chip a sample from it with a stonemason's hammer and chisel failed outright — the surface would not even scratch.

As the party descended the far side of the hill on Totem Isle, Mani kept a careful watch for any sign of Hans — the Southern prisoner who had escaped custody with the aid of an Old Islander Woman — or of the woman herself, but found no trace of either, concluding they were likely watching unseen from higher ground. The path led to a recently constructed, now abandoned Southern camp by a lake. The camp contained bodies of Southern soldiers — mauled further by scavenging wildlife, but bearing wounds from knife, spear, and sling-stone rather than gunfire, which the party took as confirmation the pygmies were responsible — alongside Southern uniforms, muskets, and papers written in cipher. Several of the camp's boats stood functional but abandoned on the lakeshore, and one showed signs of having recently been taken, consistent with how Hans and the Old Islander Woman might have made their escape. A cannon shot was heard from the direction of the first island where they had left some of their crew, and Noddy's seagull familiar, Pocket, spotted the "Advance" arriving in the channel and smoke rising from the first island.

Loading up with muskets to carry down, the party climbed back to the hilltop to check on the "Advance" through the spy glass, spotting it gliding into the channel and, through the lens, the two Southern prisoners and gun crew still being ferried in from the first island. As they turned to head down, Mani looked once more at the black rock and confided in Knick Nab a growing unease: if all magic truly came from the Two, as he had always believed, what was this thing that neither god had blessed? Knick Nab's best guess was that there might simply be other gods out there too. The party then decided to return to the "Advance," taking some Southern uniforms and muskets. Knick Nab salvaged a gold tooth and an earring from the dead Southerners. They rowed back to the "Advance," capturing an extra small boat as a prize — with Mani formally rechristening Cosimo's illusionary champion, until then known only as "Handsome," as "Handsome Gulliver Gold." Onboard, they reported their findings to Lieutenant Gunter, including the Southern camp, the pygmies (dubbed "Abominations" by the crew), the strange black rock (mentioned only briefly, without detail on its true significance), the ciphered papers, and a journal from the spy post indicating the post was last active 6-8 months ago. Captured muskets and uniforms were turned over to the Master of Arms, Bors; Knick Nab, trailing the gear out of curiosity, discovered that the ship kept no dedicated store of spare uniforms — the gear ended up with the sailmaker's mate instead, stored alongside spare sailcloth. Mani and Knick Nab kept pistols for themselves — Knick Nab, being ambidextrous, took two, cased differently from Northern equipment, along with gunpowder, shot, and bullet molds.

Later, Werner De Rendal, Cosimo, Knick Nab, Riu, Noddy, and Mani were summoned by Captain Barrows. They recounted their findings, particularly about the "Abominations." Pressed on the size of the Southern force, the party estimated 12 to 20 based on the camp's size and number of beds, though predation on some of the remains made an exact count impossible. Mani, framing the pygmies as Abominations born outside the sight of the Two, suggested that — time permitting — purging the island's population might be worth pursuing as a secondary objective alongside recapturing Hans; Captain Barrows agreed such creatures should be dealt with, though the voyage west remained the priority. He then sent for Prelate Jacque. Cosimo, fetching the prelate, found him and the younger priest, Nicolas, startled while looking through books. The party repeated their story. Prelate Jacque, after viewing a chart of the area, requested a private discussion with the Captain.

Knick Nab — who, as the Captain's de facto cabin boy, slept in a small alcove just outside the Captain's cabin and enjoyed freer run of the ship than the others — and Noddy (via Pocket, perched at the stern windows) eavesdropped on the Captain and Prelate. They overheard an argument: Jacque wanted to return to The Capitol due to the "Abominations" and Cosimo's powers, his suspicion fueled in part by Stanley's awed account of "Handsome Gulliver Gold" rising into the air during the earlier fight with the Southerners. Captain Barrows refused to deviate from his orders to sail west but agreed to stop at the next port, Port Zylos, for Jacque to send word. Jacque insisted Cosimo be investigated in The Capitol and kept confined until then, to which the Captain reluctantly agreed.

The PCs began to plot how to discredit Prelate Jacque to prevent Cosimo's removal, privately worrying that their earlier discovery of Bitterroot might be connected to the origin of the "butternut people" and recalling that the Church had previously moved to erase all knowledge of the root; they resolved to keep what remained of their own stock hidden from Jacque. Cosimo was confined to his bunk by Lieutenant Gunter. Captain Barrows then privately tutored Knick Nab in navigation, showing him charts of the Channel Islands and their planned, somewhat indirect, route to Port Zylos (estimated 4-5 days) — a route chosen partly to avoid known shoals and partly, Knick Nab suspected, to keep their heading obscure from any hidden observers. Barrows also pointed out an island along the way known for fresh water (and snakes), and explained that the ship they had pursued earlier had escaped south into a channel prone to fog banks — not an uncommon occurrence there — rather than out toward open water, repeating something he'd shared before: that the Southerners seemed to have some ability to call upon the weather itself. Wary that the Captain's course might simply be humoring them, Mani had Werner De Rendal quietly confirm with the ship's pilot that they truly were bound for the port, which he was able to verify.

The party initiated their plan against Prelate Jacque. Having weighed harsher options — a staged accident, or besmirching Jacque's reputation outright — they settled on the safer course of making him appear to be losing his grip on reality, reckoning it least likely to invite further scrutiny from the Church. They also set up a simple watch, with Noddy tracking Jacque's movements from his usual post in the crow's nest and signalling down to the others, while Cosimo's trips to relieve himself doubled as his cue to act. Noddy, discovering for the first time that he could channel spells through Pocket's senses, attempted to put Jacque to sleep with a spirit mastery spell while the bird watched him through his cabin's porthole; the casting succeeded, but Jacque proved too strong-willed to be affected and simply continued reading. Over the next two days, Jacque missed both morning and evening services, with Nicolas covering for him each time. Knick Nab's first attempt to slip into Jacque's cabin while the prelate was at the head was abandoned as too risky with people watching, but a later attempt succeeded: he found Jacque researching "History of Heresy," the religious practices of the southern "sand people" (one such book left face-down and clearly well-thumbed), the "Fire Cult," and maps of southern lands including the "Glass Lands" and their coastal cities. Cosimo created a foul, eye-watering stench at the ship's head while Jacque was using it, driving him to retreat below in disgust and order Cosimo out of sight, and later conjured a sulfurous, brimstone-like smell around Jacque's cabin at dusk, drawing a midshipman and a knot of confused sailors to investigate before it dissipated. He also used a sound illusion to make strange noises — blasphemous swearing — appear to come from Jacque's cabin floorboards. Noddy repeatedly cast Distraction on Jacque whenever he came into view, leaving him prone to stumbles and lapses. Meanwhile Mani quietly spread doubt about the prelate among the crew, reminding anyone who would listen of Cosimo's heroics — including catching the assassin who had tried to blow up the powder room — and wondering aloud why the prelate had turned against him. Cosimo's own attempts to attend services met with increasing restriction: Jacque himself first ordered him below decks after the stench incident, but Cosimo defied this to attend evening service anyway; Nicolas turned him away, and Cosimo's loud protest about being denied his right to worship drew a crowd and set the crew talking, turning his confinement — until then not general knowledge — into shipboard gossip. The next morning, Nicolas had two Marines physically escort him below decks and post permanent guard over him, leaving the party to communicate with him only at mealtimes or when he was allowed to relieve himself. On the second day, as Cosimo created his sulfurous smell outside Jacque's cabin, Noddy spotted an unknown ship ahead — smaller than the "Advance" and thought at first glance to be a merchant vessel.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• Noddy, like Mani and Cosimo, sensed that the strange black rock on Totem Isle was a significant source of power. Only Knick Nab and Noddy have so far managed to attune to it directly, and even they don't know how to draw upon it; the rock itself was found to be impervious to damage, and when Mani had lain against it, his Medallion briefly clung to its surface with an audible click, as though pulled by a lodestone.
  • The Southern spy camp on Totem Isle had been inactive for approximately 6-8 months, according to a journal found there.

  • The "pygmies" of Totem Isle are small (two to three feet tall), blue-skinned, dressed in white but for a red-clad leader, live in a network of tunnels, use primitive weapons, and are hostile.
  • The party speculated privately that Bitterroot may be connected to the origin of the "butternut people," though this remains unconfirmed, and chose to keep their own remaining stock of the root hidden from Prelate Jacque.
  • It was reconfirmed that only Mani seems capable of removing the party's Medallions from others.
  • Captain Barrows is under orders to proceed west and is resistant to returning to The Capitol.
  • Prelate Jacque is deeply suspicious of Cosimo's abilities and the "pygmies," demanding an official investigation in The Capitol; his suspicion was fueled in part by Stanley's account of "Handsome Gulliver Gold" rising into the air during the earlier fight with the Southerners.
  • The "Advance" plans to stop at Port Zylos. Captain Barrows is teaching Knick Nab navigation, and estimates the voyage there at four to five days; Werner De Rendal separately confirmed with the ship's pilot that they were indeed on course.
  • Mani, reflecting on the party's run of fortune — including three Southern ships captured to date — privately concluded they must be genuinely blessed, and worried that Prelate Jacque's suspicions threatened to undermine the Captain's trust in that blessing as much as Cosimo's own standing.
  • The other Southern ship escaped earlier into a channel to the south known for fog banks, not an uncommon occurrence in the area, rather than out toward open water.
  • Knick Nab discovered Prelate Jacque researching "History of Heresy," the religious practices of the southern "sand people," the Fire Cult, and southern geography (including the "Glass Lands" and cities there).
  • The party discussed strategies to discredit Prelate Jacque and prevent Cosimo from being taken to The Capitol, rejecting harsher options such as a staged accident in favor of making him appear to be losing his sanity.

docs.title: A Captured Ship and a New Command
Events and Actions
docs.text:
The session opened with a review of the party's ongoing plan to discredit the elder priest, Prelate Jacque, aboard the "Advance," whose suspicions about Cosimo's magic threatened to have him shipped off to the capital for investigation. Their efforts so far had included Cosimo conjuring illusions of foul smells and ranting voices from Jacque's cabin, coordinated through a chain of lookouts who signalled whenever the old priest left his quarters. Rumours of Cosimo's abilities continued to spread through the crew in exaggerated form — the "Handsome Gulliver Gold" illusion, a mysterious extra cannon down the coast, and a sea troll story that had grown into a small legend — and Cosimo had briefly been guarded in his bunk after a second unsanctioned appearance at chapel, though the guards had since been lifted.

Noddy, keeping watch from the mast, was first to spot a small, single-masted ship in the distance; the alarm went out and the "Advance" beat to quarters. The party scattered to their stations: Mani fell in with the other Marines at the forecastle before being sent aloft to the fighting top as a sharpshooter, Riu began preparing the sick bay for casualties, Cosimo loaded pistols and rifles, and Knick Nab stayed close to the captain to run orders. As the "Advance" closed, the strange vessel — later identified as "The Green Gull" — was seen to carry no proper cannon, only a pair of small swivel guns, marking it as no warship. Captain Barrows ordered warning fire aimed high, at the sails rather than the hull, and the bow chasers, worked by two gun crews including Werner's, opened up. Early shots went wide or skipped past the hull, but a follow-up struck true: Werner's crew put a shot through the rigging that severed the control line for the ship's mainsail, crippling its ability to maneuver. "The Green Gull" attempted a desperate turn into a side channel but couldn't make it, and as the "Advance" drew alongside with gunports open, the merchantman struck her colours.

The ships were lashed together and First Lieutenant Clugny formally crossed to accept the surrender, asking the merchant captain directly if he yielded his vessel; the captain agreed at once. Marines under Sergeant Vasquez, led across by Mani, rounded up "The Green Gull's" small crew at gunpoint, while four of the enemy sailors slipped over the far side and tried to swim for the islands rather than be taken. Mani, given permission to fire, and the other Marines shot all four dead in the water as they swam. Cosimo crossed with a party of sailors to help secure the ship itself, tracking down and repairing the severed sail control line.

Searching the hold — found to be packed with sacks of rice — Mani and Cosimo heard the sound of trickling water and traced it to the starboard side, where a swollen, waterlogged rice sack was found plugging a crack in the hull, its cause impossible to tell with the sack still lodged in place; freeing the sack to investigate nearly reopened the leak before Third Lieutenant Gunter came down personally to take charge, calling for the ship's carpenter to properly seal the crack with oakum and pitch.

Captain Radulf, master of "The Green Gull," was brought aboard the "Advance" for interrogation; Knick Nab, serving the wine, spilled some in his nervousness. While the interrogation was underway, Cosimo added another beat to the campaign against Jacque: a sound illusion of the prelate's own voice, muttering a crude, out-of-character remark about the captain from the quarterdeck, overheard by three sailors and Second Lieutenant Conrad and deepening the impression that Jacque had begun talking to himself. Radulf claimed to be a simple merchant carrying rice from the North to sell in the South, but Captain Barrows declared the ship and its cargo a prize of war regardless, promising the crew would eventually be treated fairly and released. Back aboard "The Green Gull," Mani searched the captain's low, cramped cabin and turned up logbooks and a small locked chest; the logs suggested the rice had been loaded near the Northern port of Zylos and was bound for a city on the southern coast — an oddity pointing to smuggling or collusion somewhere in Zylos. Second Lieutenant Conrad caught Mani in the cabin and confiscated the logbooks, though Mani insisted on personally carrying them, along with the chest, over to the "Advance's" Quarter Master. Knick Nab, listening at the door of Captain Barrows's cabin, overheard Barrows and his lieutenants discussing the same suspicion — that someone in Zylos was likely colluding with or being paid off by the South — and deciding to route the prize to Port Sardina instead of Zylos, both to avoid tipping off whoever was responsible and because Port Sardina offered better odds of getting dispatches back to the capital.

With time running short before Jacque could see Cosimo shipped off to the capital, the party argued over how to finish him off politically. More elaborate schemes — including planting evidence that Jacque himself intended to burn the ship rather than let it fall into Southern hands — were floated and set aside as too complicated; the party settled on a simpler combination: two forged notes, plus another sound illusion of Jacque muttering to himself. Knick Nab, coached by Cosimo on the wording, drafted two rambling, heretical notes accusing the ship's officers — with the captain named at the top — of straying from the truth of the Two and demanding "purifying fires" as the only cure. One note was slipped into the pile of papers on Jacque's own desk during a moment when his cabin was empty. Getting the second note into his pocket proved harder: Knick Nab's first attempt went into the wrong priest's robes, mistaking Nicolas's hanging robes for Jacque's, and he had to sneak back in to retrieve it before it was discovered. The second, live attempt succeeded only with help: Mani intercepted Jacque with a genuine, unburdening confession about having killed a man for the first time, holding his attention, while Noddy cast Distraction on him at the same moment. Between the two of them, Knick Nab managed to slip one page of the note into Jacque's pocket; the second page he simply left on the floor by the cabin door to be found.

Summoned to the captain's cabin, Knick Nab was pressed by Captain Barrows himself about his friendship with Cosimo and Cosimo's "overly zealous" talk of the Two. Under the weight of the captain's questions, Knick Nab chose to remove his headwear and reveal his elven ears, hoping the gesture would help Cosimo's case. Barrows, badly shaken, called him a monster; Knick Nab countered that the Two's insistence there were only two gods was itself suspicious — the more loudly that claim had to be made, he argued, the more likely it was that others existed. Barrows offered to let the moment simply not have happened, but chose instead to keep the secret, telling Knick Nab that a monster who had saved his life was no monster at all, and that the revelation had only deepened his trust in him. Citing his need to keep his lieutenants aboard the "Advance," and a wish to put some distance between Cosimo and Jacque's scrutiny, Barrows gave temporary command of "The Green Gull" to midshipman Werner — over First Lieutenant Clugny's open skepticism about Werner's inexperience — ordering him to complete repairs, sail her to Port Sardina, and turn her over to the authorities there. To Knick Nab specifically, "because I feel I can trust you," Barrows entrusted two charts of the Channel Islands and a set of sealed dispatches for the capital, to be forwarded on personally or through trusted means once the opportunity arose. Werner requested the same group that had gone ashore with him earlier, plus the most experienced sailor from his gun crew, Salter. In the scramble to get underway, Cosimo pilfered a few basic carpentry tools from a reluctant carpenter's mate, Riu drew extra medical herbs from the ship's surgeon, and Mani, denied a whip by the bosun (who kept sole custody of the ship's whip and cat o'nine tails), settled for taking his pistol instead. As he crossed over, Cosimo told Sergeant Vasquez in passing that Jacque had asked him to fetch a supply of oil and oakum for his cabin — one more invented detail planted to feed the ship's suspicion that the prelate meant to burn the vessel rather than let it fall into enemy hands.

As "The Green Gull" cast off, Jacque burst from his cabin demanding to know what was happening, and ordered the younger priest Nicolas to go with the departing ship to "keep the faith." Still in his heavy robes and carrying his sword, Nicolas leapt for the departing vessel without waiting; Cosimo's telekinesis, Noddy's distraction spell, and Werner's feigned "assistance" combined to throw off his jump, and he slammed into the ship's side and fell into the gap between the two hulls. Noddy called the alarm, and Werner dove in after him, wrestling him up from underwater and swimming him back while others pulled them both aboard with ropes. As the ships drew apart, Cosimo shouted back at Jacque that his blind adherence to dogma had blinded him to the work of the Mother and Father, and Noddy attempted to magically whisper "let him go" in Jacque's ear, to little apparent effect. Jacque, for his part, called across the water for Cosimo to turn himself in at the capital's temple to be judged, and told the shaken, soaked Nicolas to keep faith but not to trust Cosimo.

Aboard their new command, Werner gathered the group privately and admitted that, rank aside, he had never captained a ship before and would need them as partners rather than subordinates; with that settled, the party set up the ship's low aft cabin — formerly Radulf's — as a locked armory and safe room for their weapons, using one of their own padlocks along with the cabin's existing key, surrendered by Radulf, and agreed it would be strictly off-limits to the four southern sailors. Those sailors were paired off with the PCs and Salter rather than left to work as a group, their knives and one pistol confiscated but their personal effects and dignity otherwise respected, while Radulf himself was kept apart from his crew, stationed at the stern near the wheel with Werner. Briefly, the party weighed the temptation of simply keeping the prize for themselves — selling the rice in the South and becoming "rice pirates" — before Werner refused outright, arguing that completing the mission honestly would do more for his family's fortunes than turning outlaw. Salter, as the most experienced sailor aboard, was made boatswain to directly oversee the four southern sailors, who were split into pairs and worked alongside rotating PCs rather than as a single group. The first two days of sailing went badly: with only Werner, Salter, and Noddy possessing any real sailing skill, and neither Werner's navigation nor his leadership up to the task, the ship nearly ran aground more than once and made almost no real progress, while Nicolas spent the time praying uselessly for their safety. Knick Nab tried and failed to charm Radulf into cooperating with vague promises of smuggling contacts. Nicolas separately sought out Cosimo for a serious conversation about his powers, saying that despite witnessing genuine miracles at the highest levels of the church, he had never seen anything like what Cosimo described; Cosimo insisted his abilities came from prayer to the Mother and Father, citing as evidence how the Mother had supposedly hidden the party from the enemy ship's sight during the earlier beach battle. Nicolas remained unconvinced but let the matter rest to "pray on it." By the third day, with progress still hopeless, Werner appealed directly to Radulf, at first offering freedom only to the four crew. Radulf pushed back, arguing that the North's treatment of Southern captives meant servitude for master and crew alike, and held out for his own freedom too — not a recommendation or a share of the profits, but outright release for everyone. Werner ultimately agreed: Radulf's people would sail the ship properly in earnest, and in exchange be given the jolly boat and set free one day's sail short of Port Sardina, on Radulf's word as a gentleman not to cause trouble in the meantime — a promise the party privately debated but chose to honour once given, judging the ship and its cargo more important than the small risk that Radulf was lying. With Radulf now directing the sailing in earnest — relaying his orders through Salter as bosun — the ship's progress improved markedly, though still short of what a full, competent crew could manage, as the session ended.

docs.title: Illusions of Power and a Burning Resolve
Events and Actions
docs.text:
The party continued their voyage aboard "The Green Gull" towards Port Sardina, with Captain Radulf and his crew sailing the vessel under Werner De Rendal's supervision. Two days in, they remained an estimated two days from their destination. Captain Radulf reminded Werner of their agreement: his crew was to be freed one day out from Port Sardina, set adrift in the ship's jolly boat to make for shore on their own. Wary from the start, the party had taken care to keep the southern sailors from bunking together or having too many chances to conspire; watching them now, the crew's diligence and Radulf's evident concern for his men only reinforced the sense that this was simply a merchant trying to save his own skin and his crew's, and that honouring the deal was his best chance of getting them all home safely. Nicolas, the young priest, conducted services; of Radulf's crew, only Bob, the sole one still devout, attended.

Cosimo Cellini Scivio suggested Nicolas keep an all-night vigil, but Nicolas declined, needing rest to bless the crew for their independent voyage; Cosimo volunteered for the watch himself instead. Riu privately asked Nicolas to curse Radulf's crew should they rejoin the Southern forces; Nicolas refused to curse men who had never taken up arms, but agreed to redouble his efforts to win them over, promising to address them all — believers or not — in one last sermon before they departed. Mani, meanwhile, kept up the quiet rapport he had been building with Bob, checking on him daily and bringing him food, and confided to Nicolas his own growing doubts about the Divinity of Two — doubts tangled up with the black stone, the invisible medallions, and the old women the elves had once spoken of. Still turning the question over that night, Mani slipped below decks to quietly renew a private dedication to Mistress Clara back in the Capitol; a ship offers little privacy for such things, but he made do.

The following morning, after a night without incident, Captain Radulf laid out his charts to show how far they had come and gave his final advice for the day: the prevailing currents and winds in this open stretch ran from east to west, meaning they would have to beat southeast against them, but once clear of the Channel Islands proper the winds and currents here were far steadier than anything they had fought through so far, so a straight if slow run should be possible. Nicolas delivered his farewell sermon, urging Radulf's crew to embrace the Divinity of Two — power, success, and life itself came from the Two, he told them, and without their blessing a man's days, and his family's, were numbered — and inviting any who were tempted to question Bob, their one devout shipmate, about what the faith had truly given him. Before their departure, Knick Nab and Cosimo searched "The Green Gull" for sabotage, paying particular attention to the earlier cannon-fire breach in the hull, but found it soundly repaired and no sign of tampering anywhere else. The party returned Radulf's crew's basic kit and clothing from their lockers, then added a sack of rice, fresh water, a cooking pot, and a share of hard tack; Radulf balked at the raw rice as useless until Werner explained it only needed a couple of days' soaking to be edible, and their three cheap knives were handed back last, as the captain boarded the jolly boat. Werner De Rendal controversially decided to keep Captain Radulf's compass despite Riu's objection that it broke faith with an otherwise fair parting; Mani sided with Werner, arguing it was a legitimate spoil of war and that Radulf, within a day's sight of land, hardly needed a compass to get there.

As Radulf's boat departed, Cosimo unleashed a dramatic display of illusion magic: he loudly "cursed" any "heretics" among Radulf's crew who might rejoin the South, conjuring an illusion of a sea creature beneath their boat and a celestial display — sun fading to moon fading to cloud — in the sky above, claiming it was the intervention of the Mother and Father. The spectacle proved almost too convincing. One of Radulf's sailors — not Bob, who had nothing to fear from a curse aimed at heretics — panicked so badly that he nearly capsized the jolly boat, until Captain Radulf knocked him senseless with an oar to restore order. Salter, the carpenter's mate, hid behind Nicolas in fear. Nicolas himself was awestruck, and when Cosimo knelt before him afterward, kissed his ring, and declared himself merely "a vessel" of the Two, Nicolas blessed him outright. Knick Nab, overwhelmed by the divine display, fell to his knees, cried out that the Two truly existed, and tore off his own headband, revealing his long and pointy ears. Only Werner De Rendal noticed, and though he tried to place what he was looking at through what lore he had, he got no further than "abomination." When Knick Nab proved too dazed by religious rapture to cover himself back up, Werner set his own hat on Knick Nab's head to hide the ears and got the ship moving again; Noddy, watching from the crow's nest, saw the whole exchange and needled Knick Nab afterward as the ship's new "Captain Stewart."

"The Green Gull" continued its journey, making good progress under the steadier winds — enough that the party began, for the first time, to feel they knew what they were doing. Later, Noddy spotted land (Port Sardina) and, closer at hand, a warship ahead, flying no flags. Shortly after, he sighted a smaller vessel some distance behind it, seemingly pursuing it. Noddy sent his familiar, the seagull Pocket, ahead for a closer look, but the bird was blown back before it could get near. Suddenly, a violent shudder struck "The Green Gull" — a drastic 180-degree wind shift, now blowing strongly towards the land. Noddy lost his footing on the fighting top's unguarded edge and went over; Riu climbed up to help and became entangled in the rigging himself, twisting his ankle badly before Cosimo climbed up to help bring them both down safely. Riu treated his own ankle with a quick healing rite to keep it from slowing him down.

With the wind now dead against them, the party reefed the sails rather than take on the far larger task of furling them outright, buying time to work out what had happened while staying underway. A closer look with the spyglass showed a fort perched above a narrow bay that commanded the approach to Port Sardina; neither strange ship flew any flag, leaving their allegiance uncertain and raising real doubts about opening fire on what might turn out to be a Northern vessel. Observations then revealed the warship was fully ablaze from bow to stern and heading rapidly towards the port, its deck piled with cargo and a lone figure crouched almost invisibly at the stern — possibly a fire ship meant to run in beneath the fort's guns; the smaller vessel trailing it, its crew visibly bracing the sails taut for speed while two figures at bow and stern gestured over the water, was suspected of magically controlling the wind. Closing the distance would also put "The Green Gull" within range of the fort's own guns, a risk the party weighed alongside everything else. After a tense debate over whether to strike at the smaller ship — the likelier source of the wind magic — or the burning warship bearing down on the port, the party settled on the warship: it offered a fallback, since they could still turn for the smaller ship if boarding failed, whereas committing to the small ship first would give up any chance at the other. They briefly considered heating shot for their swivel guns to spread the warship's fire further, but discarded the idea for want of time and a fire of their own to heat it with, and held shooting out the warship's rudder in reserve as a last resort should boarding fail outright. Mani quoted the "Rules and Regulations of the King's Navy" on the duty to engage, and Riu judged that ramming the warship early enough could still knock it off course before it reached the channel.

Their plan took shape as they closed the distance: Salter would cut the warship's rudder lines and make fast a tow rope to "The Green Gull" to drag the rudder — and the ship's course — off true, while Werner stayed at the helm with him to hold their own vessel in position. Mani, Cosimo, and Knick Nab would board the flaming vessel itself to deal with the figure seen crouching, barely visible, at its stern, and to fight through to the wheel or the anchor if either could still be reached. Nicolas was told to keep watch on the smaller ship and call on whatever divine help he could against it. As "The Green Gull" pulled alongside, the warship became fully engulfed in flames from bow to stern — the heat of it washing over the boarding party even before they set foot aboard — and "The Green Gull" itself began to catch fire from the intensity.

docs.title: NPCs & Creatures
docs.text:
• Captain Radulf: Captain of the captured Southern merchant ship, "The Green Gull". Negotiated for his and his crew's freedom, gave sailing advice to the last, and knocked one of his own men senseless with an oar to avert a capsizing.

  • Nicolas: Young priest of the Divinity of Two, accompanying the party; profoundly shaken by Cosimo's display of power.
  • Salter: Carpenter's mate from the "Advance", assigned to "The Green Gull".
  • Pocket: Noddy's familiar spirit, inhabiting a seagull; sent ahead to scout the pursuing ship but blown back by the sudden wind.
  • Figure on Warship: An unidentified individual seen crouched almost invisibly at the stern of the burning warship, amid piles of cargo on its deck.
  • Crew of Smaller Ship: Crew of the tiller-steered pursuing vessel — two sailors bracing the sails taut for speed, plus figures at the bow and stern gesturing over the water, suspected of controlling the wind.
  • Sea Creature (Illusion): An illusion of a sea troll or sea serpents created by Cosimo.

docs.title: Locations
docs.text:
• The Green Gull: The prize ship under the party's command.
  • Channel Islands' Waters: The general area of travel.
  • Near Port Sardina: A fort perched above a narrow bay commanded the approach to the port; the location of the climactic encounter with the unidentified warships. Closing on the ships would bring "The Green Gull" within possible range of the fort's own guns.

  • The Smaller Pursuing Ship: A much smaller, tiller-steered vessel trailing the warship by several hundred feet, its crew bracing the sails taut for speed while two figures at bow and stern gestured over the water — suspected source of the sudden, unnatural wind.

docs.title: Conflicts
docs.text:
• The Compass Dispute: Werner De Rendal's decision to keep Captain Radulf's compass led to a disagreement with Riu, who argued it broke faith with a fair parting; Mani sided with Werner, calling it a legitimate spoil of war.
  • Cosimo's "Curse": Cosimo's illusory display and "curse" on Captain Radulf's departing crew caused panic on their boat, subdued only when Captain Radulf knocked the panicking sailor unconscious.
  • Near Fall from Crow's Nest: The sudden wind shift caused Noddy to nearly fall from the unguarded fighting top. Riu was injured while assisting, twisting his ankle in the rigging.
  • The Boarding Debate: The party argued over striking the smaller, likely wind-controlling ship or the larger burning warship bearing down on Port Sardina. With neither ship flying a flag — leaving their allegiance uncertain — and the fort's guns within possible range, the party weighed the risk of firing on a potentially friendly vessel before settling on the warship as the option that preserved a fallback.
  • Impending Confrontation: The party prepared to board a burning warship and deal with a smaller, potentially hostile, magic-using vessel. "The Green Gull" began to catch fire.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• The party continued to struggle with advanced sailing but managed a day's travel successfully under Captain Radulf's guidance and later on their own with his advice, learning that the winds and currents beyond the Channel Islands were far steadier than what they had fought through so far.
  • Nicolas demonstrated his oratorical skills but declined to perform curses, choosing persuasion over condemnation.
  • Mani voiced his growing doubts about the Divinity of Two — tangled up with the black stone, the medallions, and the old women the elves had spoken of — while continuing to build a quiet rapport with Bob, the one devout sailor among Radulf's crew.
  • Cosimo's powerful illusion magic was displayed, attributed by him to the Divinity of Two, which deeply impressed Nicolas and other party members; Cosimo knelt before Nicolas afterward and was blessed in turn.
  • Werner De Rendal observed Knick Nab's long and pointy ears after Knick Nab removed his headband in a moment of religious fervor, but could learn nothing more specific despite drawing on what lore he had.
  • The party discussed naval regulations regarding engagement, with Mani quoting from the "Rules and Regulations of the King's Navy."
  • The nature of the wind change was debated, with suspicion falling on the smaller ship engaging in weather/wind magic; Riu judged that ramming the larger ship early enough could still alter its course, and Mani used his knowledge of engineering to confirm that a collision at that size difference could indeed knock the larger ship off its heading before it reached the channel.
  • Strategies were debated for dealing with the fire ship and the smaller vessel, ultimately settling on the fire ship as the option that left open a fallback against the smaller one.
  • The party weighed heating shot for their swivel guns to spread the warship's fire further, but abandoned the idea for lack of time and an onboard fire to heat it with; shooting out the warship's rudder was set aside as a fallback if boarding failed entirely.
  • Mani speculated that an expenditure of magical power this large was unlikely to be an isolated event, suspecting it was tied to something bigger unfolding that day.

docs.title: Trial by Fire: Diverting the Burning Wreck
Events and Actions
docs.text:
The party, aboard the "Green Gull", intercepted a warship heavily ablaze and heading directly towards Port Sardina's fortified harbour. Before committing to a plan, they debated at length how a small crew might actually redirect a much larger vessel under fire and time pressure — forcing the wheel, hauling on the rudder from outside, or dropping anchor were all weighed and found wanting on their own — and settled instead on a multi-pronged boarding effort that could pursue several of these at once. Salter and Nicolas remained on the "Green Gull" to manage it and combat any spreading fires, while Werner De Rendal, Knick Nab, Noddy, Cosimo, Mani, and eventually Riu, undertook the perilous task of boarding the enemy vessel.

The boarding was fraught with danger. As the "Green Gull" closed the distance, an enemy sailor rose into view on the burning ship; for a moment its sails seemed to droop, as though their power had been drained, before he gestured toward the "Green Gull" and spoke words in an unfamiliar tongue, conjuring a hazardous crackling sphere of energy at the "Green Gull's" bowsprit. Noddy doused himself with magically condensed water and cast Distraction on the enemy sailor, rattling his composure, but Mani's rifle shot still went wide, blasting a chunk of railing instead of the man himself. Maintaining Distraction demanded Noddy's constant concentration, doubling the effort of everything else he tried to do for as long as he kept it up.

Knick Nab's first attempt to run up the burning ship's bowsprit ended in a fumble that left him stuck beneath it. Cosimo cast "Blur" on Noddy, who then successfully used his leaping magic to land on the burning ship near the enemy. Mani's first attempt to swing aboard via rope fell short, but a second, fate-favoured attempt saw him swing in and open with a kick to the groin from behind, then follow up with an unarmed blow that drove the wind from the man and left him stunned. Werner, attempting to board from the "Green Gull", was zapped by the energy sphere; the shock wrenched his hand into a claw and tore its tendons, leaving it useless for several minutes of fighting and climbing to come. Cosimo trained the swivel gun on the enemy sailor for cover fire, only belatedly realizing that smoke and flame had obscured his line of sight for several rounds; when he finally fired, the heavy cover the smoke gave the man carried the shot wide. During these events, a drooping length of sail in the "Green Gull's" own rigging slipped down into the flames and caught, and the "Green Gull" began to catch fire in turn.

Onboard the burning warship, Werner, despite his injury, managed to climb aboard but was further burned while navigating the flames. Noddy, seeing him struggling against the heat, reached out and doused him with a second casting of condensed water, and the soaking gave Werner just enough of an edge to push on to the wheel without roasting himself further. He reached the wheel only to find it spinning uselessly, disconnected from the rudder below — he hauled on it anyway in desperation, burning his arm further for nothing. Knick Nab freed himself from beneath the bowsprit and pressed onward. Cosimo also boarded, finding himself in a dangerously hot section of the ship; a quick look around showed him the ship's wheel standing between the main and mizzen masts, wreathed in flame. Noddy tried a Lore spell to identify the magic behind the crackling trap; he confirmed it was definitely a spell but found its nature too foreign to recognize further, then turned to assessing the dire situation, noting the ship was intentionally set to burn — its deck was piled with tinder and loose lumber that had no business being there — and observing the rapidly approaching port. Riu, after initially lashing the wheel of the "Green Gull" to steer it slightly away, later leaped aboard the burning vessel to assist.

Still stunned and now facing the boarders, the enemy sailor tried to flee deeper into the smoke and fire, blundering into the flames twice and burning both legs badly as he went. Knick Nab gave chase, caught him, and ended the fight by throwing him down hard onto the ship's railing, crushing his trachea; the man collapsed, unable to speak, and lay gasping and dying as Knick Nab searched his body.

A desperate, multi-pronged plan was enacted to divert the burning ship: Werner fought his way below deck to the tiller room, which was also on fire, and was joined there by Cosimo; between them they sawed through the tiller's thick restraining ropes with an ordinary dagger, slow and unglamorous work compared to what was happening above. Mani and Knick Nab, after Mani sustained burns while searching, located a boarding axe and began chopping at one of the masts. Riu leaped ahead to the ship's port anchor and began cutting it loose with his own axe; Knick Nab crossed the burning deck with a dagger to help him, narrowly avoiding the flames himself, and together they cut the anchor free. The anchor and its chain plunged into the sea with a rattling roar sharp enough that Knick Nab called out for everyone to brace themselves. Noddy reached the captain's cabin through a window, finding it otherwise stripped bare but for two map cases, which he pocketed. Riu, having finished with the anchor, joined him there and held his legs as Noddy dangled head-down out of the window to work his rope-work magic, sending a length of rope down to the rudder and tying it fast before climbing back up to pass the free end across to the "Green Gull".

As the burning ship closed the final distance in the late afternoon — around four o'clock — alarm bells rang out across Port Sardina's battlements, which now loomed directly overhead; the fort's cannons, caught by surprise, could not depress far enough to fire on a target so close in. The combined efforts succeeded: Werner and Cosimo cut the tiller free and threw it over; Mani and Knick Nab felled the mast, causing drag; and the "Green Gull" pulled on the rudder via the rope. The sudden pull nearly hauled the "Green Gull" into the burning wreck itself, forcing its crew to cut the rope loose once the turn had taken hold. The burning warship veered off course and slammed into a cliff face opposite the fort — no gentle grounding, but a hard impact carrying the wreck's full momentum.

However, the "Green Gull" was now badly on fire and had run aground or was otherwise in severe trouble. The player characters remaining on the burning wreck faced the urgent need to escape: Knick Nab and Mani planned to dive into the water and make their way around the hull, while Noddy and Riu, able to leap clear with their magic, faced no such difficulty.

He conjured a crackling energy trap at the "Green Gull's" bowsprit and fought with two long daggers. Stunned by Mani, he fled through the flames, burning himself badly, before Knick Nab caught him and crushed his trachea against the ship's railing, leaving him dying and unable to speak.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• Before boarding, the party weighed several ways to redirect the fire ship — forcing its wheel, hauling on its rudder from the "Green Gull", or dropping its anchors — and, finding no single option reliable on its own, decided to attempt several of them at once.
  • The party learned that the enemy warship was deliberately set on fire, its deck stacked with tinder and loose lumber rather than the usual gear of a working ship.
  • The ship's wheel was disconnected, and the tiller was secured in place, indicating a deliberate attempt to keep it on a fixed course.
  • Noddy reasoned that if the ship had been rigged as a fire ship, its powder magazine had likely been emptied beforehand so it wouldn't explode before reaching its target.

docs.title: All Hands to the Left: A Fiery Escape and a Tense Arrival
Events and Actions
docs.text:
The session began with the party having successfully diverted an enemy fire ship, driving it to ram the cliffs near Port Sardina rather than run aground — still afloat, still burning, but no longer a threat to the harbor. Their own vessel, the "Green Gull," lay disabled nearby, caught in irons with her sails useless and fire beginning to spread across her rigging. Most of the PCs were still aboard the burning fire ship, with sharks spotted in the waters below.

A coordinated effort, albeit fraught with peril, ensued to abandon the fire ship. Werner De Rendal, trying to climb clear of the flames below decks, was driven back when a burning beam collapsed near him, breaking one of his harpoons and leaving him staggered and badly burned, with both the stairway and the gunports beyond it cut off by fire. Knick Nab and Mani chose to swim, navigating waters where two sharks circled; Mani kept the dispatches dry by clenching them in his teeth as he went. Cosimo also braved the swim after jumping from the fire ship's stern. Noddy used a magical leap to reach the "Green Gull," while Riu, spotting Werner trapped and smoldering at the rail, tossed him the end of a rope and then leapt across himself. Werner went over the side clutching the rope, took a fresh burn to the leg in the process, and swam the rest of the way, arriving aboard the "Green Gull" gravely weakened. The party members were eventually all recovered aboard the "Green Gull." Salter and Nicolas, who had remained on the "Green Gull," successfully extinguished the fires that had spread to their ship.

Once regrouped, the PCs spotted a mysterious spellcaster on the stern of the pursuing southern vessel conjure a large, sparkling magical cloud, roughly twenty feet across, that began drifting toward the "Green Gull." Several PCs attempted musket and cannon shots at the distant figure — Salter fired one of the shots himself, since none of the PCs had a steady enough hand with a gun — but the range, several hundred feet, put the shots hopelessly out of reach. Noddy spent the intervening minute casting Protection on six of his companions, granting each a bonus to resist spells and elemental harm; Nicolas prayed aloud for the Father and Mother's protection as the cloud closed; and Riu invoked his "Staying" ability to push against it. The push split the cloud in two; the halves oozed around the party's ship and dissipated harmlessly by the time they reached the "Green Gull's" former position. With no trained sailors aboard and their rigging damaged, the party abandoned the idea of using sails and instead rowed the ship manually through the gunports in her hull, laboriously working her away from the burning wreck. As they passed beneath the fort's cannon, well within range of its guns, Werner signaled with flags that they were friendly — a prize ship of the Northern Navy — and the fort held its fire. The fire ship itself burned on but did not explode.

A small boat came out to meet the "Green Gull," and a harbor pilot climbed aboard, took the wheel himself, and began barking orders, guiding the ship deeper into Port Sardina's harbor — a long, narrow, steep-sided gash of an inlet crowded with ships moored two and three deep against the wharves. Along the wooden walkways at the base of the cliffs, people were already hauling handcarts of barrels and buckets, bracing for a fire that in the end never reached them. As the pilot took them in, Riu drew on a ritual technique that let him channel power points contributed by his companions to work magical healing on Werner's burns, casting it twice in succession, though the worst of them would still need days to mend. A cheer went up from the shore as they passed. With the danger seemingly behind them, Noddy sent his familiar Pocket aloft to scout south along the direction the fire ship had come from, confirming there was no larger invasion fleet following behind the single vessel that had fled. The pilot brought the "Green Gull" in to a berth beside a row of warehouses, where they were met by a naval officer, a squad of soldiers, and Bertin, the Harbor Master. Werner, as acting captain, presented their prize ship and his orders. Knick Nab revealed he had dispatches for Major Hubert, the fort commander. The party was instructed to assist with unloading the "Green Gull's" cargo of rice and informed that Major Hubert would expect a report.

While Werner and Riu began drafting a report, Noddy discussed two maps he'd found in the fire ship's captain's cabin with Knick Nab: one a detailed map of a major southern port city, the other a map of a large island marked with a "Totem." Knick Nab took possession of both maps. During the unloading, Knick Nab slipped away amid the bustle of the docks to deliver his dispatches to Major Hubert at the fort.

Later, Noddy noticed Knick Nab's absence and also observed four barrels — clearly not part of the "Green Gull's" cargo — had been added to the pile of unloaded rice in the warehouse. Mani's inquiry to Bertin about the barrels was brushed off. Suspecting smuggling, the party pried open two of the four barrels by main strength and confirmed both held wine, though they found no clue as to why it had been added to their haul, beyond perhaps padding the value of their prize. A search for Knick Nab led Mani to a beggar named Pew at the edge of the market, who, for a couple of coppers, confirmed he'd seen Knick Nab heading toward the fort; Mani paid him further and asked him to keep watch over the "Green Gull" for anything else that might be added or removed. The party finished unloading and used the last of their time aboard to search the now-empty hold for anything they might have missed, finding nothing beyond the old, already-repaired damage from when they'd first seized the ship. Their own tally of rice bags came up two short of Bertin's official count of 386 — a discrepancy Werner chose not to mention when he wrote up his report.

Meanwhile, Knick Nab made his way up to the fort alone, charming his way past a young guard at the outer checkpoint by insisting Captain Barrows had ordered him to deliver the dispatches in person. At the fort's inner gate, when another guard tried to take the dispatches from him to carry in himself, Knick Nab again pressed his insistence on personal delivery, leaning on his luck to make it stick, before being left to wait under guard for some ten minutes. Hubert took the sealed dispatches, locked most of them away in his desk, and set aside one page — addressed to him and marked "to be conveyed in person by Knick Nab." He mentioned that he had known Captain Barrows since the two served together as midshipmen decades earlier, working their way up through the ranks aboard the same ships, and that an old injury had since ended his own service at sea and confined him to shore duty commanding the fort. He then questioned Knick Nab closely about his and his companions' service to Captain Barrows, pressing him on how they had come to intervene at Barrows's court martial with no evidence beyond Knick Nab's word, and on their uncanny run of "fortune." Sensing Hubert's real interest lay in something called "the Three," Knick Nab invoked his boon to press the point — causing Hubert to blurt the term aloud before catching himself. Knick Nab, seizing the opening, revealed his own physical anomaly, declaring himself no follower of "the Two" and voicing curiosity about "the Three" instead. Hubert recoiled at first, briefly calling him a mutant who should be destroyed by the strictures of the Two, then caught himself, insisting he meant no harm and that he cared nothing for the Two's rules in this matter, though he admitted he needed a wiser friend's counsel before discussing "the Three" any further. Major Hubert, intrigued and cautious, decided to detain Knick Nab at the fort for further discussion and sent a squad down to the docks to fetch the rest of the crew.

As the day wound toward evening, a squad of soldiers arrived at the dockside asking for Werner and his crew; Nicolas, who had spent the day sitting apart in quiet meditation rather than helping unload, rose without prompting and fell in alongside the others, tacitly counting himself part of the crew. The party finished unloading, gathered their belongings — including Knick Nab's sea chest and a spare length of rope, half-joking that it might be needed to keep him from disappearing again — and were escorted up through the town, across the fort's open "killing field," and inside, their foot lockers following behind on a cart. Along the way they passed Pew again; Mani tipped him another coin and introduced himself properly as Manuel, and the escorting squad, noticing the party's injuries, slowed its pace to accommodate them. Werner, Riu, Mani, and Cosimo were each interviewed individually by Major Hubert. Werner recounted spotting the theft that led him to speak up for Barrows at the court martial, and downplayed the party's role in fending off the vessel that had chased the "Advance"; excused afterward, he had a fort doctor treat his burns with salves and bandages while he waited on the others. Riu confirmed the unnatural winds that had driven the ships toward the harbor and described watching the enemy spellcaster through a spyglass, crediting Werner and Knick Nab with the initiative shown at Barrows's court martial. Mani spoke of being "Bound by Fate," recounting how he and his companions had each independently been guided into each other's paths by "strange old women" — describing how he had been thrown in jail after an illegal duel and shared a cell with Werner, the two of them escaping together in a cart driven by a mysterious old woman, the same sort of old woman, he said, who had steered another of his companions into the group as well — and asked that the group be kept together in their future Navy postings, a request Hubert said he would try to honor; shown the dispatch envelope, he also noticed three faint parallel lines scored into its back. Cosimo, shown the same envelope, likewise noticed the lines, recognized them as similar to markings on the Gildenhome Map, and urged Hubert to send ships in pursuit of the fleeing southern vessel while there was still time; Hubert brushed off his questions about the enemy's "confounding powers," hinting only that there was more at stake than a ship's boy could be told. Pressed on how he knew of such matters, Cosimo spoke of his years as an altar boy in the church and rumors of great riches beyond the western seas, marking himself in Hubert's eyes as a devout follower of the Two. Hubert questioned each of them about their "fortune" and motivations but revealed nothing further of his own suspicions in return. All were informed they would be quartered at the fort for a few days. Nicolas was also seen being escorted to Hubert's office as the others were led away to their rooms.

docs.title: Conflicts
docs.text:
• The party contended with fire, the sea, and sharks while escaping the burning fire ship.
  • Werner De Rendal sustained multiple burn injuries and a broken harpoon while fighting clear of the collapsing decks, and was gravely weakened by the time he was hauled aboard the "Green Gull."
  • The party's vessel, the "Green Gull," faced a magical "sparkling cloud" attack from the southern enemy ship, which they successfully countered.
  • The party's attempts to strike back at the retreating southern vessel and its spellcaster with musket and cannon fire fell short at extreme range.
  • Knick Nab underwent a tense interrogation with Major Hubert, culminating in the revelation of his physical secret — which Hubert first met with a flash of hostility, briefly calling him a mutant who should be destroyed, before catching himself and offering reassurance.
  • Werner, Riu, Mani, and Cosimo were individually interviewed by Major Hubert.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• The southern forces possess magical abilities, including wind manipulation and offensive magic (the "sparkling cloud").
  • A scouting flight by Noddy's familiar Pocket confirmed no larger southern fleet was following the single vessel that fled — this attack was not the vanguard of a bigger invasion.
  • Major Hubert served with Captain Barrows as a midshipman decades ago and rose through the ranks alongside him, before an old injury forced him into shore duty commanding the fort at Port Sardina.
  • Major Hubert is keenly interested in the PCs' string of "fortunate" successes and their connection to Captain Barrows.
  • Major Hubert is investigating a concept or group known as "the Three," and suspects the PCs might be involved or know something. Knick Nab confirmed Hubert's interest and expressed his own.
  • Major Hubert intends to consult a friend or colleague more versed in these mysteries before discussing "the Three" with the party any further.
  • Knick Nab revealed his physical anomaly to Major Hubert, distancing himself from "the Two."

docs.title: Revelations and Invitations in Port Sardina
Events and Actions
docs.text:
Following their arrival in Port Sardina and the securing of their prize ship, the "Green Gull," the party (Werner De Rendal, Mani, Cosimo, Riu, and Noddy) found themselves quartered in the local fort under the authority of Major Hubert. Werner, concerned about four suspicious barrels of wine added to the prize ship's cargo, penned a note to Major Hubert, sealed it with his family crest, and had a guard posted outside his door deliver it that same night.

The next morning, they were summoned by Major Hubert's aide, Smithers, only to learn that Knick Nab had departed Port Sardina on a ship, arranged by Major Hubert himself. His absence reopened an old frustration — Knick Nab had slipped off alone several times before — and the party debated it before agreeing, at Mani's urging, to always tell one another where they were going from now on. They also wondered whether Knick Nab felt the same unsettling pull they experienced when separated from one another, a sensation several of them had noticed before, and whether his apparent unconcern about it might mean something. Hubert explained Knick Nab felt threatened by an upcoming conversation and feared persecution.

The remaining party members then met with Major Hubert. He discussed Knick Nab's departure, admitting that he had recently learned something troubling about Knick Nab which he had not yet had the chance to raise with him directly, though he stopped short of calling it grounds for persecution. He listened to the party's belief that fate bound them together, and confirmed their desire to continue operating as a group. Hubert informed them that Captain Barrows of the "Advance" was not headed to Port Sardina, revealing that the two had served together as junior officers years before and remained close friends — which explained his familiarity with, and gratitude for, the party's role in clearing Barrows' name at his court-martial. He also spoke about the strategic importance of Port Sardina as a frontline port against the South and acknowledged the South's mysterious wind-commanding powers, noting that the ability appeared to be wielded by more than one person acting in concert — one aboard the fire ship itself and another on the ship trailing it — which he considered significant enough to report back to the capital. Werner described the "glowing blob" burn he received, which Hubert noted did not seem like a power of The Two; Cosimo, pressed on his own familiarity with the ways of the Two as a former altar boy, said he would consult the local clergy and sought library access to better understand it. Hubert expressed skepticism about the quality of the local Governor's library for researching such matters and warned against openly discussing these unusual powers to avoid panic. Werner inquired if Major Hubert had heard of "Gildenhome," but Hubert had no knowledge of it. Werner also asked about his grandfather, a renowned sailor famed for his skill in the harsh conditions of the North (Hubert specifically demurred at calling him an explorer); Hubert knew the name — his own father had trained under the man — and confirmed the expedition had likely passed through the Channel Islands, which had long served as the natural westernmost launching point for voyages further out, before it vanished without a trace, adding that any surviving records would most likely be found in the admiralty's libraries in The Capitol.

Later, the party met Governor Frederick Francisco, who effusively thanked them for saving the port. He invited them to a fete at his mansion the following night. During this meeting, Mani requested replacement clothing and a fencing master, Cosimo asked for library access and to study under a prelate, Riu also requested library access, and Werner asked for clothing, lodging, and training in Gunnery and navigation. The Governor took a personal interest in Werner's prospects, noting he was already a midshipman and pressing Major Hubert to give him preference toward an eventual officer's commission aboard a ship of the line. The Governor and Major Hubert made various promises to accommodate these requests. Noddy and his seagull, Pocket, were also invited to the fete.

Major Hubert informed them they could collect their prize money from Harbor Master Bertin. He also mentioned an opportunity to join an initial force to secure the island where the Southern incursion was found, though it would depart in a few days, leaving little recovery time for Werner.

The party collected their prize money from Harbor Master Bertin, who had them confirm the manifest of rice bags brought off the "Green Gull" (the tally came out two bags in their favor) before paying out 10 silver pieces each; as they had done before, they set aside a silver apiece for their shared coffers, bringing the common fund to roughly 50 silver. Salter, who had accompanied the prize crew, was found already deep in his cups; they gave him only part of his share on the spot, promising the rest once he had sobered up, and he wandered off to drink further. They then dressed as well as their means allowed — mended uniforms and borrowed finery, with Noddy fashioning Pocket a scarf ascot for the occasion — and, weapons limited to swords and daggers worn as ornamentation, made their way up to the Governor's mansion for the fete. Announced to the room as the crew of the "Green Gull" and met with polite applause, they were introduced by their proper titles, including Werner as the third son of Duke Kasimir De Rendal and Noddy, to his amusement, as "Mr. Noddy" — a marked step up from what the guards had been calling him. At the party, they were greeted by the Governor and his wife, Daliah. They were surprised to meet Randolph the Chronicler, who was also a guest and revealed to be the fencing master the Governor had mentioned — Randolph noted he had already shown Mani a thing or two back in the Capital and agreed to continue his training now. Randolph explained he was en route to The Academy — an island itself well south of the mainland, once considered neutral ground but no longer safe to reach casually now that flags of truce go unrespected — and had come this way as a safer, if less direct, route than the larger port that lay along the main channel through the islands.

The fete's guests were mostly naval officers and their ladies, with a smaller number of merchants and their families in attendance and two Priests of the Two present, quietly listening to the evening's conversation. Mani spoke with ship captains about future naval appointments — one thanked him personally, noting his ship had been moored nearest the harbor mouth and would have taken the worst of the blaze — and recounted a carefully edited version of their adventures to Randolph, crediting a decoy cannon and a well-placed shot for turning back their pursuers, mentioning the fight on the island and the prisoners they took, and noting that one prisoner had escaped with help from an old Islander woman and been pursued to a neighboring island — all while omitting the pygmies, the saboteur, the secretive nature of the camp they'd found, and anything mystical; Randolph took it all down in his notebook without pressing for more. Their edited story drew different interest from different quarters — naval officers pressed for tactical detail, merchants asked after cargo and tonnage — but nothing in the room suggested anyone was listening more closely than simple curiosity would explain; Mani, still watchful for the odd three-line mark he had once glimpsed on the back of an envelope, thanked Randolph again for the gift of his main gauche, then checked Randolph's notebook margins and his own reflection in a mirror for it, but found nothing. Cosimo performed impressive magic tricks, particularly for the Governor's daughter, Suzette, and his wife, Daliah, producing coins from behind ears and from beneath a lady's petticoat before making a turtle dove vanish into the rafters; Suzette begged for an encore, and Cosimo answered with a whispered invitation to a private viewing another time. Mani, drawing on his own merchant family background, engaged with merchants and learned about local trade, which included crops like rice and, significantly, slaves; the merchants noted that in more peaceful times traders of any nation could do business here, though these days only Northern ships called.

Noddy observed a "black sparkling mist" during Cosimo's greatest working yet — the elaborate, many-layered miracle that had driven off the southern crew — seemingly drawn from the party's Medallions towards Cosimo; both he and Cosimo agreed it resembled the sparkling auras they had seen around people while chewing Bitterroot. Mani noted that the Medallions seemed to affect him differently than the others: he alone had ever managed to remove someone else's, he had once felt strangely drawn to the great black stone on the island, and yet whenever he tried to take off his own he found himself inexplicably distracted before he could finish. The party discussed the nature of fate, the possibility of powers beyond The Two, Knick Nab's potentially Elven heritage (due to his pointed ears, similar to A'Wood the smuggler), and the mysterious properties of their Medallions, recalling that A'Wood himself had once spoken of his people's belief in fate being guided by figures he described only as "two old women." They resolved to keep faith with whatever force had bound them together and press on, while agreeing Cosimo should be more discreet about performing miracles openly, and that keeping Nicolas close as a friendly, if not fully-informed, ear among the clergy might help shield them from more dogmatic churchmen.

Before the night was out, the party also weighed how to spend the next two years while Werner recovered and their next posting was arranged. They agreed unanimously to stay together and sketched out individual pursuits to fold into that time: Riu hoped to return to the Capital to study under Mistress Clara and Mistress Mary and to visit The Academy for further research, while Noddy meant to press on with his navigation training and his bond with Pocket. They floated adopting occasional group "hijinks" — infiltration, minor mischief, and the odd card game — as a standing pastime, discussed hiring street urchins to retrieve further Medallions from the skeleton in the Capital since only Mani seemed able to remove one safely, and considered selling some of their stored Bitterroot through Mani's merchant contacts before agreeing to preserve it for further study instead.
