docs.title: Revelations, Departures, and a Priest's Crisis in Port Sardina
Events and Actions
docs.text:
The party (Werner De Rendal, Mani, Cosimo, and Noddy) attended a fête at the Governor's Mansion in Port Sardina, hosted by Governor Frederick Francisco. Knick Nab was not present. Amid a crowd of military officers, merchants, and their spouses, the four were recognised and celebrated as the heroes who had turned back the burning ship threatening the port — an unusual degree of attention for a group of teenagers who would not otherwise have been invited.

Earlier that evening, Knick Nab — still shaken over the recent discovery of his pointed ears and fearful of what it might mean for him — had slipped away to see Major Hubert alone. Hubert was sympathetic, assured Knick Nab he personally held no grudge against him for his nature, but agreed it was a dangerous thing to have discovered, and offered him an immediate way out: passage that very night aboard the Amada, a small, fast Northern Navy cutter that ran solo missions deep into Southern waters, commanded by the renowned Captain Otto "Cut Close" De Guzman. Hubert wrote out orders on the spot and sent Knick Nab off as the ship's new "captain's mate." Making his way alone across town toward the cutter's berth on the cliffside, Knick Nab was startled in the dark by Pew, the beggar the party had questioned earlier while searching for him, who got around on a crutch for want of a leg and an arm. Recognising the description he'd been given, Pew directed him back toward the Governor's party where the others had gone and, for a silver piece, agreed to deliver a note to them and deny ever having seen him. Knick Nab then made his way down to the berth, where an armed watchman challenged him, checked Hubert's letter, and sent for the captain. Aboard the Amada, the crew scrambled into a sudden flurry of activity to make ready for a night departure, and Knick Nab was brought before Captain De Guzman.

At the Governor's party, the group spoke with Governor Francisco, his wife Daliah, and their daughter Suzette. Noddy delighted the Governor by putting his seagull Pocket through tricks — including, when asked if the bird could perform, having it simply shrug, which the Governor found uproariously funny once he caught the joke. Cosimo mingled among the nobility, placing friendly small-stakes wagers without invoking any of his skills. He tried his charm on Daliah with no success, then spent much of the evening courting Suzette's circle of friends instead, setting his sights on winning her over properly.

Randolph the Chronicler, also unexpectedly in attendance, revealed that his business in the Capitol was concluded and that he intended to travel on to The Academy to deliver the information he had gathered, having judged Port Sardina the safest place to arrange appropriately escorted transport. Mani asked to accompany him and continue his training; Randolph agreed readily, explaining that The Academy is a neutral, information-driven institution — it does not simply admit visitors, but its scholars will pay for information of value, and personal requests for knowledge require compensation in kind. He admitted he rarely visits the place himself, since its real work of gathering, verifying, and cataloguing knowledge falls to the historians and researchers who live there, and noted that those formally admitted to study are usually recruited much younger than Mani, though nothing stopped him from continuing Mani's training personally. Mani hinted that he and his friends possessed information that might be worth a great deal to The Academy, and Randolph, intrigued, agreed that if Mani could help expedite his own passage there it would be well repaid — admitting that being the one to deliver such a find would also do his own standing with his superiors no harm, though he cautioned that arranging safe transport could easily take weeks or months regardless. He gave Mani a written address for a training session at 6 a.m. the next morning.

Mani then sought out Governor Francisco and, playing on the Governor's evident fondness for the party, secured his support in arranging safe passage for Randolph and the party to travel together — the Governor promising to put in a good word with Major Hubert, and even offering to have a song composed in Mani's honour. Learning the party had nowhere to stay, the Governor recommended (after briefly reconsidering the propriety of the suggestion) The Treasure Hunt, a gambling house and inn he'd heard was popular with sailors. Mani also spoke with Major Hubert directly; Hubert, noting that Werner's burns looked considerably worse than anyone else's, confirmed he was already looking into arranging Randolph's transport, agreed to defer the party's naval duties until their injuries had healed (since their own ship, the Advance, was not expected back soon), and said he would see about having them assigned to whatever vessel carried Randolph. He brought Mani and Randolph together to confirm the arrangement, mentioning in passing that Randolph would introduce them to a contact of his at The Academy named Engerrand — a name Mani carefully noted despite having no context for it. When Mani asked whether The Treasure Hunt would be a suitable place to lodge, Hubert confirmed it was, warning only that it would run pricier than most rooms in town, if more comfortable for it.

With Major Hubert's permission, the party spent one further night in their quarters at the Fort. The next day, Werner, Mani, Cosimo, and Noddy went looking for lodgings and found Pew begging in the main square again; tossing a few coppers into his hat, they asked for directions to The Treasure Hunt, which he gave, and, in the same breath, produced Knick Nab's sealed note. The note turned out to be a rambling, guilt-stricken poem in which Knick Nab likened himself to a "scrawny chicken" too faint-hearted to fight alongside them, explained his fear that the recent "Abomination" incident might draw unwanted attention to his pointed features, affirmed his loyalty to the group, and confirmed he had taken a Medallion with him. Amused and touched in equal measure, the party voted — half in jest — to adopt "Chicken Legs" as Knick Nab's new nickname.

Following Pew's directions, the party found The Treasure Hunt — a large, lively gambling house, tavern, and inn near the harbour, owned by a man named Rees. Looking for breakfast, they instead discovered Nicolas the priest slumped unconscious across the bar, dead drunk. They quietly got him to their table rather than cause a scene, and once he came around, dazedly asking whether Mani — "the one with the gifts" — was among them, Mani drew on their earlier bond from saving Nicolas from the water and coaxed him into talking. Dishevelled, unshaven, and barely out of his teens, Nicolas confessed he had spent the last two days praying and drinking in roughly equal measure, overwhelmed by what he had witnessed of the party's connection to the Mother and the Father; he explained that even Jacque, the priest who had trained him, had never shown him anything like it, and he wept, unable to explain how the party achieved what he could not. Mani reassured him and convinced him to resume conducting services — Nicolas agreed to hold them on the beach for the local sailors, with Mani assisting once a week for as long as his own duties allowed, so long as Nicolas himself was sober. The party also weighed having Nicolas quietly vouch for them as the heroes of the port to help their standing at the inn, but with his face still down on the table decided he was in no state for it and set the idea aside for another time.

Cosimo separately raised the idea of attempting a ritual casting of a healing spell, Concussion Mastery, to treat Werner's ongoing burns from the previous session's fire-ship battle, despite not having learned the spell himself yet; it was established that such a ritual was possible in principle, though risky, given the wide gap between the spell's level and Cosimo's own. Two of Werner's burns were mild enough that the spell could plausibly reach them, but his worst burn remained too severe regardless, and the party set the idea aside as not worth the risk for now, with an eye to revisiting it once Cosimo had advanced further. The party then arranged rooms at The Treasure Hunt for the month, with meals included, and closed out the session discussing their next steps: the trip to The Academy, a return visit to the island with the black stone, and a longer-term plan to call again on Burlyman at the Crow's Nest in the Capitol to see about acquiring another Medallion, reasoning that a crew of their own would eventually need more than one. They also weighed how much of what they knew they were willing to share along the way, and worked out a proposed system of rotating leadership: Noddy pressed for the group to lean into a scouting and reconnaissance role — stealth, surveillance, and information-gathering — for whatever ship or navy they ended up serving, while the others agreed that whoever held the lead at a given moment, whether for nautical matters, dealings with the Church, or some other specialty, should be backed by the rest, with some sign — a hat or small token was floated — to mark who currently held it.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• Knick Nab has left Port Sardina on the Amada, a special military cutter bound for Southern territory, commanded by Captain Otto "Cut Close" De Guzman. He took a Medallion with him and left a note explaining his fears, referencing the "Abomination" incident and the "cause of the three." Reading the note, the party puzzled over what "the three" refers to, not having pursued the topic when the Major had raised it in an earlier session.
  • Randolph the Chronicler is also in Port Sardina and intends to travel to The Academy. He is willing for the party to accompany him and continue Mani's training.
  • The Academy is a neutral institution that takes no sides; its scholars live on gifts given in exchange for keeping people informed of world affairs, and it does not simply admit visitors — new information can itself be a form of compensation for a personal request.
  • Governor Francisco and Major Hubert are supportive of the party accompanying Randolph to The Academy. Major Hubert also agreed to defer the party's naval duties until their injuries heal, since their own ship is not expected back soon. An individual named Engerrand at The Academy was mentioned as a contact Randolph would introduce them to.
  • Nicolas is deeply troubled by the party's spiritual manifestations, having never seen anything like it even from Jacque, the priest who trained him.
  • The party discussed future objectives, including travel to The Academy, a return visit to the island with the black stone, and — further out — a trip back to the Capitol to see Burlyman about acquiring another Medallion, on the reasoning that a crew of their own would eventually need more than one.
  • The party weighed how much to reveal to The Academy: the existence of the indestructible black stone seemed safe and interesting enough to share, without disclosing its connection to their Medallions or its apparent power; the pygmies' survival was already public knowledge and no risk to mention; but the Bitter Root's unusual properties and the map fragment referencing "Gildenhome" — so far shown only to the elf A'Wood — were to stay undisclosed as leverage for later.
  • The party proposed a rotating command structure based on expertise — Mani taking the lead in nautical and tactical matters, Cosimo taking the lead in dealings with the Church or the Divinity — with an understanding that whoever held the lead in the moment would be backed by the others without argument, half-joking that they'd treat insubordination the way a ship's captain would once they had a crew of their own. Noddy separately pushed for the group to embrace a scouting and reconnaissance role — stealth, surveillance, and information-gathering — for whatever ship or navy they end up serving with.
  • "The Treasure Hunt" is a local establishment for lodging, food, and entertainment, owned by a man named Rees.
  • Picking up on a phrase from Knick Nab's note ("reform the chain, the Medallion"), the party half-jokingly settled on "The Medallion" as the name for the ship they intend to one day own, complete with a battle gong in place of a ship's bell.

docs.title: Reunion in Port Sardina, Commission for the West
Events and Actions
docs.text:
The session commenced after a two-year time skip, with the Player Characters (PCs) now at level 2. A summary of the intervening two years was provided: Werner De Rendal recovered from burns at The Treasure Hunt in Port Sardina over the better part of a month, tended by army surgeons, though the ordeal cost him his third harpoon, hard to replace this far south. The party (sans Knick Nab) took rooms at The Treasure Hunt rather than shipboard hammocks and made it their home port for the two years: Cosimo gambled away his money at the dice tables (managing at one point to draw Suzette, the Governor's daughter, away from a fancier gathering to join him), while Riu introduced Noddy to the mysteries of bathing, to Pocket's evident delight. Mani trained daily in the yard under Randolph the Chronicler, working toward his ambition of becoming the finest swordsman of the age. Meanwhile, Knick Nab had slipped away the night before the Governor's fete to serve aboard the cutter "Amada" under Captain Otto "Cut Close" De Guzman, a Northern navigator of some renown who had handpicked a notably tight-lipped crew. Knick Nab suffered a month of worsening fatigue and pain he passed off as seasickness before it subsided — his fellow sailors read his frailty as weakness even as they came to respect his evident determination — after which he was taken under De Guzman's wing and taught naval tactics and navigation as an unofficial captain's mate. The "Amada" ranged south and to the western edge of the Channel Islands hunting the South's "wind blowers," escaping several perilous engagements through good fortune and the crew's skill, but never managed to capture or identify one. The ship avoided proper ports almost entirely, resupplying ashore on quiet beaches or river mouths and once being careened in some out-of-the-way spot to scrape barnacles and shipworm from her hull and keep her speed; Knick Nab also noted, without ever learning why, that the "Amada" carried no member of the Divinity of Two among her crew, unlike every other Northern vessel.

The rest of the party served aboard a supply ship, revisiting the old Southern encampment site — now occupied as a Northern watch post — and sneaking up to Blackstone Peak by night, where they found the excavated strange rock had been quietly covered over again and found nothing new. New Admiralty orders soon curtailed further excursions: with the South proving to command the seas, the Northern fleet was pulled back to a purely defensive picket along the Channel Islands, and the party spent most of the two years on routine, unglamorous shipboard duty under Major Hubert's careful stewardship, gaining experience but no prize money. Their one notable diversion came escorting a supply run to The Capitol, where they slipped ashore through the smuggling tunnel to visit Burlyman at The Crow's Nest; the tunnel itself showed no sign of discovery, though the carts within had plainly been moved since their last passage. Burlyman was glad to see the passage still secret, but his news was grimmer: Randolph had since left the tavern, and soon after the party's own departure, Priests of the Divinity of Two had stormed the tavern searching for the PCs. Mistress Mary and Mistress Clara had confronted the priests over the intrusion, and in the resulting argument were marched off by the priests and soldiers, accompanied by a young red-headed man — implied to be Stick Stab — and had not been seen since. While there, the party checked the hidden chamber beneath the cellar and confirmed no fresh Medallion had appeared on the skeleton. A long debate followed over whether to bring in an outsider — a kidnapped street urchin, or more palatably a paid companion — to test whether an unclaimed Medallion would manifest for someone new; Riu argued the experiment would settle whether the Medallions were meant only for the six of them, and pledged not to place one on anyone without the group's consent, but the party voted the idea down as needlessly dangerous and unkind to whoever was chosen. Cosimo left letters for Mistress Clara with Burlyman before they departed. Throughout the two years, the party's own priest Nicolas remained ashore at Port Sardina rather than being posted to a ship, preaching most mornings on the beach; sober, he proved a fiery and popular speaker, though he was often found in his cups.

The PCs then shared their level 2 advancements before the narrative returned to the present. The party (Werner, Riu, Noddy, Cosimo, Mani) arrived back in Port Sardina aboard an unremarkable merchant escort, finding the harbour emptier than they remembered — much of the fleet was out on patrol — and berthing beside a small, unfamiliar cutter that Werner recognized, after a round of perception checks, as the "Amada," the ship Knick Nab had vanished aboard two years before. Granted two days' shore leave, Mani marched straight for the "Amada's" gangplank to ask after their friend; the officer of the watch there, a mustachioed figure in a striped hat later introduced as Lieutenant Blaque, could only tell him Knick Nab had already gone ashore. The party made for The Treasure Hunt instead, their one known haunt in the port, where Knick Nab — visibly filled out and changed after two years at sea, and oddly winded by nothing more than his first beer — was found nursing a drink. Mani seized him from behind in a bear hug, hauled him up out of his seat, and kissed him on each cheek before buying a round; the group pressed Knick Nab for an explanation of his sudden departure, and he admitted only that he'd taken something he felt had been taken from him first, and had never discussed it with anyone else aboard the "Amada." Mani declared, half-drunkenly, that the group was bound together by fate regardless of what else Knick Nab might be, and that he belonged with them; Nicolas, also in the tavern and in his cups as usual, overheard Mani call Knick Nab's absence "an insult against God" and corrected him without looking up — "gods," plural. The reunion soured when talk turned to Mary and Clara: Knick Nab confirmed, when asked, that the red-headed man from Burlyman's account had indeed been Stick Stab, and Mani grew seriously and uncharacteristically angry at the priests responsible and began drinking harder, vowing that when the party next reached them, the Divinity would surrender the two women, whether or not it was ever put to a vote.

Before the party could act further, Lieutenant Blaque of the "Amada" arrived at the tavern with word that Major Hubert wanted to see all of them at once. They marched to the fort, where Hubert received them warmly and asked each in turn how their service had gone: Werner effused implausibly about the glories of shipboard life, Knick Nab admitted with rare candor that he'd mostly lived in a hole, Riu allowed that two years of surgical and gunnery training had left him eager to test his skills against a real enemy vessel, and Noddy described a middling two years in the grey between open war and peace. Beneath the pleasantries, Hubert's evident frustration soon showed: two years of purely defensive war against the South's mysterious wind-manipulating "wind blowers" had yielded nothing but attrition, and his orders gave him no room to pursue the answers he believed the war needed. The party pressed the case that they, uniquely, had already fought and killed one of the wind blowers by fire during the Fire Ship incident, and could do more good hunting answers than standing picket. Unable to issue the order himself without disobeying his own superiors, Hubert instead proposed the party take the "Amada," under De Guzman's command, on an unofficial westward voyage of discovery — chasing the same trail that swallowed Captain Maynard and, later, Captain Barrows. The party agreed unanimously to go west, settling first on Port Zylos as a waypoint to gather intelligence and contacts before striking further out. Randolph the Chronicler was summoned — again asking Hubert for passage to the Academy, and again being refused — and agreed to join the expedition as cartographer and chronicler, on condition that anything he learned would ultimately be shared with the Academy; he was firm that he served neither North nor South, only the Academy's mission of gathering and disseminating knowledge to all, and mentioned that the Academy holds an annual "Dispersal" — its next falling on the first day of spring — at which newly gathered knowledge is shared with legitimate scholars from anywhere in the world. Asked for a letter of introduction that would let the party call on the Academy's resources in the future, he declined to write one for now, though he did not rule it out once he had seen more of what they could offer. The party also debated, and voted against, bringing their own priest Nicolas along, judging the risk and awkwardness of a Divinity priest aboard the "Amada" to outweigh any benefit — though they arranged to take a set of priest's robes in case Cosimo needed to bluff the role.

Left largely to themselves afterward, the party debated how best to use their new latitude. Riu and Noddy raised the idea of infiltrating a Southern port directly — slipping in undetected to seize a wind blower off the street or out of a tavern — arguing that the party's unconventional talents, from Pocket's aerial scouting to Cosimo's illusions, might succeed where two years of the "Amada" chasing wind blowers at sea had not; Knick Nab confirmed that in all that time, none of the "Amada's" actions against the South had ever been on land. The debate ran long, but the party ultimately voted to hold course for the West, tabling a direct raid on a Southern port as an option to fall back on later, and agreeing that Port Zylos would double as a first chance to look into Southern activity before they struck further out. In the same discussion, they asked Major Hubert to check Port Sardina's records for any sign that A'Wood — the elf of uncertain loyalties they had once helped escape north through the smuggling tunnel — had passed through.

Hubert saw to outfitting the expedition: twelve gold pieces for supplies, access to naval stores for blunderbusses, pistols, shot, powder, and grenades, smoke bombs to be made from wet gunpowder, priest's robes and whatever spare Southern-looking uniforms could be found — Hubert cautioned that ordinary sailors' clothing hardly differs between North and South, so anything useful would have to be officer-grade, the South's short navy-blue jackets rather than the North's royal blue. By the meeting's end he had also located an Islander slave fluent in Common and Islander to serve as translator. He confirmed rune paper — needed for Riu's plan to inscribe spells into runes readable by non-casters — was not available anywhere in Port Sardina and would have to be sought in Port Zylos. Werner argued for and secured a letter of authority instructing De Guzman, or any other officials the party might encounter, to extend them full cooperation — insurance against being redirected by a larger Northern flotilla or left without standing should De Guzman himself be killed — though his separate bid for an actual lieutenancy was turned down as beyond Hubert's authority to grant; he settled instead for the promotion to Senior Midshipman he learned of in the same sitting.

Captain De Guzman himself arrived to meet the party: a flamboyantly dressed, deliberately unmilitary figure in a purple doublet and broad-brimmed hat. He agreed to the mission but was frank about the strain nine additional passengers and their cargo would put on a ship built for a much smaller crew. On hearing Werner's name, De Guzman recognized the De Rendal house at once — House De Guzman, he explained, was itself a lesser Northern family, sworn to naval service rather than trade, and had long fallen under the De Rendals' sway — and revealed that his own grandfather and Werner's grandfather had learned to sail together in their youth, both taking to whaling and trade rather than the military — it was De Guzman's own father who later broke with that tradition for a naval career; De Guzman's grandfather himself vanished around the time De Guzman was born, and he had heard old, half-credible family tales of a single ship that once returned from a similar westward expedition, only to sink shortly after. Werner had no answers to offer, but the connection plainly meant something to both of them. De Guzman explained that the "Amada" ran with only two officers — himself and Lieutenant Blaque — everyone else being a sailor experienced enough to need no supervision; Werner would technically outrank the crew as midshipman but agreed to serve purely as an observer and defer to them, an arrangement De Guzman welcomed. The ship carried no dedicated medic or carpenter, De Guzman said, since every hand did a bit of everything, and he was glad to have Riu's healing skill aboard regardless. The party decided against a detour to a nearby island to gather more of a valuable root they had a small stock of, agreeing to sail directly for Port Zylos. De Guzman asked that the party not reveal their true destination to his crew until the ship was underway. Before departure, the party also wondered whether holy water could be turned against the wind blowers' magic; learning that the Church does bless water for such purposes, they added a stock of it to their purchases, meaning to bless their shot with it. The party arranged for a keg of decent rum and a small bag of spices to be brought aboard as a goodwill gift for De Guzman's crew, and the "Amada" was set to depart for Port Zylos on the morning tide.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• The PCs are now level 2 and detailed their new abilities and skills.
  • The war against the South continues, with the North maintaining a defensive posture. The South utilizes "wind blowers," individuals capable of manipulating weather or ship speed.
  • Mistress Mary and Clara were taken from The Crow's Nest by Priests of the Divinity of Two, who were searching for the PCs, nearly two years prior. Stick Stab was confirmed as the red-headed man who led the priests there.
  • Major Hubert commissioned the party for an unofficial mission: to travel west aboard the "Amada" with Captain De Guzman to seek answers regarding the South's power and the missing Captain Maynard/Barrows.
  • The expedition will include the six PCs, Randolph the Chronicler, Salter, and an Islander slave translator.
  • The first destination is Port Zylos.
  • Randolph the Chronicler's condition for joining is that all information gathered will be shared with The Academy; he answers to neither North nor South, only to the Academy's mission of gathering and disseminating knowledge to all. The Academy holds an annual "Dispersal," its next due the first day of spring, at which newly gathered knowledge is shared with legitimate scholars from anywhere in the world.
  • The party discussed the potential risks of the Chronicler learning their secrets.
  • Captain De Guzman is a skilled but reckless captain; his ship, the "Amada," is fast and maneuverable but lightly armed and will be crowded with the new additions.
  • Major Hubert will investigate why the Divinity of Two is searching for the PCs; the party judged it too risky to send Nicolas to ask around the capital himself, since it might reveal that they remain in the area. Pocket's own recollection, when questioned, confirmed that two priests and a red-headed man had been watching the docks the day the party first sailed away from the capital, suggesting the Divinity's interest in them predates the later raid on The Crow's Nest, though its cause is still unknown.
  • Captain De Guzman's grandfather and Werner's grandfather learned to sail together in their youth, both taking to whaling and trade; it was De Guzman's own father who broke with that tradition for a naval career. House De Guzman is itself a lesser Northern family, sworn to naval service rather than trade, and has long fallen under the De Rendals' sway. De Guzman's grandfather disappeared around the time De Guzman was born, and family legend tells of a single ship that once returned from a similar westward expedition, only to sink shortly after.
  • Rune paper, needed for Riu's plan to inscribe spells as runes readable by non-casters, is unavailable in Port Sardina and will have to be sought in Port Zylos.
  • Distinct regional accents exist across the world, including a recognizable Southern accent; Salter, a Southerner serving with the party, is one example.
  • Holy water can be purchased from the Church and used to bless items, including shot, against supernatural threats such as the wind blowers.

docs.title: Zylos Bound: Preparations, Portents, and a Mysterious Past
Events and Actions
docs.text:
The session opened with a recap of items owed to the party from the previous session. The party was introduced to Batu Batu, a short, stocky, and slightly plump Islander (slave) who would serve as cook aboard the "Amada." His family had a long history of service in the Northern Navy's kitchens and mess halls, and though he had been posted on ships before, this was his first time as sole cook aboard a vessel this small. The rest of the "Amada"'s crew was further detailed, including Captain De Guzman, Lieutenant Blaque, sailors Tom, Ben, and Mark, and Salter (formerly of the "Advance"), a Southerner and competent sailor brought aboard in part for his skill with woodcraft and carpentry.

The party received a letter of authorization from Major Hubert intended to secure passage and support; Knick Nab alone noticed Hubert subtly marking it with three small lines before handing it over. Hubert also gave them their contact in the port of Zylos: Lieutenant Dardell.

There was a detailed description of the "Amada": a fast, agile single-masted cutter with a single deck, a movable bowsprit that swings out to carry an enormous spread of sail once clear of port, a broad beam for stability, and a shallow keel. She carries six 10-pounder cannons plus two swivel guns, kept lashed along the sides on deck rather than stowed below, since there is no lower gun deck; when not needed, her boats were sometimes towed astern rather than stowed, trading a little speed for extra working room on deck. Duties on the "Amada" were assigned: Noddy as the chief top man (lookout), Mani in charge of the guns, Riu as the ship's doctor, Werner responsible for rope maintenance, and Cosimo designated as a marine for boarding actions. With the party, Salter, Batu Batu, and Randolph the Chronicler all coming aboard, the crew — previously about ten hands — roughly doubled, which Captain De Guzman expected would put real pressure on the ship's space and stores. The existing crew was visibly wary of so many new hands joining at once, though the mood stayed short of any real hostility; Knick Nab, already a known quantity from his prior two years aboard, settled back in immediately, while the others had to earn their place. Mani wasted no time doing so, taking it upon himself to inventory the ship's small arms, cleaning and sharpening every pistol and sword in the armory without being asked.

The PCs acquired various equipment from the armory: Werner obtained a rifle with shot, a keg of powder, and three slightly mismatched harpoons; Noddy got a crate of 12 smoke bombs; and Mani an extra pistol. Riu was assured access to healing herbs — bleeding relief, concussion relief, and stun relief among them. Cosimo acquired a lute. Knick Nab arranged for Batu Batu to prepare a special first meal to boost crew morale, and Riu separately spent some off-duty time getting to know Batu Batu personally.

A concerning development was Knick Nab's recurrence of the severe fatigue and pain he had endured at the start of his previous two-year voyage. The illness resurfaced upon his return to port this time, showing it is not tied to being away from his companions.

The "Amada" set sail for Zylos, a voyage expected to take eight days but completed in six thanks to her speed. It was largely uneventful; they passed one other ship, a Northern vessel, without incident, flying Northern flags throughout since the "Amada" also carries other colours for use elsewhere. Upon approaching Zylos, Knick Nab, having been there before, described it as a large, mountainous, U-shaped island oriented north-south, long and skinny, whose bulk shelters the rest of the Channel Islands from the open sea; the port (Newport) lies on its sheltered eastern side, inside a broad, naturally sheltered bay.

They arrived at Zylos on an overcast, drizzling day and found the anchorage crowded with heavy naval ships off a port town of a few thousand people. Captain De Guzman anchored well offshore, and the party (Werner, Mani, Knick Nab, Noddy, Cosimo) decided to take a boat ashore, accompanied by Salter, who would guard the boat. They were hailed and briefly challenged by a Northern patrol ship but allowed to proceed once Lieutenant Blaque exchanged words with it. The PCs dressed to avoid drawing attention as official military personnel: Werner passed as a Northern sailor in his sealskin cloak with his harpoons, Mani presented as a well-dressed but unaffiliated civilian, and Cosimo and Noddy dressed as common sailors, with Noddy's seagull familiar drawing no particular notice.

Ashore, a harbor official directed them to leave their boat at the dock for a copper coin, and Salter found a spot in a nearby tavern to watch it while he dried off. The party located the Tattered Sail, a tavern near the Admiralty building, to inquire about Lieutenant Dardell, having found the tavern reserved for officers only closed to them since none of the party could properly claim that status. Over bowls of the tavern's famous "endless stew," Werner, posing as Dardell's nephew, learned from the innkeeper that Dardell was likely at Admiralty House, had a good reputation, and had suffered some kind of accident years ago that had left him seriously impaired; the innkeeper had only known him as a boy, before it happened. Knick Nab observed the tavern patrons, noting some "working ladies" but nothing overtly suspicious.

At Admiralty House, sentries challenged the party at the door; Werner claimed a personal, family matter and named Major Hubert, and a message was carried inside. They were initially told that Lieutenant Dardell was busy and to return tomorrow. Cosimo — presenting himself to the aide as one "Emanuel Alonso," an assumed name — then produced their letter of authorization from Major Hubert. After a wait of about ten minutes, the aide returned it, saying Lieutenant Dardell would see them that same evening at 6 PM (eight bells) instead.

With five hours to wait, they returned to the tavern. An elderly man entered, known locally as "Steel Hand" for the old, scratched artificial hand he wore in place of his own, fastened by straps riveted to the metal that ran up beneath his sleeve. A serving girl (the barkeep's daughter) immediately attended to him, seeming to expect him and fussing over his comfort due to the weather. Mani asked the barkeep about him and learned that "Steel Hand" had been a fixture of the tavern for years, had no means to pay for his own keep, and was looked after out of respect for his service to the country; he drank only Grog. Mani, after a rebuffed attempt to charm information from some "working ladies," bought the old man (whose name they later learned was Ish) a cup of Grog. Upon hearing the name "De Rendal" (Werner's family name), Steel Hand's demeanor softened, and he called Werner's grandfather a "fine man." He then began to sing a Northern whaling shanty, which Werner recognized and joined in, though Steel Hand also added a verse unfamiliar to Werner.

In a fragmented conversation, punctuated by moments of lucidity and confusion, Steel Hand claimed Captain De Rendal "rode the sea serpent and was never seen again" from "The King's Ship." He described the sea serpents making "terrible sounds, the shrieking" before they come and pull their victims down into the depths. He also mentioned that "the cleric came back" from that fateful voyage. When asked about his own lost hand, he attributed it to a sea serpent, and when pressed on where it happened, he confirmed it was far to the west — his garbled answer seemed to suggest it happened in the very same event that took Captain De Rendal, implying Steel Hand himself had been aboard the King's Ship when it met its fate, though he could not or would not clarify further. Prompted by the party, he revealed an old, faded blue-black tattoo of a serpent on his arm, which coiled up and disappeared under his sleeve. He also spoke of "terrible winds" that "came and they came and they came" when asked about how ships survived sailing west before the Great Change. Pressed by Knick Nab for anything more specific — a heading, a landmark, anything that might place where the King's Ship went down — Ish could only trace a vague gesture in the air. Knick Nab, drawing on his own experience of the North, knew that sailors tell all manner of sea serpent tales, and that most are just that — stories grown from ordinary whale encounters, especially when a chased whale gets away and the disappointed whalers claim a "serpent" took it instead.

Prompted by all this, Werner told the others what he knew of his grandfather's fate: Captain De Rendal had been one of several captains chosen by the King to lead a large, multi-ship expedition west before the Great Change, selected for his renowned skill as a sailor. The expedition vanished; only a single ship ever limped back, and it sank in terrible condition within sight of the De Rendal family's castle, in water too deep for young Werner to reach when he tried diving for it as a boy. No one had ever explained why the King ordered the voyage in the first place.

The party was escorted through Admiralty House and met with Lieutenant Dardell, who stood only with visible difficulty as they entered. Werner introduced himself formally as Senior Midshipman Werner De Rendal, and Cosimo — still using his assumed name — as a Marine private, before the party laid out their mission: to sail west and learn how the South was working its wind magic. Dardell warned he could spare only a few minutes. He knew nothing of the West himself, but confirmed that both Captain Maynard and Captain Burrows had passed through Zylos years ago; Burrows, more recently, had stopped to resupply and was believed to have visited Old Port before heading further west. Old Port, on the western side of the island, was destroyed by waves during the Great Change; Dardell described the Change itself as a sudden and total upheaval in the weather, not a gradual worsening, and said Zylos's exposed western coast — where Old Port stood, fully open to the sea — bore the brunt of it while the rest of the Channel Islands were spared by the island's shelter. He mentioned rumors of past smuggling there, though he believed the blockade had curtailed most of it, and knew little else about the place. He also raised a lead of his own: a ship called the "Green Gold," which had passed through the Channel Islands about two years prior heavily loaded with rice and crewed by Southerners, though he couldn't confirm whether it had ever actually come through Zylos, and thought it might have come from one of the other Channel Islands instead.

Lt. Dardell showed them a map of Zylos: a mountainous, crescent-shaped island marked with a lighthouse at each tip and scattered small fishing villages, but no roads. He agreed to search the archives for any charts of the West. Pressed about the risk of Southern spies in Zylos, he said he was more concerned about ships leaving the port carrying information out than about ships arriving, and had heard nothing of specific southern agents within the Admiralty itself; at the party's request, he agreed to keep note of the names of any ships that left Zylos over the following days, in case they proved useful later. He promised discretion about the party's visit, given the sensitivity implied by their letter.

Returning to the tavern, the party asked Steel Hand about Old Port. He recalled that the King's Ship had stopped there because "the cleric and the censure" (a Divinity of Two inquisitor) needed to go ashore, and that the pair rejoined the ship before it sailed on to its final, fateful voyage.

The party returned to the "Amada." Cosimo, using his engineering knowledge, judged Newport too recent to be an old settlement, though he guessed a smaller settlement may have stood on the site before it was built up. They discussed how to reach Old Port with Captain De Guzman, who advised against taking the "Amada" there directly — the waters around Old Port are treacherous and would put his ship at real risk — and suggested instead sailing north along the eastern coast to find a landing point, then attempting an overland crossing of roughly twelve miles. The Chronicler, when consulted, had little specific information about Old Port beyond confirming its abandonment after the Great Change, but thought a church had likely stood there, since any settlement of its age would have one; asked to clarify, he pointed out an actual Divinity of Two church nearby, distinguished by its two spires, as the kind of building he meant.

The session concluded with the "Amada" sailing north along Zylos's eastern coast, passing a few small settlements along the way. They identified a small fishing village of three or four buildings as the most promising overland crossing point to Old Port. Mindful that questions about Old Port asked openly back in Newport could reach the wrong ears, the party had deliberately avoided pressing anyone else in port about it once they'd learned what they needed from Dardell and Ish. The party discussed their approach for the days ahead: pack several days' worth of food, weapons, and coin; try to recruit a local guide, possibly with the help of a bottle of good drink as a gift; approach Old Port under cover of darkness if conditions allowed for stealth, and otherwise pose as smugglers scouting the ruined port for business, a story consistent with its reputation. They also planned to have Captain De Guzman keep the "Amada" watching nearby once they went ashore, ready to intercept any boat that tried to slip away from Old Port and warn others of their presence. They reasoned that whatever had once been valuable at Old Port had likely long since been picked over, but that information — about the cleric, the censure, and Captain Burrows's visit — might not have been, and resolved to search the ruined church there first.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• The party received a letter of authorization from Major Hubert, which bore three subtle, deliberately made lines.
  • Their primary contact in Zylos is Lieutenant Dardell, who has difficulty standing.
  • The "Amada" is a very fast and agile single-decked ship armed with six 10-pounder cannons and two swivel guns, kept lashed on deck since there is no lower gun deck; specific duties were assigned to each PC.
  • Knick Nab's recurring illness is not linked to separation from his companions, as it returned while he was with them in port.
  • The immediate mission is to go to Zylos, contact Lt. Dardell, and then investigate Old Port.
  • Old Port on Zylos was destroyed by waves during the Great Change. Captain Burrows visited Old Port before his last voyage west, and Captain Maynard also passed through Zylos years ago.
  • "Steel Hand" (Ish) recounted that Werner's grandfather, Captain De Rendal, sailed on "The King's Ship" and "rode the sea serpent and was never seen again." He also stated, "the cleric came back" from this voyage.
  • Captain De Rendal was one of several captains chosen by the King to lead a large, multi-ship expedition west before the Great Change; the fleet vanished, and only one ship limped back before sinking within sight of the De Rendal family's castle.
  • A "censure" (an inquisitor of the Divinity of Two) and a cleric went ashore at Old Port from "The King's Ship" and rejoined it before it sailed on to its final voyage.
  • "Steel Hand" has a prominent serpent tattoo on his arm.
  • "Steel Hand" (Ish) lost his own hand far to the west; his fragmented answer suggested it happened in the same event that took Captain De Rendal, implying he was aboard "The King's Ship" when it met its fate.
  • Lieutenant Dardell described the Great Change as a sudden, total upheaval in the weather rather than a gradual worsening, and said Zylos's exposed western coast — where Old Port stood — bore the brunt of it while the rest of the Channel Islands were sheltered by the island itself.
  • A ship called the "Green Gold," crewed by Southerners and heavily loaded with rice, passed through the Channel Islands about two years ago; Lieutenant Dardell could not confirm whether it had called at Zylos itself.
  • Lieutenant Dardell will search the Zylos Admiralty archives for any maps or records pertaining to lands west of the Channel Islands, and agreed to note the names of any ships leaving Zylos over the following days.
  • The party discussed various strategies for approaching Old Port, considering overland travel from the eastern side of Zylos versus a direct sea approach; they settled on landing overland and having the "Amada" stand by to intercept anyone who might try to slip away from Old Port and raise the alarm.
  • The "Amada"'s crew, previously about ten hands, roughly doubled with the party, Salter, Batu Batu, and Randolph the Chronicler aboard — a change Captain De Guzman expects will strain the ship's space and stores. The existing crew was wary but not hostile toward the newcomers; Knick Nab, already known from his prior two years aboard, fit back in immediately.
  • Northern sailors' talk of sea serpents is, by Knick Nab's reckoning, mostly just talk — many such tales trace back to ordinary whale encounters, particularly when a chased whale escapes and disappointed whalers blame a "serpent" instead.

docs.title: Events and Actions
docs.text:
The party, accompanied by Salter and Batu Batu, disembarked from the "Amada" at a small fishing village on Zylos to begin their overland journey to Old Port, a landing party of eight ferried ashore in the ship's boat; two sailors rowed them in and returned it to the ship, with a semaphore signal arranged to recall it and a fallback rendezvous off the coast at dawn on the fourth day. At the village, Knowles's Islander crew, though presented as fishermen mending nets and coiling rope, kept muskets casually within reach as the party approached. They spoke with Freeman Knowles, a freed Islander running the settlement whose polished speech struck the party as unusual — enough that they privately wondered if he had once served as an agent of the South. Knowles confirmed the path to Old Port, warned that the place was abandoned and might attract undesirables like smugglers, and — after eyeing their rifles — remarked that they looked capable of handling whatever the road might throw at them, "except maybe that sickly one." He also pointed them to a clean, safe spring roughly five hours down the trail and, in exchange for the bottle of rum they left with him as thanks, wished them well on their journey.

The trek involved crossing varied terrain. Knick Nab's recurring illness flared up, causing significant fatigue; at the spring, he began chewing on a piece of medicinal root, which brought temporary relief. Some hours further along the trail, Werner realized the party was being followed; Noddy sent Pocket, his seagull familiar, to investigate and confirmed it was only a young Islander girl. When Knick Nab offered her a silver piece — after she had first refused a proffered water skin — she took the coin, spoke a single word in Islander, and ran off; Batu Batu translated the word as a request for something sweet, leading the party to guess she was after cane sugar, a trade good associated with the islands.

As dusk fell short of Old Port, the party made camp for the night in a sheltered, wooded hollow. By nightfall the medicinal root's effect had worn off, and Knick Nab's fatigue and discomfort returned. Noddy spotted a distant glow along the coast, like a giant fire or a lighthouse, too far off to identify. That evening, Cosimo cast "Item Feel" on his Medallion, learning its purpose is "Detection." The next morning was clear and bright, and the party continued toward Old Port.

Approaching Old Port, the party debated whether to sneak up on the watchtower or simply approach in the open, a question Knick Nab settled — after chewing another dose of medicinal root to steady himself — by stepping straight out onto the road; the rest followed, walking up openly. Watching through Pocket, Noddy saw the sentry duck out of sight, then a warning shot cracked out and the man was spotted fleeing through the tower's base door and down the path toward the town, presumably to alert whoever else was there. Investigating the tower afterward, they found only a few basic supplies left behind — a water skin, a haunch of roast meat, and a spent, still-smoking musket — evidence the sentry had been camped there a while.

Scrambling for cover from the shot, several of the party stumbled through a field of low stone slabs hidden in the undergrowth near the tower; Mani took a closer look and identified it as an old graveyard. He felt drawn to one grave, inscribed "Chronicler Willem" — the same unusual pull he recalled feeling toward the black stone on Totem Isle two years before. Upon excavating it with Salter's trenching tool, helped by Knick Nab and Batu Batu, they found skeletal remains, the rotted remnants of a wooden coffin, and a small, sharp shard of black, sparkly stone; Riu checked it over for anything hazardous before Mani pocketed it. Noddy attuned to the shard and confirmed it held real power, though a subsequent attempt by Cosimo to channel that power did not succeed. Batu Batu pointed out a copper, beak-shaped button fixed to another grave's footstone; examining it, the party identified it as a plague marker, and many graves from the year KS3 22 were found similarly marked, including possibly Chronicler Willem's, though his marker may simply have fallen away.

Before entering the ruined town, the party agreed on a cover story to use if confronted: rather than reveal their naval mission, they would claim to be searching the church for information about Werner's grandfather, who had passed through decades earlier on the ill-fated voyage that preceded the Great Change, taking care not to emphasize his noble blood for fear of being held for ransom. They then moved toward the main ruins of Old Port, identifying a large, dilapidated church carved into the cliff face — the only structure still standing amid the wreckage — with one of its two towers collapsed entirely; recalling that a similar cliffside church in the Capital had concealed extensive dungeons beneath it, they made straight for it. Using his illusion magic, Cosimo concealed their approach in stages, casting a series of illusory domes to mask their advance from two watching guards — one on the church's balcony, another crouched behind rubble below it — while Pocket scouted ahead. Cosimo also wrapped the party in a Sphere of Silence to muffle their footsteps as they crept up a makeshift staircase toward the church. Near the top, as Cosimo poked his head through the last illusory dome, he came face to face with a third guard hidden just beneath the stairs, who spotted him in the same instant.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• Freeman Knowles confirmed the path to Old Port and described it as abandoned, potentially attracting undesirable people like smugglers, and of no current tactical value; his polished manner struck the party as unusual for an Islander in his position. He explained that a freed Islander is customarily known as "Freeman" followed by the name of whoever freed him — Knowles's own name meant nothing to the party.
  • Cosimo's Medallion has the purpose of "Detection."
  • The graves at Old Port's cemetery are laid out in the fashion of the Divinity of Two, with a headstone marking birth and a footstone marking death. Mani identified the recurring "KS3" inscription as referring to the reign of King Sebastian III, dating many of the graves to around forty years ago — consistent with the timing of the Great Change.
  • Noting how many graves shared the same death year, the party debated whether the cemetery held one mass-casualty event or two — plague, and possibly something else, such as an execution — and resolved to dig up further graves and examine Chronicler Willem's remains more closely on their way back through.
  • The black stone shard found in Chronicler Willem's grave is similar in appearance to the material of the Totem on Totem Isle, emanates a sense of power, and was confirmed by Noddy's Attunement to hold real power, though Cosimo could not yet draw on it.
  • The party discussed whether Knick Nab's worsening illness might be tied to the Medallions and his two years' separation from the group, noting that previous separations of half a day or so had never produced anything close to this reaction.
  • Riu's knowledge of medicine turned up how plague is handled aboard Northern ships: the sick are isolated and the vessel barred from port until it's clear who will live, the dead are collected by masked handlers wary of dangerous fumes, and their graves are marked as a standing warning not to disturb them — cold comfort for a party that had just finished digging one up. Those who had directly handled Chronicler Willem's remains (Mani, Knick Nab, Salter, and Batu Batu) took the news better than most, reasoning that a forty-year-old plague victim was unlikely to still be contagious.
  • The party settled on a cover story for Old Port: that they were searching the church for information about Werner's grandfather, who had stopped there decades earlier before his fatal voyage west, while agreeing to downplay his noble blood so as not to invite a ransom demand.
  • The party strategized their approach to the watchtower and, later, the ruined church.

docs.title: Deserters, Diplomacy, and Discovery at the Ruined Church
Events and Actions
docs.text:
The party investigated a ruined church on Zylos, seeking information related to Captain Barrows' past visit and the activities of a cleric and censure from two decades prior. Noddy scaled a tree outside the church and launched himself twenty feet into the air to land on its balcony — a feat as spectacular as the time he'd leapt from one ship's crow's nest to another — while Riu, more subtly, levitated up beside him, giving the party eyes on the interior. From ground level, Knick Nab called into the darkness, pointing out that the deserters had opened fire on the party first, declaring the party blessed by the Powers, and demanding the occupants come out with their hands up or be killed, backing the ultimatum with a mix of charm and intimidation. His charm proved unexpectedly potent: several of the men inside became his instant, devoted fans, while one took such an irrational dislike to him that he counted the rogue as an enemy, complicating the negotiation that followed. Asked afterward whether he'd called on the power of the Two to aid the performance, Cosimo could only admit, still faintly astonished, that he hadn't — whatever had swayed them so completely wasn't his doing.

Three deserters—Big Red, Tibalt, and Perkin—emerged, claiming their ship was wrecked about a month ago. During the initial encounter, one of their companions, Smith, had his kneecap shattered by the party, and another unnamed deserter suffered a broken arm. The party split the three apart to question them individually while Cosimo took charge of Smith, disarming him and assessing the wound; Riu later attended to the man with the broken arm, spending roughly an hour splinting and setting the bone. Cosimo also cast Shadow to slip along the shattered upper wall and peer down into the ruin unseen, spotting the deserters' lean-to camp with its fire pit and goat carcass and the rope-strung chasm beyond, confirming no one else was hiding among the wreckage before reporting back to Noddy. Riu determined Smith's leg injury was too severe to treat effectively in the field — amputation was possible, but his survival afterward would depend on facilities the party could not provide. Mani, troubled by the outcome, raised the grim possibility of easing Smith's suffering rather than leaving him to a slow death, though the party ultimately left the matter unresolved. Big Red, uneasy about what might happen to him and his companions, asked whether cooperating would earn them leniency from the Navy; the others scoffed, reminding him there was no hope of that, but Mani told him not to worry about it, and instead advised the group to present themselves at Old Port later claiming their ship had simply been lost at sea, promising to leave behind some rum and their weapons when the party departed.

Guided by Cosimo's knowledge of church layouts — the customary division between public worship space and private clergy quarters, with twin altars dedicated to the Mother and the Father — the party searched the ruins for a hidden passage. The deserters' camp, a lean-to made from a propped sailcloth alongside a campfire and a part-eaten goat carcass, stood against a section of wall that turned out to be nothing more than ordinary rubble from the church's collapsed towers, ruling out one hypothesis. A thorough search of the public area found no hidden markings; Mani, hoping to sense something of what lay ahead, held out his Medallion — once felt drawn to the great black stone atop Blackstone Peak — but felt nothing from it. The search did reveal that the two altars could be moved. Pushing them in unison exposed two levers beneath, one of which had been smashed and was unusable. Activating the working lever triggered a mechanism that collapsed a roughly sixty-foot section of wall in a cloud of dust and stone shards, unveiling a previously hidden, dark passage. The collapse also swept away the old rope bridge spanning a deep chasm in the church floor — a chasm that, judging by the delayed splash of falling debris, descends hundreds of feet to the sea below. Batu Batu, hearing the crash from outside, rushed up anxiously to check on the party before being reassured that all was well.

To access the new passage, Noddy leapt across the roughly ten-to-fifteen-foot gap, carrying a rope and anchoring its far end. Riu cast night vision on himself, then tied the same rope to his own waist and levitated down into the chasm, descending about thirty-five feet — the full length of rope available — to check the rock face for any passage that might have been split open when the chasm formed, finding none, before levitating across to join Noddy. With not enough rope left to safely harness everyone, and the passage beyond clearly dark, the rest of the party readied a half-empty lantern and improvised torches from tarp and cord. Drawing on rope-work he called literally his profession, Cosimo rigged the crossing by looping their remaining line back and forth around an anchor point to weave a rough platform, laying one scavenged ladder across it as a deck and lashing the second up as a handrail, with Noddy's eighteen-foot whip serving as an improvised lifeline for whoever crossed. Mani went first and crossed cleanly; Knick Nab followed, slipped, and fell some ten feet before smacking into the wall, left dangling above the void until the whip fastened to him let the party haul him up and across, battered but unhurt. Cosimo crossed last with ease. Batu Batu and Salter, left in charge of the deserters, remained on the near side throughout.

Upon entering the revealed private chambers of the clergy, the party found badly deteriorated papers and book remnants — moldy, waterlogged, and largely disintegrated — which they carefully collected in hopes they held the information they'd come for. They gathered everything else of note in the room too, reasoning that nothing there had been touched in decades.

  • Tibalt: A deserter encountered at the ruined church.
  • Perkin: A deserter encountered at the ruined church. Separated from the others for questioning after showing visible unease at the mention of southern wind witches, which he called "the enemy" and "the mystery" — though he denied any personal encounter with one.

docs.title: Conflicts
docs.text:
• An armed confrontation at the church entrance — begun when Smith, stationed on the balcony, opened fire on the party first — left two deserters seriously wounded: Smith's kneecap shattered by gunfire, another's arm broken.
  • Tense, drawn-out negotiations with the three surviving, conscious deserters (Big Red, Tibalt, and Perkin), complicated by Knick Nab's charm-induced reputation among them and by open distrust among the deserters themselves over whether the Navy would show any of them leniency.
  • Knick Nab slipped and fell while crossing the makeshift bridge over the chasm, left dangling above the void until Noddy's whip — fastened to him as a safety line — allowed the party to haul him back up.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• The group of five deserters (Big Red, Tibalt, Perkin, Smith, and one unnamed) have been at the ruined church for approximately one month following a shipwreck. They are not aligned with the South.
  • The deserters possessed no information regarding Captain Barrows' visit two years prior or the cleric and censure from twenty years ago.
  • The deserters confirmed the collapsed crack was the only known way in or out of the ruin; none of them had crossed the chasm or explored beyond it, though Big Red admitted to having looked down without investigating further.
  • Cosimo shared insights on typical church architecture, specifically the distinction between public and private areas, which aided the party's search.
  • The chasm within the church descends hundreds of feet to the sea. Cosimo reasoned that a natural chasm would have wrecked the surrounding structure, while a deliberately built one would have had the structure built around it — since neither quite fit what they saw, its true origin remains unknown.
  • The party discussed the ethics of their actions towards the deserters and the feasibility of providing medical aid. Riu concluded that Smith's leg injury was likely fatal without advanced medical intervention, and Mani raised the possibility of easing his suffering rather than leaving him to die slowly.
  • The party discovered that mechanisms within the church (e.g., a secret door) could be activated by levers concealed in the altars.
  • Mani informed one of the deserters that the party had previously killed a "southern wind witch." Perkin's reaction suggested the wind witches are viewed as a real, if rarely discussed, threat among common sailors.
  • The party confirmed that slaves are permitted to handle weapons in at least some circumstances, informing their decision to arm Batu Batu with a musket to help guard the prisoners.

  • A lantern with a small amount of oil remaining, found in the ruins and used alongside improvised torches (tarp and cord) to light the darker areas.
  • The party temporarily secured weapons from the deserters:
    • Three muskets (one of which was on the balcony).
    • At least two pistols.
    • A cutlass.
    • Several knives.
    • Small quantities of gunpowder and shot from each deserter.

docs.text:

  • Riu spent roughly an hour providing medical attention to the deserter with the broken arm.
  • The original makeshift rope bridge across the chasm was destroyed.
  • The party agreed to leave behind several bottles of rum and most of the deserters' weapons and gunpowder when they eventually departed.

docs.title: Echoes from a Doomed Voyage: Relics, Writings, and Revelations
Events and Actions
docs.text:
The party continued their exploration of the ruined temple in Old Port, Zylos. After dealing with a group of deserters in the previous session, they had crossed the chasm where the bridge had collapsed and reached the temple's private quarters, finding a collection of old, damaged writings there. A search for valuables yielded 11 silver pieces and, more significantly, a finely crafted épée — a +20 AP, -1 size rapier with the bearing of a holy sword — which Cosimo found and gave to Mani.

Noddy dispatched his seagull familiar, Pocket, to scout the surroundings while the search continued. Pocket surveyed the clifftop around the temple and the collapsed port below, finding little of note beyond a small boat grounded on the rocks. The party then decided to leave the deserters — Big Red, Tibalt, and Perkin — behind. Mani gave them food and booze and told them to claim they had been shipwrecked if anyone asked, assuring Big Red that he did not consider them deserters and that if he ever commanded a ship of his own, he would remember men who had proven loyal.

Concerned about plague exposure from Chronicler Willem's grave, disturbed earlier in the investigation, Riu cast a "Cure Disease" ritual on the entire party as a precaution — eight castings in all. It succeeded on everyone but Knick Nab. The party then re-excavated Willem's grave — Riu working alongside Salter and Batu Batu, the "Amada"'s cook, who had helped dig it up the first time — and, examining the remains with Mani's assistance, concluded that Willem had been stabbed in the back, not killed by plague as his headstone claimed. Searching further for anyone of note, they found a second grave from the same year, also marked as a plague victim, belonging to a "Peter De Rendal" — Werner's own grandfather. Excavating it turned up no obvious wound, but also no trace of any personal effects, which struck Werner as strange for a man of his station. While he searched, Cosimo, genuinely devout, quietly said a prayer for the dead man's soul, since Werner was too absorbed in the discovery to pause for one himself. Once the examination was finished, the party reburied Peter, and Cosimo spoke a short blessing over the grave asking the two to watch over his rest. Rather than carry the bones home immediately, Werner took a rubbing of the headstone and carefully noted the grave's exact location for a later return.

With their business at the graveyard finished, the party marched back across the island to the anchorage, camping overnight at the same spot they had used on the way in without incident. They signaled their ship from the shore near the fishing village and were ferried out, taking on fresh fish and water before setting sail.

Riu then set about salvaging and deciphering the fragmented writings recovered from the temple, and the party spent a long while puzzling over the cryptic, damaged pages together. The fragments spoke of a "Maelstrom" that could not be passed without the aid of a "heretic," and of "De Rendal's forecast" — which they slowly realized referred to Werner's own grandfather. Other pieces described a "totem" covered in scratches that gave off wisps of light whenever struck, the "sacrifice of Bayar" to end an unspecified heresy that "Grantos" had first described, and "Sebastian's insistence" that the expedition accept an unnamed outsider, presumably the heretic. One passage told of an "Affliction," resembling a plague, that spread among the crew after they returned with a captive guarded by "the I'hand" — evidently a rank rather than a name — possibly a native from the West; the author of the writings confessed to suffering the same affliction and doubted he would live to finish his account. A final fragment mentioned a "Diad," a holy relic of the Divinity of Two carried on the voyage and afterward lost or consumed.

Turning to the totem itself, the party compared the single scratch on each of their own medallions against the writings' description of something "covered in scratches," taking rubbings and striking the medallions against Chronicler Willem's shard to see if anything happened. Nothing did, though the exercise reminded them of an earlier occasion — when Cosimo, having taken command of a captured rice ship, released its crew a day out from port under a solemn vow invoking the mother and father, and wisps of light were visibly drawn from each of their necklaces into his invocation, a display so convincing that Nicolas, the young priest who witnessed it, took it for a genuine sign of the two's favor. Recalling it now raised the uneasy thought that whatever caused the Affliction in the old writings might not be as unfamiliar to them as they had assumed.

The party discussed these fragments and their implications at length, theorizing about the nature of the expedition, the Great Change, and the fate of the crew, before deciding to return to Newport to consult Randolph the Chronicler and Steel Hand.

Aboard the "Amada," they presented the writings to Randolph, along with the épée Cosimo had found; Randolph admired the blade, noting that its religious iconography suited a cleric of the two, though a duelist's weapon like this was an unusual — if not unheard of — choice for one of the faithful to carry. Randolph recognized Chronicler Willem's name and thought it plausible his grave lay at Old Port. He meticulously copied the fragmented texts but did not recognize the names Bayar or Grantos.

Mindful that their ship had been the target of sabotage in the past, the party agreed to keep their questioning discreet rather than draw attention by asking openly about a forty-year-old voyage on the King's Ship. Upon arrival in Newport, they sought out Steel Hand at the "Tattered Sail" tavern. He was not there when they arrived; Mani slipped the tavern girl a bribe of two bronze pieces for word of his whereabouts, and while she wouldn't say where he lived, she promised he'd be along within the half hour and that the party would be covering his food and drink for the evening. After a short wait, he was brought to their table. Plied with drink, Steel Hand revealed a great deal more about the fateful voyage, though it took patience and repetition to draw out. Werner's grandfather, De Rendal, had been the expedition's Sailing Master, not its captain. Bayar — whom Steel Hand called "the Badman" — was one of the two clergy aboard, and was responsible for the eventual destruction of the totem. Grantos, a native guide from the West who had "showed us the way," was very possibly the heretic mentioned elsewhere in the writings; his aid had been essential to crossing the Maelstrom, but he did not return with the ship. The natives they encountered in the West were, by Steel Hand's account, "very friendly" at first. Steel Hand confirmed he had once been "Iron Hand," the man who guarded the captive brought back from the West, and the first of the crew to succumb to the affliction. He also recalled a grueling stretch of the voyage spent hauling a boat, not the main ship, "over the ice" during an especially cold segment of the journey. Riu tried to examine his prosthetic hand directly, but found only a solid, seamless piece of metal fused to his arm, with no visible joints or mechanism; Steel Hand insisted it had worked fine before he fell ill, and had never worked since. Wary of being overheard as the questioning wore on, the party checked the room — only the tavern girl seemed to be paying them any real attention, keeping a close eye on how quickly the bottles she had brought were emptying.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• Piecing the writings and Steel Hand's account together, the party assembled a rough narrative: the King's Ship was forced by King Sebastian III to carry a heretic whose aid alone made crossing the Maelstrom possible, with a censure and a priest — one of them Bayar — aboard specifically to watch him. Where they landed, the natives were friendly at first and had a strange totem; when the two judged it too dangerous to leave standing, Bayar destroyed it — using the "Diad" to do so — and the fleeing ship was nearly overwhelmed by the effects even far out at sea.
  • The party suspected the totem's destruction, rather than the crew's later plague, may have been the true cause of the Great Change — and that the Maelstrom itself might have been sustained by the totem's power, meaning it may no longer bar the way west at all.
  • Comparing their own medallions to the writings' description of a scratched totem recalled an earlier occasion when one of Cosimo's rituals drew wisps of light from each of their necklaces, raising the uncomfortable possibility that the "Affliction" described in the writings has more in common with things the party has already witnessed than they would like.
  • The party confirmed that their own medallions each bear a single scratch, while another group entirely is known to mark itself with three; what that distinction actually means was left unclear, but it left them wondering just how closely their own necklaces might resemble the "totem" from the writings.
  • Chronicler Willem was murdered — stabbed in the back — rather than killed by plague as his marker claimed.
  • The heretic who helped the ship cross the Maelstrom on the way out did not make it back. Recalling what they already knew of wind witches, the party theorized that this "heretic" may in fact have been a captured wind witch, compelled by King Sebastian III to see the expedition through the Maelstrom.
  • Whether Bayar survived destroying the totem was left an open question; the party recalled Steel Hand's earlier claim that "the cleric" had returned to Old Port aboard the King's Ship, and reasoned the "sacrifice of Bayar" more likely meant the loss of the Diad itself than Bayar's own life.
  • Randolph raised the possibility that Chronicler Willem's own journals, if judged heretical, were never destroyed at all — only confiscated and filed away in the Church's secret index of banned writings, though he had no idea where, or even whether, such a collection actually exists.
  • With no official orders compelling them west — only the standing charge from their patron in Port Sardinia to try something the Admiralty's conventional tactics hadn't, since two years of Captain de Guzman's own efforts to intercept a wind witch at sea had already failed — the party weighed two ways forward: keep tracing the old expedition's route in search of a means to reach the West, or shift tactics and try to seize a wind witch ashore in a southern port instead, using the infiltration skills they had been building toward operating in enemy territory. They leaned toward continuing west, pending a few final questions for Steel Hand.
