  • The official Northern narrative is that Major Hubert was secretly working for the South all along, and that the Amada disappeared with him amid the confusion once this came to light.
  • The North has had a presence on the island for at least two years, though the temple under construction is running months ahead of schedule and its incoming clergy have not yet arrived.
  • The Stone Men have been largely subjugated and forced into slave labor alongside the local Islanders; only a small number remain free in their original home to the north, too few to be worth the trouble of retrieving.
  • The North has established a difficult but functional "Northern Passage" to this region, bypassing the Maelstrom — Perkins describes it as bitterly cold and thoroughly unpleasant, though passable.
  • The war with the South is in a state of official truce in the east (the Mainlands), but the conflict continues unofficially in the west; as far as Perkins knows, the South still has no way through but the Maelstrom itself, crossed only with the aid of their wind witches.
  • Studying the raiders' map properly for the first time, the party identified the "Stone Man home" (the mountain marked at its centre) and their "staircase to God" (a pyramid, the tower to their sky god), along with a long-ruined "Old Wall," a caravan route, a possible trading post, and a body of water the raiders described only as a place where "there are no more ships." Both the Stone Man home and the Old Wall lie a couple of weeks' walk across the desert, alongside a stretch marked with scorpions worth avoiding.
  • The party discussed how to manage the perception of their Islander companions, deciding that both Batu Batu and Leela would need to pretend to be slaves to avoid suspicion — a fiction that visibly troubled Batu Batu, given his own status as a Navy slave beside Leela's freedom.
  • Pressing the question of how a slave might be freed, the party learns that only an owner can grant freedom, that the freed slave customarily takes the former owner's name — as with Freeman Knowles, the freed Islander they met on Zylos — and that it requires formal paperwork and is rarely granted, typically only for truly exceptional service. Since the Navy owns Batu Batu, not the party, they have no power to free him themselves.
  • The party learned of a Southern port in the region — Perkins, deep in his cups, slurred the name almost past recognition ("Port Lisker," "Liz Gurr," "New Lisgar") — and let slip rumors of a significant pirate problem — some group operating "hiding in plain sight," close enough to strike at shipping yet impossible to locate.
  • Perkins also revealed that the port at the river delta remains small and poorly organized, with ships simply anchoring wherever the unpredictable depths allow, and that no shipbuilding of any kind has been established on this side of the Maelstrom.
  • Despite the years lost, the party's medallions show no sign of change, looking and feeling exactly as they did before the mist.
  • Passing through the settlement, the party sees no fortifications, cannon, or gun slits on any building, and nothing to suggest the town is braced for attack — only routine patrols, as though the surrounding desert is considered defense enough.
  • A massive, patrolled wall now blocks the river valley, preventing easy access to the coast.

docs.title: Items Gained
docs.text: • The official notice from the Divinity of Two declaring the party as heretics, which Knick Nab took from a public pillar.

docs.title: Items Lost
docs.text:
• Approximately three years of time.
  • Whatever gear remained in their sea chests aboard the missing Amada, now presumed unrecoverable.

docs.title: Events and Actions
docs.text:
Approaching the river gate they remembered from five years before, the party found it transformed: a new wall now ran the full width of the river valley, manned and lit with torches, clearly built to keep people from leaving rather than to keep anyone out. A low watchtower stood where the wall met the desert's edge, manned by a single guard and equipped with a Greek fire thrower to cover the approach. Cosimo judged a static illusion useless against a physical wall and gate — and doubly risky out in the open desert, where the constant drift of tumbleweed and heat shimmer would make anything frozen in place stand out. Noddy briefly weighed charming the tower's lone guard to sleep so the party could slip past below him, but the party held back rather than risk him being punished for dozing on watch, and confusing him instead was floated as a gentler option; in the end they settled on the simplest plan, skirting around through the desert, and kept Noddy's tricks in reserve only for the case that a guard at the gate itself actually challenged them. Noddy sent his seagull familiar, Pocket, up to scout, confirming the wall ran only to the edge of the river valley and stopped short of the open desert beyond.

Wrapped in cloth taken from the Stone Men raiders, the party pushed out into the dunes, wary enough of the giant scorpions rumored to hunt there that Riu deliberately altered his gait and dragged his feet rather than risk his usual footsteps giving him away. The going was brutal, sand shifting underfoot with every step, and once they had gone only a short distance the town and its wall vanished entirely behind them, leaving nothing but featureless dunes in every direction, disorienting in the same way as open sea. Noddy's uncanny sense of direction carried them east and then back north, and after a few hours of marching they returned to the edge of the river valley, shook the sand from their gear, and pressed on toward the coast. Along the way, Mani brooded aloud over being branded a heretic for a mission he had volunteered for out of loyalty to the Navy — recalling how he'd joined up to make something of himself after a difficult upbringing, only to survive the Maelstrom crossing and the giant spider queen and be rewarded with a heretic's brand — and began embracing a harder, more villainous edge to his personality, while the party debated wages owed, personal valuables carried, and how best to disguise themselves for what was to come. They also weighed what to do about a mounted messenger, should one overtake them on the road to the delta, and settled on a simple answer: pull him off his horse before he could report them.

By the early hours of the morning, they reached a rise overlooking a river delta supply depot that barely resembled the place they remembered — the water sat higher now, and the ground was crowded with new construction. What they saw was a spread of palm trees, twisting tidal channels, catwalks, an empty gallows, a warehouse under construction, and a canvas-covered tent. The largest vessel moored at the jetty was a single-masted cutter-like boat with someone visibly asleep aboard under a canvas cover, alongside a smaller pinnace for ferrying people and a wide, slow cargo boat built for hauling rather than speed. Further out to sea, a spyglass and a string of excellent sailing rolls from Werner identified six larger ships riding at anchor — two frigates, two brigs, a sloop, and a cutter — with the two brigs tentatively identified from later evidence as the merchant ships First Light and The Bull. Werner judged that fully crewing any of the bigger ships took far more hands than the party had, likely thirty to thirty-five for the sloop or cutter and somewhat fewer for the slower, less heavily worked brigs, and that only the small boat at the jetty was realistically within their reach.

With too few hands to simply seize a ship, Mani proposed forging a letter of authority and bluffing their way aboard, backed up by Noddy's charm if anyone balked, framing the whole scheme around a new personal motto extolling the virtue of audacity. He also settled on a stock threat to keep any commandeered crew compliant once they were underway: asking them, early and often, how long they thought they could tread water. Alternatives were floated and set aside for use only if things went loud: swimming out with Noddy's seagull setting small fires as a diversion, one of Cosimo's illusions to draw attention elsewhere, or conjuring a thick fog to cover a quiet escape. The party agreed that if the bluff collapsed, they would fall back to the small boat or simply run north along the beach.

Before committing, they weighed where to go once free. Noddy could sense a totem to the west worth investigating, and pirates were floated as a possible haven, but the party leaned toward sailing north around the island to the shipyard the Stone Men used, marked on their old map, rather than risk the Maelstrom crossing again in an unfamiliar boat. Noddy also offered a slower alternative — using his shapeshifting magic to study and impersonate a ranking Northern officer — but it demanded a full day he judged they couldn't spare, so the party pressed ahead with the forged-letter plan instead, agreeing to scout the warehouse first before committing to anything.

To gather intelligence first, Knick Nab and Noddy stealthed to the blind side of the warehouse and climbed its rough stone wall using Knick Nab's silk rope, discovering the roof was little more than woven reeds over a few support beams, with a canvas-covered vent hole in the middle for ventilation. Crossing it proved awkward: Knick Nab put a foot straight through the reeds and had to widen the hole to drop himself inside, while Noddy, unable to walk the beams safely, ended up levitating flat on his stomach and hauling himself across hand over hand. The noise nearly gave them away — a guard below asked "what's around back?" before being waved off by his partner — but both got inside undetected. There, Knick Nab found the warehouse full of food stores and barrels of wine and rum, and a small office stacked with logbooks; the most recent volumes recorded only imports of food and shipbuilding materials, nothing about arms or gunpowder, and named two ships, the First Light and The Bull, as recent deliveries. Digging back through older volumes turned up nothing but more of the same — months of imports and no record of anything ever going out — though the stacks of rum barrels throughout the warehouse were noted as flammable enough to serve as a diversion later if needed. His climb back out went less smoothly than his climb in — an attempt to leap for the roof's edge ended with him crashing into a barrel of cymbals below before he simply used the rope Noddy dropped for him.

With the ledgers checked, the party split into three groups and moved on the depot. Mani left his Navy uniform behind to pose as a plain sailor instead, reasoning that real Marines would ask too many questions of one of their own, and the party trimmed down what they carried rather than risk unusual gear giving the lie to their story. Thus disguised as "Corporal Hicks," Mani and Riu, the latter carrying the forged letter, approached the two guards at the warehouse front with a story of a shipwrecked crew returning to their ship; Noddy stood ready to charm the guards if the story faltered. Riu had spent the earlier hours crafting the forgery from a genuine document Major Hubert had given them in Port Zylos, rewriting its contents in the name of Admiral Codemar — reasoning that five years' silence gave Hubert's superior ample time for a promotion nobody at this outpost would know about — and carefully transferring the original letter's wax seal onto the new page, with Werner's help lending the whole effort administrative polish. The forged letter, and Mani's forceful bluster, carried the bluff completely: the guard, Apon, could read it himself — surprising the party — and deferred entirely to their word, organizing men to move supplies once pressed further.

Meanwhile, Knick Nab slipped past the tent holding around two dozen chained Islanders and Stone Men — some recognizable as villagers from the settlement they'd visited before — confirming they were shackled together in pairs rather than individually, and paused to look in on a badly beaten man locked in a gibbet nearby, held in place by a simple padlock on the cage's base; the party resolved to spring him during their escape, with Noddy's door-opening magic marked as the likely means. At the same time, Werner led Cosimo, Batu Batu, Leela, and Salter to a trio of trees a short distance away, each scored with the three slashes of the Triad and arranged in a triangle. Probing the sand with a rifle ramrod, Werner struck something solid a few inches down and began digging, uncovering the buried lid of what looked like a vault door and, beneath it, all six of the party's own footlockers, one bearing Knick Nab's name and the Triad's mark. The party scratched the names off the lockers before hauling them out, wary of being caught with six lockers belonging to known heretics.

With the guards thoroughly convinced, the enslaved Islanders and Stone Men were roused from the tent and put to work carrying barrels of water, rum, salt pork, and ships' biscuit down to the jetty, while the party's footlockers went aboard as well. Mani quietly asked Batu Batu to find out whether any of the other enslaved Islanders had experience at sea, in case extra hands were needed to help crew the boat. Werner made a point of telling Batu Batu he was a free man, though the declaration only confused him further given the ongoing loyalties at play. The session ended on a cliffhanger as the sergeant asleep aboard the boat stirred awake and began questioning the commotion around him.

docs.title: NPCs & Creatures
docs.text:
• Northern Marines: Guards at the supply depot, including one named Apon, who — unusually — could read, and after examining the party's forged letter deferred to it and helped organize the loading of supplies. His unnamed partner could not read.
  • Enslaved Islanders and Stone Men: A group of approximately two dozen prisoners — some recognizable as villagers from the Isle of Sands settlement, others Stone Men — shackled together in pairs by the ankle, held in a tent and forced to load supplies for the party.
  • Man in Gibbet: An unidentified, non-Islander prisoner being publicly punished in a cage secured by a simple padlock. He was alive but in very poor condition; Knick Nab looked in on him while passing.
  • Northern Sergeant: An NCO who was sleeping aboard the boat at the jetty and was roused by the party's activities at the end of the session.
  • Salter, Batu Batu, and Leela: Assisted Werner and Cosimo in excavating the buried footlockers from beneath the three marked trees.

docs.title: Locations
docs.text:
• River Delta Supply Depot (Isle of Sands): A makeshift port and warehouse area established by the Northern forces at the mouth of the river, featuring palm trees, tidal channels, catwalks, an empty gallows, a warehouse under construction, and a tent holding enslaved prisoners. Little of it matched the party's memory of the spot from years before; the water now sits higher and the site has been built up considerably. It serves as a logistics hub for the ships anchored offshore, worked by a single cutter-like boat, a pinnace, and a wide cargo boat moored at its jetty.
  • River Gate Wall: The fortification blocking the river valley leading out of the Isle of Sands town, now rebuilt to span the entire valley from edge to edge, guarded and torch-lit, with a low watchtower — armed with a Greek fire thrower — at the point where it meets the desert. It stops short of the open desert itself.

docs.title: Conflicts
docs.text:
• The session's primary conflict was a high-stakes social encounter, as the party bluffed their way past Northern guards to commandeer a boat and essential supplies for their escape.
  • Knick Nab and Noddy's rooftop infiltration of the warehouse nearly ended in disaster twice — a foot punched through the flimsy reed roof, and a guard below almost noticed the noise before being waved off by his partner.
  • The bluff nearly slipped when Mani and Riu described their ship to the warehouse guards as "shipwrecked" — the same story Knick Nab was, coincidentally, spinning to the guards over by the tent at that very moment, despite the two groups having had no chance to coordinate. Pressed on how they could have known to keep their story consistent with Knick Nab's, Riu covered the gap by claiming unusually sharp hearing, backed by a strong roll, and the guards let it pass.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• The party's personal footlockers had been mysteriously transported from the Amada and buried beneath a triangle of trees on the island, each marked with the sign of The Triad, suggesting the secret society is tracking and aiding them.
  • The party identified a Northern fleet of six ships offshore: two frigates, two brigs, a sloop, and a cutter. Logs found in the supply warehouse indicated recent deliveries from two merchant ships named the First Light and The Bull, which the party presumed were the two brigs; the ledgers otherwise recorded only food stores and shipbuilding materials, with no mention of arms or gunpowder. The names, captains, and purposes of the other vessels were unknown.
  • The Marines guarding the depot seemed to know little about the fleet itself — not the captains' names, nor whether the crews were still aboard after weeks at anchor — suggesting the depot's garrison operates largely in the dark about naval movements beyond their own resupply duties.
  • Werner estimated that fully crewing the sloop or cutter would take roughly thirty to thirty-five hands, with the brigs requiring somewhat fewer — far more than the party's nine could manage, ruling out an outright seizure of any of the larger ships.
  • The party discussed the status of their Islander companions, Batu Batu and Leela, concluding that while they could not officially be freed without causing confusion, they should be treated as free people.

docs.title: Items Gained
docs.text:
• The party recovered their six personal footlockers, buried beneath the three marked trees; their contents were not inspected before departure.
  • Riu forged a letter of authority in the name of Admiral Codemar, transferring the original wax seal from Major Hubert's letter onto the new document.
  • The party began loading a boat with several barrels of water, salt pork, biscuits, and rum.

docs.title: Items Lost
docs.text: • Nothing of note was lost.

docs.title: Events and Actions
docs.text:
With the mysterious prisoner still trapped in the gibbet by the jetty, the party moved to free him under cover of magic and misdirection. Since Cosimo remained a wanted man, he adopted a new alias, Shivbo, for the rest of the operation. Noddy conjured a dense fog around the cage, cutting visibility to barely a foot, while Cosimo raised a sphere of silence over the same spot so Knick Nab could work the padlock unheard. Mani drew Sergeant Perkins aside with an invented tale of Vice Admiral Codemar's impending visit to the outpost and the promise of a promotion, talking him into ordering a soldier to march the rest of the Islander laborers away from the jetty, while Werner kept the second sentry occupied with idle chat about his posting, deflecting questions with talk of "secret orders" he claimed he couldn't discuss. Inside the silenced fog bank, Knick Nab wrestled with a padlock stiffened by salt air and weather, finally forcing it open with a crack loud enough to startle him — though the sphere kept the sound from carrying — before dragging the barely conscious prisoner clear and using a moment's misdirection about a stray barrel to steer that same sentry, now wandering blind through the fog back toward his post, safely past without being noticed. Once the prisoner was aboard the boat, Cosimo raised an immobile illusion of a man still hanging in the cage to delay anyone noticing he was gone.

Freed from the gibbet, the man was too far gone to speak or stand and had to be carried the rest of the way. Up close, the party got their first good look at him: the remains of a once-fine leather doublet, scarred and battered as though from old weapon blows, along with boots and heavy trousers with a large buckle. His head was shaved but for a ridge of longer hair worn like a crest down the centre, and both bare arms were covered in an extensive array of tattoos, though the poor light and fog left the designs themselves unexamined. Raw chafing marked his wrists and ankles where he'd been bound, and patches of blackened skin showed the toll of his time in the cage. Riu began simple first aid, dribbling water onto a cloth to moisten the man's lips, judging that dehydration after days in the cage was the most immediate danger; he was in no state to be moved further than the bottom of the boat. As the boat cast off, Werner laid his own jacket over the man, both to keep him warm and to keep him out of sight.

As the party rowed away with Batu Batu and Salter on the oars, Noddy sent his familiar, the seagull Pocket, ahead to scout the anchored Northern fleet — two frigates, two brigs of differing size, a cutter, and a sloop, with the brigs riding closest to shore and the frigates furthest out. Accepting a heavy penalty for casting through an animal with no hands or voice, Noddy used a presence spell to sense roughly twenty souls aboard the larger of the two brigs, with only one man visibly on watch. While the party weighed their options, Werner discovered a sealed letter hidden among his own effects in the recovered footlockers, written hastily in Captain De Guzman's hand: the South had arrived, and De Guzman would try to meet the party a day or two down the coast to the south, having arranged for the footlockers themselves to be buried at the depot before he fled, exactly as previously discussed. With a destination now in hand, they debated keeping their small boat, boarding the heavily crewed brig, or chancing the faster but more complex cutter or sloop further out; Knick Nab's sailing expertise settled it, judging that with only a handful of capable sailors among them, a brig under their own control would still outsail either smaller vessel fully crewed by the enemy. Pocket then confirmed the second, smaller brig carried only about six souls.

Deciding against a riskier escape in their longboat, the party chose to capture the smaller of the two Northern brigs anchored offshore, agreeing to take it soft — through bluff and charm — with force as their fallback if the bluff failed. As they closed in, Cosimo cast a spell to weaken the iron of the two Islanders' leg shackles, and repeated blows with the back of a hatchet finally snapped one link of the chain joining them together, though the hatchet broke in the process. Mani and Noddy boarded first, alone, under the pretense of delivering secret orders via a forged letter, with Mani adopting the alias "Lieutenant Albert Campion" while Noddy stood ready to work his charms on the captain. The captain, roused from sleep and missing his jacket, grew suspicious of the invented orders, the unfamiliar name, and an offer of gold as compensation for the inconvenience, and moved to signal the other ships in the fleet. This forced the party's hand, and the rest of the crew scrambled aboard as Werner threatened the captain with a javelin while Cosimo cast a spell to muffle the sounds of the ensuing struggle. Noddy's charm on the captain failed to hold, so he cast confusion instead, leaving the man unable to give orders even as he armed himself with a harpoon in a daze.

The combat was swift and decisive. Knick Nab climbed to the fighting top and kicked the lookout there, shattering his ankle and dropping him where he stood, while Noddy's sleep spells took two more sailors out of the fight one by one. Werner threw his javelin, critically wounding the captain and pinning his arm to the mast, then invoked a fresh alias — "Corporal Corbin Dulock of the Royal Marines" — to order the rest of the crew to stand down. Faced with overwhelming force, the remaining two crewmen surrendered.

With the ship secured, Riu performed desperate emergency surgery on the captain, who was bleeding to death from the javelin wound. He tied off a tourniquet on the spot to keep him from dying on the deck, then cast a spell to slow the bleeding further; once the captain was moved into his cabin, Riu packed the wound with gunpowder and touched it off with a boarding axe heated white-hot by Noddy's magic — a dramatic, screaming ordeal that nonetheless left the captain alive, facing an estimated eighty days to recover. The party offered the surviving crew gold and safety in exchange for helping sail the ship, but the shaken sailors refused for now, so they were disarmed, gagged, and confined below decks alongside the two sleeping men, to be asked again once they'd had time to think it over. Werner stripped the captain of his weapons, keys, and signal flags. They debated how best to slip away unnoticed — Cosimo floated a static illusion to disguise the empty anchorage they'd be leaving behind — before settling on a plan to simply brazen it out: sail out openly with their own boat in tow, claim they were bound north on a quarantine run while secretly turning south for the coastal rendezvous with De Guzman, and keep a plague flag ready to raise if any pursuing ship demanded they stop.

docs.title: NPCs & Creatures
docs.text:
• Sergeant Perkins: A Northern NCO overseeing the loading of supplies and enslaved Islanders at the depot jetty. Mani talked him into sending the rest of the Islander laborers away from the jetty with an invented story about Vice Admiral Codemar's impending visit.
  • Captain of "The Bull": The commander of the merchant brig, found freshly roused with his jacket off and his powdered wig askew. He was confused by Noddy's magic, critically wounded by Werner, and saved by Riu's surgical intervention.
  • Crew of "The Bull": Six sailors who were quickly overwhelmed. One had his ankle shattered by Knick Nab, two were put to sleep by Noddy, and the remaining two surrendered.
  • The Man from the Gibbet: A badly beaten, unidentified prisoner freed from the gibbet at the depot this session. He is noted for his unusual appearance — a shaved head with a crest of longer hair, a worn and battered leather doublet, and arms completely covered in tattoos — and for the raw marks at his wrists and ankles from his bindings.
  • Freed Islanders: Two male Islanders freed from Northern service, still individually shackled but separated from the chain that had bound them leg-to-leg, and persuaded by Batu Batu to join the party with talk of freedom and good food. One gives his name as Tamiti.
  • Pocket: Noddy's familiar seagull, sent ahead to scout the anchored fleet and used to sense the number of crew aboard each of the two Northern brigs.

docs.title: Locations
docs.text:
• River Delta Supply Depot: The gibbet and boarding point from the previous session, where the party freed the man from the gibbet under cover of fog and silence before rowing out to the anchored fleet.
  • The Anchored Northern Fleet: Six vessels riding at anchor in the bay — two frigates, two brigs of differing size, a cutter, and a sloop — with the brigs closest to shore and the frigates furthest out. Noddy scouted the fleet with his familiar before the party settled on which ship to take.
  • The Brig "The Bull": A small, two-masted merchant brig belonging to the Northern fleet, anchored offshore from the depot, riding light with an all-but-empty hold as though its cargo had already been delivered. Most of the session takes place on and around this vessel as the party captures it.

docs.title: Conflicts
docs.text:
• A tense covert operation to free the man from the gibbet, relying on fog, a sphere of silence, a fabricated rumor of Vice Admiral Codemar's visit, and an illusory decoy to keep the guards from noticing.
  • A high-stakes social bluff against the brig's captain, which escalated into violence when it failed.
  • A brief but brutal melee in which the party systematically neutralized the ship's small crew to seize control of the vessel.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• The party fully committed to an act of piracy, capturing a Northern vessel by force.
  • A letter from Captain De Guzman, found hidden among Werner's recovered belongings, revealed that the South had arrived and that De Guzman intended to rendezvous with the party a day or two down the coast to the south — and explained that he had arranged for their footlockers to be buried at the depot before he fled, exactly as previously discussed.
  • They developed a clever strategy to escape the rest of the Northern fleet: sail out claiming to be bound north on a quarantine run, then quietly turn south for the rendezvous, keeping a plague flag ready as a deterrent to any pursuit.
  • Riu's medical skills were put to an extreme test, proving he could perform life-saving surgery under dire circumstances, though the captain faces an estimated eighty days of recovery.
  • The party learned that their new ship, "The Bull," is a merchant vessel with no cannons and only two swivel guns.
  • The party noted that "The Bull" was missing its own ship's boats, an unusual and potentially concerning situation for a vessel of its size.

docs.title: Items Gained
docs.text:
• A two-masted merchant brig, tentatively identified the previous session and confirmed as "The Bull."
  • The weapons, keys, and signal flags taken from the captured captain, along with the personal effects of the rest of the crew.
  • A sealed letter from Captain De Guzman, found hidden among Werner's recovered footlocker belongings.

docs.title: Items Lost
docs.text: • Werner's hatchet was broken while freeing the manacles of the two Islanders in the longboat, its head flying loose and gouging the boat's planking.

docs.title: Events and Actions
docs.text:
Still holding the six captive crewmen from "The Bull"—the wounded Captain De Torres and his five sailors, tied, searched, and gagged on deck since the previous night's fight—the party's first move was to get them out of earshot, hauling them below into the cramped crawl spaces under the fore and aft decks rather than the main hold, so they couldn't overhear the escape plan being hashed out above. With that done, the party spent the early morning hammering out a cover story before anyone came to investigate: they would run up a plague flag, claim disease had broken out aboard, signal the same by semaphore, and volunteer as little detail as possible if hailed. Getting the undermanned ship moving proved its own struggle—with only a handful of the party competent at sailing, Mani rallied everyone he could spare into a scratch crew, and between fumbled rigging and a leadership-fuelled push they managed to raise the main sails and haul up the anchor while Cosimo layered illusions over the ship to hide the change from anyone watching. Before they could finish, a boat crewed by soldiers from "The Caliper," led by a Corporal Vasquez, set off to investigate. Mani, posing as a lieutenant, met them at the rail and spun a story of a grounded ship, secret orders, and a doomed rescue mission, inventing the name "Lieutenant Trollmer" on the spot when pressed. When Vasquez demanded to see the captain, Noddy—disguised by illusion to look like the wounded Captain De Torres—staggered out feigning delirium and convinced the corporal to let them sail off to quarantine among a cluster of islands to the southeast, buying the party's escape.

With the boarding party gone, Werner searched the captain's cabin and returned with a chart of the region, one of roughly fifty aboard, marked with dead-reckoning position notes and a scatter of unexplained "K" marks attributed to a surveyor named Colchester; tellingly, every one of the fifty charts covered only the route between the port and the ice crossing, as though the ships that sailed it were never meant to go anywhere else. With the ship's boat under tow, Mani rode in it alongside Beck—armed, watchful, and keeping him apart from the rest of the pressed crew—and spent the better part of an hour building rapport, learning of the crew's grim history and the fleet's makeup while offering in return a claimed family history of smuggling goods between north and south. Meanwhile the others debated their heading—weighing an unknown southern route, a westward course toward rumoured pirates, and a known river delta to the north—before settling on the delta as their first stop in search of water and shelter. Riu split his attention between Captain De Torres, still unconscious in his cabin, and the badly weakened man freed from the gibbet the previous session, dribbling watered rum into him a little at a time in hopes of reviving him. Beck and the rest of the pressed crew were eventually won over with rum, coin, and a plain explanation of the situation, and set to work sailing in earnest.

An hour into their escape, with the Northern fleet's masts just dipping below the horizon, Noddy's seagull familiar Pocket spotted a two-masted ship raising sail behind them and closing fast. To gain speed, the party cut loose the boat they had been towing. Cosimo tried a string of illusions to throw the pursuit off—a shrinking decoy ship left adrift, then a shifting cloak thrown over "The Bull" itself—but the pursuing ship adjusted course to follow regardless, its wake no obstacle to whatever was tracking them, suggesting the tricks weren't working. Sent ahead for a closer look, Pocket confirmed it as the cutter "The Caliper," and reported a priestess of the Divinity of Two on its bow, in garb matching one glimpsed on the pier before the party fled port, gripping a staff in both hands—leading the party to suspect they were being magically tracked. Realizing they could not outrun their pursuer, they turned to fight, planning to close the distance and board.

As the ships charged one another, "The Caliper" fired its bow chasers, using chain shot that tore through "The Bull's" forward sail and yardarm; Noddy, already invisible and stripped down in preparation for his planned leap onto the enemy ship, was left dangling unseen from the wreckage of the rigging rather than pitched into the sea. The two freed Islanders were armed and warned that capture meant a return to slavery, while the crew's meagre arsenal of muskets, pistols, and swivel guns was distributed and mounted, and Mani—having just carved the names "Fate" and "Destiny" into his own pistols—took up a rifle. His first shot at the priestess went so wide it cost him the weapon; grabbing another, he fired again as the range closed, only for her magic to turn the ball aside and leave her with a graze. Cosimo readied a stun cloud he could summon anew each round to sweep the enemy's deck once the ships closed, planning to time it with grenades lobbed below, and then conjured a grand illusion of "Handsome Gulliver Gold," glowing and radiant, to leap aboard the enemy ship's bowsprit and denounce its crew as heretics—"You are heathens who challenge my avatar," he thundered, "turn back and repent your ways, lest you be bogged down and clouded in the stench of your own sin." As Noddy prepared to leap onto the enemy's mainmast to shatter it with sorcery, a scream of terror tore from the enemy's deck, followed by a tremendous cracking sound: a colossal kraken erupted from the sea between the two vessels, bringing the confrontation to a chaotic halt.

docs.title: NPCs & Creatures
docs.text:
• Beck: A captured sailor from "The Bull" and spokesman for its five pressed crew, who provided the party with intelligence on the Northern fleet and its operations. He told Mani he was a former northern whaler pressed into service after a criminal conviction, describing a brutal overland crossing hauling supply sleds across the ice—the same fate that put Captain De Torres aboard "The Bull." Riding under guard in the ship's boat as it was towed, he warmed further to Mani over an hour of conversation, remarking that the party "present themselves like pirates" and hearing in turn a claimed family history of smuggling between north and south.
  • Corporal Vasquez: An officer sent by boat from "The Caliper" to investigate "The Bull" shortly after the party seized it. He was talked out of boarding by Mani's fabricated orders, issued in the name of a "Lieutenant Trollmer," and Noddy's convincing impersonation of the wounded Captain De Torres.
  • Captain De Torres: The captured captain of "The Bull," who remains unconscious throughout the session. Noddy successfully impersonated him, disguised by illusion, to deceive the boarding party from "The Caliper."
  • The Man from the Gibbet: The badly weakened prisoner freed from the gibbet the previous session, still unconscious and unable to speak. Riu fed him watered rum through the day, hoping he might be well enough to rouse by the next.
  • Captain Colchester: The captain of the pursuing cutter, "The Caliper," identified as a mapper and surveyor.
  • Pocket: Noddy's seagull familiar, sent far out ahead to scout the pursuing ship, confirming it as "The Caliper" and reporting its crew, guns, and the priestess standing in its bow before the two ships came within unaided sight of each other.
  • Priestess of the Divinity of Two: A powerful, unnamed cleric seen on the bow of "The Caliper," gripping a staff in both hands, her garb matching a priestess glimpsed at the pier before the party fled port. She appeared to be tracking the party and was capable of deflecting projectiles.
  • The Two Freed Islanders: The pair rescued from slavery the previous session, including Tamiti; both were armed and warned that capture would mean a return to bondage as the party prepared for battle.
  • Handsome Gulliver Gold: Cosimo's illusory champion, conjured glowing and radiant to leap aboard "The Caliper" and denounce its crew as heretics before the fight was interrupted.
  • Kraken: A massive sea monster that surfaced between the two ships, interrupting their battle.

docs.title: Locations
docs.text: • The Sea off the Isle of Sands: The entire session took place on the open ocean, as the party fled north from the Northern fleet under a plague flag, pursued by "The Caliper" toward a river delta they hoped would offer fresh water and shelter.

docs.title: Conflicts
docs.text:
• A tense bluff aboard "The Bull" when a boat from "The Caliper," led by Corporal Vasquez, arrived to investigate, resolved through Mani's fabricated orders and Noddy's disguised impersonation of Captain De Torres.
  • A naval chase between the party's seventeen souls aboard "The Bull" and the faster, more heavily crewed Northern cutter "The Caliper," reckoned at some forty sailors and marines, which closed the distance despite Cosimo's illusions.
  • "The Caliper" opened fire, disabling "The Bull's" forward rigging with chain shot.
  • The session ended on a cliffhanger as a three-way conflict between the two ships and a kraken was about to begin.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• Having heard the six captive crewmen mutter and argue as they were subdued, Mani and Werner placed their accents as distinctly northern—specifically the cadence of men raised aboard whaling ships, not merely northern sailors in general.
  • The crew of "The Bull," including its unconscious captain, De Torres, are disaffected conscripts, making them potential allies.
  • The party gathered significant intelligence on the Northern fleet from Beck. A major supply route runs from the Isle of Sands north through The Shatters to an "ice crossing," escorted by the brig "The First Light," the sloop "The Fortnum" (captained by Herod), two unnamed frigates, and their pursuer, the cutter "The Caliper" (captained by Colchester, a mapper and surveyor). Beck also warned of pirates—remnants of the losing side of the war—operating to the west, the reason the fleet always sailed escorted, and mentioned a strong presence of the Church of the Two in the port town, including public lists of accused heretics.
  • One of the roughly fifty charts found in the captain's cabin showed the region in detail, marked with dead-reckoning position notes and several unexplained locations marked "K" and attributed to Colchester; their purpose remained unclear, though the party noted that all fifty charts covered only the route between the port and the ice crossing, suggesting the crews who sailed it were deliberately kept ignorant of the surrounding waters.
  • Weighing an unknown southern route against a westward course toward rumoured pirates and a known river delta to the north, the party chose to head north, reasoning it offered their best chance of finding fresh water—a tally of their stores showed roughly two weeks of food at normal consumption but barely a week of water at the same rate, with rationing able to stretch each further but leaving water as the true constraint on how far they could go.
  • The party concluded that the priestess was likely using magic to track them, rendering their illusions ineffective for concealment even after multiple attempts to throw off pursuit.

docs.title: Items Gained
docs.text:
• A detailed chart of the region, taken from the captain's cabin, marked with dead-reckoning notes and the unexplained "K" notations attributed to Colchester.
  • The ship's small armory: three muskets, three pistols, a blunderbuss, and two swivel guns—one already mounted, one they'd brought aboard themselves—along with powder and shot, all distributed and readied ahead of the fight.
  • An inventory of supplies aboard "The Bull"—salt pork, ship's biscuit, rice, sailcloth, and rum and fresh water in hogsheads—amounting to roughly two weeks of food but barely a week of water at normal consumption for seventeen souls.

docs.title: Items Lost
docs.text:
• The ship's boat, under tow since the party fled port, was cut loose to gain speed during the chase.
  • "The Bull's" forward sail and yardarm were destroyed by enemy cannon fire.

docs.title: Events and Actions
docs.text:
Rather than parley further, Werner steers "The Bull" straight at "The Caliper" to force the issue at close quarters, bellowing at the crew to crowd on every inch of sail and to cut free any rope or tentacle that comes aboard. Just as the two hulls close, someone on the enemy deck cries out "Kraken!" moments before a massive kraken erupts from the sea between them. The two ships collide and become entangled in a mess of rigging and grappling hooks, yardarms grinding together as crews scramble across both decks. The party immediately launches a full-scale assault, aiming to cripple the enemy's masts, crew, and command staff before the fight — or the kraken — turns on them. Mani opens with a shot at the priestess near the bow, but she deflects the bullet with a flick of her hand — an unsettling display of power for what should have been an easy kill.

As six tentacles rise from the water in three pairs, the kraken seizes hold of both ships almost at once, and the party turns the chaos to their advantage. Riu shields himself against stray gunfire before studying the creature's behavior; he judges it is simply hunting for food rather than acting with any malice or direction, and works to keep its attention fixed on "The Caliper" rather than "The Bull." Knick Nab goes further: rather than fighting the priestess a second time, he throws her down with a brutal hip-throw, declares he is "feeding her to the kraken," and leaves her within reach of the tentacles, which drag her screaming over the side and down into the beast's beak.

Noddy climbs into the enemy's rigging to shatter "The Caliper's" masts with Cracks Call. His first attempt is nearly cut short when the entangled yardarms threaten to sweep him off the ropes; he abandons the spell mid-cast and leaps to the safety of the second mast rather than risk the fall, then casts it successfully once he's clear, cracking the mast top to bottom in a shower of splinters, though it remains standing for now. A botched follow-up spell later in the fight leaves him badly rattled and short on confidence for the rest of the day. Riu adds grenades of his own throughout the battle — a first lobbed into the crowded midships that scatters the enemy crew and scorches one of the kraken's own tentacles in the blast, a second that explodes at the captain's feet, blowing him off them and finishing off the mast Noddy had already cracked, sending it crashing down into "The Bull's" own rigging, and a third at the base of the foremast that brings the rest of the enemy's rigging down and pitches two marines out of the fighting top.

Cosimo blankets the enemy's main deck and quarterdeck in choking Tear Cloud gas, casting it four times over the course of the battle, and conjures Handsome Gulliver Gold, his illusory champion, who strides among the enemy denouncing them as heretics before dissolving into another blinding cloud of gas. Balanced on the ship's rail, one of the priests tries to bind him in place with a compulsion spell — "You shall not pass. You shall stay there and be eaten by the kraken" — only to watch it pass through him harmlessly, since Gulliver Gold is no creature of flesh; Gulliver Gold merely drifts closer and answers that he serves the true will of the two, not the priest's "vile lies." As the ships finally pull apart, Noddy blankets "The Caliper" in a fog bank to cover their withdrawal, while Cosimo fires one last Tear Cloud into its retreating midships.

Amid the mayhem, Mani swings aboard the enemy ship on a rope and duels the second priest at the stern, opening with a rapier thrust that carves a dueling scar across the man's face before headbutting and grappling him to the deck. The priest recognizes Mani by his birth name, Manuel de Barret, and tries to compel him to freeze in place with a spell, but Mani's long-standing resistance to magic holds firm. As Mani closes in to finish him, the priest warns him, "When I'm gone, you'll be nothing — I'm the wellspring from which you flow," before Mani kills him. Werner shoots the enemy captain, stunning him and later blowing off one of his fingers as the man tries to flee the gas. On their own ship, the party deals with tentacles that come aboard; Leela attacks one with her formidable axe, hacking clean through it, and Werner uses a swivel gun to blow another one completely off.

With "The Caliper" dismasted, burning, and being consumed by the kraken, the party manages to cut their ship free and escape; Werner directs the crew through the tangle of severed rigging even as their own main yardarm takes a further battering from the enemy's collapsing mast. Knick Nab has a close call: trying to swing clear of Cosimo's gas cloud, he misses his landing and drops into the water right beside the kraken, forced to climb the hull's ropes one-handed while a stray tentacle gives chase. Noddy throws him a lifeline and Riu, drawing on what he'd learned of the creature, talks him through staying still to avoid drawing its attention; the party hauls him aboard as they pull away. A lone marine leaps for "The Bull's" sail as "The Caliper's" fore mast comes down beneath him, misses his landing, and falls hard onto the deck below, breaking a finger but surviving; Mani talks him into joining the crew afterward, sharing his own story of being cast out by the Navy and put on a heretic list without explanation.

In the fight's aftermath, wary that the Divinity of Two somehow tracked them down in the first place, the party strips the dead priest of anything identifying and feeds his body to the kraken rather than risk him being traced. They also set aside the idea of returning to scavenge "The Caliper's" wreckage as it burns and drifts, unwilling to go anywhere near the kraken's hunting grounds again. In a lighter moment, they resolve to send the Priesthood of the Two a taunting letter — written, they decide, on tanned kraken skin — announcing the fate of their priest. The session ends with the party having decisively won the battle, leaving "The Caliper" to be destroyed as they set course for a river mouth to repair the ship and take on water before continuing toward a pirate enclave to the south.

docs.title: NPCs & Creatures
docs.text:
• Kraken: A colossal sea monster roughly 80 feet across that erupted into the battle between the two ships, seizing sailors from both crews with its tentacles before ultimately fixing its destructive attention on "The Caliper" and devouring the priestess Knick Nab fed to it.
  • Priests of the Divinity of Two: Two priests were aboard "The Caliper." The priestess at the bow showed an unsettling display of power, deflecting Mani's opening shot with a flick of her hand, before Knick Nab threw her down and left her within reach of the kraken, which dragged her screaming over the side and devoured her. The priest at the stern recognized Mani by his birth name, Manuel de Barret, and tried to magically compel him to freeze in place, but Mani's long-standing resistance to magic held; Mani scarred him in their duel, and as he closed in to finish him the priest warned, "When I'm gone, you'll be nothing — I'm the wellspring from which you flow," before Mani killed him.
  • Captain Colchester: The captain of "The Caliper," stunned by an early shot from Werner, maimed when Werner shot off one of his fingers as he tried to flee the gas, and finally blown off his feet by a grenade from Riu. He was left aboard his doomed ship, taking with him whatever charts he had made as a noted mapper and surveyor of these waters.
  • Crew of "The Caliper": The Northern navy crew and marines were largely neutralized by the party's magical assaults and the chaos of the kraken attack.
  • Leela: Proved her combat prowess by fighting a kraken tentacle with her axe, severing it outright — a weapon that seemed particularly effective against the creature.
  • Handsome Gulliver Gold: Cosimo's illusory champion, conjured to fight alongside the party once again — striding among the enemy to denounce them as heretics before dissolving into another blinding cloud of Cosimo's tear gas. One of the priests tried to bind him in place with a compulsion spell, only to watch it pass harmlessly through him, since Gulliver Gold is no creature of flesh.
  • The Marine Recruit: A Northern marine who leapt for "The Bull's" sail rather than go down with "The Caliper's" fore mast, missed his landing, and fell hard onto the deck below, breaking a finger but surviving. Mani talked him into joining the crew afterward, sharing his own story of being cast out by the Navy and put on a heretic list without explanation — a fate the marine recognized as his own.
  • Shark Fin: The rescued pirate, still recovering aboard "The Bull" from his ordeal in the gibbet, shared what he knew of the dangerous waters to the south once the fighting had died down.

docs.title: Locations
docs.text: • The Sea off the Isle of Sands: The entire session takes place on the open ocean, on the decks of the entangled ships "The Bull" and "The Caliper."

docs.title: Conflicts
docs.text:
• A massive, chaotic three-way battle between the party's ship, a pursuing Northern cutter, and a kraken.
  • The party successfully boarded and systematically dismantled the command and crew of "The Caliper" through a combination of magic, ranged attacks, and melee combat, including Mani's duel with the second priest and Knick Nab's brutal takedown of the priestess.
  • The kraken's appearance was a decisive factor, absorbing much of the enemy crew's attention and, once the party fed it the wounded priestess, eliminating one of their most dangerous threats outright.
  • The party defended "The Bull" from kraken tentacles that came aboard, with Leela's axe and Werner's swivel gun driving them off.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• The priests of the Divinity of Two are powerful and knowledgeable foes, as one of them knew Mani's full name, suggesting the party is being specifically hunted. The stern priest's attempt to magically compel Mani to freeze in place failed against his long-standing, unexplained resistance to magic — a trait the party has come to rely on.
  • Leela's axe, recovered from the priests on Spider Island, is confirmed to be a weapon designed to fight giant creatures.
  • Riu's study of the kraken during the fight suggested it was driven by simple hunger rather than any directed malice or command, a read that let the party steer its attention toward the enemy ship rather than their own.
  • The party enthusiastically discussed how they could skin and process the severed kraken tentacle, hoping to fashion sword sheaths, climbing boots, and other trophies from its hide to commemorate their victory.
  • Shark Fin told the party of a dangerous, shoal-strewn region to the south called the Shatters, said to be infested with krakens like the one they just fought, and of established pirate enclaves further south still, reachable by ships that use "wind witches" to cross the maelstrom in a way the north cannot.
  • Mani asked Shark Fin whether he had heard of a Captain Barrows, but got no real answer — the exhausted pirate begged off, promising to address it later.
  • With "The Caliper" burning and lost, any detailed charts of these waters went down with Captain Colchester, its mapper and surveyor; the party's own charts cover nothing but the routes north, leaving them dependent on Shark Fin's word for anything to the south or west.
  • Werner ran the numbers on their water situation: emptying every spare food barrel and refilling it would stretch their supply to roughly 65 days for the whole crew, a calculation that factored into the decision to prioritize the river stop.
  • Following the battle, the party weighed their next steps and settled on a plan: sail up a nearby river to repair the ship and replenish their water supply before continuing on toward the pirate enclave to the south, setting aside for now the option of heading west toward another totem. They also began kicking around what to do once they reach the enclave — selling "The Bull" outright for something more manageable, or simply recruiting more crew and adding cannons to the ship they already have — without settling on either.

docs.title: Items Gained
docs.text:
• Kraken Tentacle: One of the kraken's arms, severed by Werner's swivel gun, remains on the deck of "The Bull," already earmarked for the cook, Batu Batu, to prepare.
  • Priest's Hat: Mani claimed the distinctive hat from the priest he defeated.

docs.title: Items Lost
docs.text:
• "The Bull" sustained damage to its main yardarm and rigging during the collision, worsened when "The Caliper's" collapsing mast came down into it, and its sails were holed by musket fire throughout the fight.
  • Two crew members were killed during the battle.

docs.title: Events and Actions
docs.text:
The session begins at sea aboard the party's newly acquired ship, the "Bull," in the aftermath of their escape from the pursuing "Caliper," which was set upon by a kraken mid-chase. The party briefly debates doubling back for the "Caliper's" charts and any survivors left behind, but decides the risk of the kraken still lurking nearby isn't worth it; they resolve instead to watch for the wreck as they pass its last known position and to seize the next vulnerable ship they cross. The escape left the "Bull" herself worse for wear, with one of her spars broken in the fight, adding repairs to their resupply needs. With that settled, they turn to their critical shortage of fresh water, eventually locating a previously unexplored river delta on the Isle of Sands coastline after some navigational uncertainty — Knick Nab at one point catching that the chart was being read upside down. Before setting out, the party takes stock of the new skills and spells each of them gained from their recent advancement, and confirms that Gus, a marine who was won over with a charm spell during the earlier boarding action, has thrown in with the crew.

At the delta, the party debates how to harvest "finger fruit" from the dangerous, animate trees that grow there without provoking them — the arid terrain offers nothing else worth gathering. An attempt to pull a bunch down using Noddy's rope-trick spell fails outright — the tree simply resists, stronger than the rope can manage — and a proposal to dangle the looted priest's body beneath the canopy as bait is floated but set aside. Riu offers to levitate up and chop free the highest bunch himself, but the others talk him out of it, unwilling to risk their only healer, and the party settles on simply felling a tree with cannon fire instead: they tow the ship's jollyboat in close to shore with a swivel gun mounted at its bow for a near point-blank shot, deliberately choosing a smaller specimen rather than the largest of the grove. Mani voices a moral objection, warning that they are diminishing the magic left in the world, but does not press the point, and the party proceeds. A single cannon shot brings the tree crashing down, where it continues to writhe on the ground; the priest's body is thrown onto it to keep it occupied while the party waits roughly an hour for it to still. Before finishing the job, the party casts a spell to sense any sentient presence and confirms, uncomfortably, that the tree was indeed thinking and aware; wary of the answer, they choose not to ask whether the surrounding, unfelled trees are sentient too. They press on regardless, using the magic rope to safely haul branches free of the mass and hack them apart, ultimately harvesting twelve bunches of finger fruit and a quantity of the tree's notably strong wood, setting aside its straightest sections as a future spar and musing that the wood might also serve for prosthetics. Afterward, Mani goes to the stump alone, places his hand on it, and internally apologizes for destroying a magical being, reaching out to the "third power" he believes is connected to their Medallions. He feels a distinct "pulse" in his hand in response — a significant event that he keeps to himself — and privately buries one of the harvested fruit beside the stump. He then carries the priest's remains, minus the arm already lost to the first tree, to a second, unfelled tree nearby, offering a word of thanks as he lays the body beneath its canopy — only for this tree to seize it just as readily, leaving the legs dangling visibly above as the party finishes loading their haul.

With their supplies replenished, the party commits to a new course. Guided by the rescued pirate, Shark Fin, they sail south for two weeks toward a pirate enclave known as "Drowned Man's Port," logging Shark Fin's periodic bearings themselves rather than relying on him alone. During the voyage, the former captain of the "Bull," who is revealed to be Werner De Rendal's cousin, De Torres, recovers from his injuries. After a long negotiation — during which Werner produces a large chunk of gold to sway him, then asks the rest of the party not to flash their wealth so openly again — De Torres agrees to join the crew as Master of Sail, sharing their goal of finding fortune and an eventual alternative way to return to the Old World; his one personal request is that word eventually reach his father confirming he is neither dead nor a heretic. Werner seals the agreement by passing rum around to celebrate. As they approach their destination, the party discusses their strategy for gaining entry to the port, their unease over how something has managed to locate them at sea even with an illusion concealing the ship, their long-term plans including the possibility of acquiring a faster vessel, and the sobering fact that between themselves, Gus, and De Torres, their crew still numbers only a handful of able hands — reinforcements they intend to find once ashore.

docs.title: NPCs & Creatures
docs.text:
• Shark Fin: The rescued pirate who is guiding the party to a safe port in the south. He is an able sailor with navigational skills.
  • De Torres: The former captain of the "Bull" and Werner De Rendal's cousin. He has agreed to serve as the party's Master of Sail.
  • Gus: A marine from the "Caliper" who jumped aboard the "Bull" during the earlier boarding action and was won over with a charm spell. He has since joined the crew, though his loyalties remain untested.
  • Finger Fruit Tree: A dangerous, animate tree that attacks creatures that stray too close. A presence-sensing spell confirmed this session that it is sentient. Its fruit is nourishing and its wood is exceptionally strong.
  • Kraken: The massive sea creature that attacked the pursuing "Caliper" mid-chase and is presumed to have destroyed it.
  • Stone Men: Dealt with by the party at the river delta while gathering fresh water, during a gap in the session's recording; the encounter itself goes unrecorded, and the second half picks up with the party already at the finger fruit grove.

docs.title: Locations
docs.text:
• The "Bull": The party's captured cargo ship and current base of operations — large, slow, and better suited to hauling cargo than to speed.
  • Unnamed River Delta (Isle of Sands): A previously unexplored river mouth on the Isle of Sands coastline, north of where the party escaped the "Caliper," where they gathered fresh water and harvested finger fruit. Unlike the swampy lowlands where the party has always found root before, this stretch of coast is arid and desert-like, its only substantial vegetation growing right at the water's edge.
  • Drowned Man's Port: An independent pirate haven roughly two weeks' sail to the south, and the party's current destination.

docs.title: Conflicts
docs.text:
• The party debated how to harvest finger fruit without provoking the animate trees; an attempt to pull a bunch down with a magic rope failed when the tree resisted, stronger than the rope could overcome.
  • Riu volunteered to levitate up and cut down the highest bunch himself, but the rest of the party talked him out of it, unwilling to risk their only healer, and turned to cannon fire instead.
  • Mani raised a moral objection to destroying one of the trees, but the party proceeded, felling it with a single cannon shot. It continued to writhe on the ground for some time afterward.
  • The body of the dead priest was thrown onto the felled tree as a distraction while it thrashed.
  • A presence-sensing spell confirmed the felled tree was sentient, deepening the party's unease even as they finished harvesting it.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• The party members shared the new skills and spells they gained from their recent level advancement: a displacement spell that offsets its target's apparent location to spoil roughly one attack in ten; a casting capable of raising a wall of packed earth; a smaller working that toughens a single solid object against damage; and sharper gunnery, sailing, and melee ability all around. A few minor skills were picked up almost as a joke, including riding and handling a camel. Rune-carving has also progressed far enough that scrolls may soon be within reach, provided someone learns the spell needed to read them.
  • The wood of the finger fruit tree is confirmed to be unusually strong and resilient, making it valuable for ship repairs or construction.
  • After placing his hand on the stump of the destroyed finger fruit tree and offering an internal apology, Mani felt a "pulse" from it. This experience, which he did not share with the others, solidified his belief in a "third power" beyond the Divinity of Two and gave him a new conviction that he must find a way to "return that magic to the world." He later planted one of the harvested fruit beside the stump, an unspoken gesture toward returning what had been taken.
  • Negotiation with De Torres: A major negotiation took place with Werner's cousin, De Torres.
    • The party explained their status as heretics and offered him the position of "Master of Sail," as they needed an experienced captain but did not want the role themselves.
    • De Torres was initially uninterested, stating his only goal was to return to his family in the Old World, a feat he considered nearly impossible. The promise of New World gold was not enough to sway him, though Werner's demonstration of a large chunk of gold prompted the rest of the party to privately agree not to flash their wealth so openly again.
    • The turning point came when the party revealed their long-term plan to find an alternative way back across the sea by allying with a southern "wind witch" or navigator. This new possibility convinced De Torres to join them.
    • He agreed to serve as Master of Sail, with the conditions that he could leave when he chose, taking his share of any profits, and that the party would facilitate his departure.
    • His one personal condition beyond the practical ones: that the party eventually help get word to his father that he is alive and not a heretic.
  • The party recounted for De Torres what they had learned of their grandfather, Peter De Rendal: his ship made it only partway back across the Maelstrom before he and most of his crew were killed — his grave later found at Zylos — most likely at the hands of the Divinity of Two.
  • A detailed discussion was held on how to gain entry to Drowned Man's Port. Success depends on finding an NPC who can vouch for them, so the party brainstormed a list of names to drop, including former associates of Captain De Guzman, Lieutenant Blaque, Major Hubert, Captain Barrows, and the Chronicler, Randolph. They considered but rejected invoking Nicolas, judging him too hostile toward known heretics to be safe.
  • Conversations with Shark Fin: The party had several key discussions with the rescued pirate.
    • Navigational Guidance: During the two-week voyage south, Shark Fin provided navigation by giving a new bearing every four hours, without revealing the destination's name until the end. The party logged these bearings to create their own chart.
    • Pre-Arrival Briefing: As they neared "The Drowned Man's Port," Shark Fin explained that entry is based on trust and reputation. He agreed to vouch that the party rescued him but explicitly refused to lie about their identities, as it would ruin his own standing. He was also visibly surprised and cowed by Cosimo's demonstration of fire magic, stating he had never seen anything like it, though he was aware of southern "navigators." When offered a position, he remained non-committal, stating he would "see what offers I get."
  • The party debated the suitability of the "Bull" for their future needs. Beyond simply wanting to outrun enemies, they were increasingly unsettled that something had managed to locate them at sea even with an illusion concealing the ship — raising the possibility of a "detect heretic" spell or similar means of tracking them — and agreed a faster vessel would be preferable for evading pursuit and potentially engaging in piracy or smuggling.
  • The party identified that De Torres's personal effects included a set of three masterwork +10 javelins (+20 vs. whales), fine enough that they screw apart into three pieces for storage and were evidently carried all the way from the Old World. These were returned to him upon their agreement.
