docs.text: (none)

docs.title: Items Lost
docs.text: (none)

docs.title: Events and Actions
docs.text:
Following the engagement with The Fortnum, The Medallion hove to within sight of land. Seabirds gathered around the ship as the crew assessed damage and work parties went aloft to address a cracked spar under Old Salter's direction, with the ship's carpenter overseeing repairs. Belowdecks, other hands swabbed out the gun decks and set the ship to rights; the crew, though short a few specialists such as a cooper, needed little direction and went about it smoothly.

Before anyone went over the side, Riu swept the ship with a detect presence spell out to forty feet and found nothing unusual among the crew. He was then lowered from the chains on a weighted rope, a small sack holding a cannonball tied at his waist to carry him under, while Mani took position above, harpoon in hand and watching the water, with Tyler and another Marine standing by with loaded rifles to relieve him. Equipped with water-breathing and water-vision spells, he descended in fathom increments to search for the two Divinity of Two priests — Arnim and Margot — who had gone overboard during the battle, pausing at each depth to look for movement and sweep the area methodically. He also tried, twice, to detect blood by scent using a spell that lent him an extraordinarily acute sense of smell, but both times found nothing beyond the ordinary decay and death that pervades the open sea — no trace of blood in particular. Around him drifted schools of fish, a strange half-solid, jelly-like creature that seemed to waver in and out of sight, and more than one small octopus and squid, but no sharks and no sign of the priests. He found nothing: the priests were simply gone.

While Riu searched below, Cosimo descended past the hold into the ballast, deep beneath the mast step, and performed a ritual there — pressing himself against the base of the main mast where it meets the keel — to commune with The Medallion and give the ship a voice through its bell, one ring for yes and two for no. Down among the ballast stone he noticed for the first time an odd, faintly blue-sheened rock mixed in with the ordinary ballast — a curiosity that, when raised later, turned out to be nothing more than slag, the leftover residue of iron-smelting commonly used to weigh ships down. Over an extended period of questioning, with young Tolly running messages between the command crew above and Cosimo deep in the bowels of the ship, the party methodically mapped the ship's capabilities. The Medallion could detect other ships and active magic within roughly twenty-five nautical miles and required no line of sight, being unaffected by weather or obstacles, though it could not detect sunken ships or treasure. It had water magic: the ability to raise and lower the water level beneath itself on command — the ability that had silently saved the ship from grounding on shoals in The Shatters. It could not distinguish between types of living creatures, could not detect individual items (it could not sense the Diad worn around a party member's neck), and could not steer itself or hold back water through a hull breach. It would give no answer at all to speculative or evaluative questions, only to concrete ones — it stayed silent when asked whether the crew's affection for it was returned, and again when asked whether it had approved of the party's removal of The Father, its original figurehead, months before. When asked whether it would permit a ram or metal reinforcement to be fitted to its prow at the next port, it answered yes — unsurprising, perhaps, since the prow had already been reinforced during an earlier retrofit, not for ramming but to carry the mortar it now mounts. The carved skulls projecting outward around the ship's exterior emit a constant fear effect on anyone who can see them, affecting crew and enemy alike — the same dread the party had felt when first approaching the ship in Drowned Man's Port, strong enough that their guide at the time had refused to come aboard at all. Most significantly, the ship can understand spoken orders without any spell: whoever holds the wheel need only speak aloud, and The Medallion will act, a discovery made easier to credit once Cosimo noted that the one skull mounted at the base of the mainmast faces backward, toward the wheel, as if listening for it.

Cosimo then attempted something more ambitious. Taking Noddy by the hand and placing his other hand on the mast step, he tried to channel power into the ship. The attempt miscarried badly: five of Noddy's power points were stripped away permanently and transferred into The Medallion. Noddy, feeling the life drain out of him, drew his knife. Cosimo offered to undo it if the knife were put away; Noddy refused the condition. Without waiting for the knife to be sheathed, Cosimo surrendered five of his own power points permanently to Noddy as replacement. Only after being restored did Noddy put the knife away and accept Cosimo's apology, though he called it the most frightening thing he had ever experienced and pressed, unsuccessfully, to have Cosimo confined to the brig over it. Knick Nab, summoned to investigate the commotion, accepted that it had been an accident and let the matter rest without a formal charge — noting only that no crew member had witnessed it. The net result was that The Medallion had been strengthened at Cosimo's permanent expense, and the incident left the two men at odds.

Shortly afterward, Noddy's familiar Pocket began behaving strangely at the bow railing, hopping and staring among the other seabirds. Pocket dove at one bird aggressively, but it dodged nimbly aside, and Pocket — sensing no danger from it — refused to press the attack, hopping back and signaling as much to Noddy. Only then did Noddy walk forward to look for himself, and with the aid of Mani's sailor's glass identified a pigeon on the rail — entirely the wrong bird for open ocean, and nothing like the gulls around it. He attempted a sleep spell; it failed. Mani, on the arbalest, fired and impaled the bird to the ship's railing. It was mortally wounded. Noddy, sensing that the pigeon might have been something like a familiar — someone's Pocket — chewed the healing root himself and tried to feed it to the bird, working an animal-healing skill he rarely had cause to use, but the wound was too severe and the bird died regardless. Only afterward did the strange question occur to him: homing pigeons fly only to a home they already know, and this ship had never been that pigeon's home. He could only conclude that whoever had sent it shared with it a bond much like his own with Pocket, and worried what the bird's death might mean for its owner.

Inspection of the body revealed a small message capsule attached to its leg — a court-martial offence under wartime naval regulations. The note was tiny and nearly illegible, but eventually read aloud as: "Were. C. Mason capable, honorable. Two gone. Orders stand. Held below, cannot help direct. Starboard quarter planking and midship rail weak. Serpent. R. [three slashes]."

The party worked through the message carefully. C. Mason was Captain Mason of The Fortnum — the note marking him as capable and honorable. "Two gone" referred to the two priests who had gone overboard. "Orders stand" meant The Fortnum was still operating under its original directive. "Held below" pointed to the writer being a prisoner, not merely a guest. The three slashes were recognized as the Mark of the Three, the Triad's secret signal. The initial R, combined with a man held prisoner aboard a naval vessel with a collection of carrier pigeons, led the party to conclude this was almost certainly Randolph the Chronicler, the Triad-connected Academy man who had kept cages of birds in his private room at The Crow's Nest in the Capitol. The tactical details were specific and deliberate: the Fortnum's starboard quarter planking and midship rail had been weakened by the sea serpent attack in The Shatters, and whoever wrote the note knew it.

Keyes was summoned and questioned. He confirmed that there had been a male passenger aboard The Fortnum: initially given the run of the ship and invited to dine with the captain, later confined under guard to a sail storeroom midship. The man had brought crates of pigeons aboard. Keyes's description of the captive matched Randolph. Keyes also confirmed the names of the two priests — Arnim and Margot — which the party already knew from questioning him after the previous engagement.

Jacopa, aloft, then called down to the deck: sails on the horizon, to windward. Noddy went aloft with his enchanted spyglass and confirmed it — the sail pattern was unmistakable. The Fortnum was back in sight.

The party debated their options. Running was possible given their speed advantage in the right conditions, but the Chronicler was aboard and The Fortnum's orders still stood — this was not a problem that would go away on its own. Knick Nab laid out the tactical parameters bluntly: at range, The Fortnum's greater firepower would win; up close, where the party's own abilities came into play, the odds evened out, as had already been proven once; and if the two ships came alongside long enough for The Fortnum's crew — outnumbering The Medallion's roughly ten to one, before counting muskets — to board, The Medallion would lose. It was pointed out that the one thing that had actually kept the crew alive in that earlier engagement wasn't any single spell so much as simply denying The Fortnum's gunners anything to aim at. The decision was made unanimously to engage and attempt a rescue, with two objectives agreed: free the captive, and slow The Fortnum enough that it could no longer give chase, without necessarily needing to sink it outright.

Several approaches were sketched. Cosimo's Earth Wall could seal The Fortnum's gun ports, buying perhaps twenty rounds before the crew could dig through. Noddy, invisible, could open a door directly into the ship's hull to slip a small party in and out, though he refused to risk Pocket doing the same and was wary of going in alone against so many. A stealthier option was raised — approaching under cover of darkness in the ship's dinghy, cloaked by one of Cosimo's illusions, while a decoy carrying lights sailed off in another direction. Knick Nab, who had once sailed under the boarding-minded Captain De Guzman, judged that closing to board was workable if the party's abilities could clear the way first. Severing the wheel's steering lines was raised as a way to cripple the ship for a couple of hours until repaired — a stopgap rather than a lasting fix, unlike knocking down a mast or holing the hull outright, either of which would put the ship out of the fight for good. Hot shot — cannonballs heated red-hot before loading, meant to set the target's timbers ablaze — and ordinary cannon fire aimed at the rudder and rigging were discussed as ways to cripple the ship without needing to sink it outright, exploiting the weakened starboard section under cover of darkness or illusion, though The Medallion carries only three guns a side, meaning a choice would have to be made between hot shot and dismasting fire rather than both. A simpler option was also floated — sending a small party aboard to hack through the shrouds and rigging with axes and swords, which would cripple the ship for hours with little risk — and Noddy suggested he could conjure a handful of illusory fires below decks to draw the crew away from the fight, though Cosimo could sustain at most two such illusions at once. Simply running was weighed too: The Medallion holds a speed advantage over The Fortnum in the right wind and could outdistance her for as long as the wind favored them. Noddy noted that his door-opening ability, used below the waterline, could probably flood and sink The Fortnum outright, but the party agreed to hold that in reserve rather than lean on it. Whether crippling the ship might be enough to make Captain Mason strike his colors was raised and set aside; Keyes, questioned again, described him as a professional who would fight hard to protect his crew but was no coward — he would yield only once convinced his duty was discharged. The party also concluded that whatever The Fortnum's standing orders were, they almost certainly concerned recovering the Diad, and agreed unanimously they would not surrender it under any circumstance. No final plan was settled; as the session ended, The Medallion was still hove to, The Fortnum's sails visible on the horizon, and the party had not yet begun to move.

docs.title: NPCs & Creatures
docs.text:
• Randolph the Chronicler — almost certainly the prisoner held aboard The Fortnum, identified from the carrier pigeon message signed "R" with the Mark of the Three and confirmed by Keyes's description of the captive.
  • Captain Mason — captain of The Fortnum. Described in the message as capable and honorable. Keyes adds that he is a professional who follows his orders and has little personal regard for the Divinity of Two; he would yield to preserve his crew if he believed his duty had been discharged.
  • Keyes — crew member of The Medallion, formerly of The Fortnum. Provided intelligence about the prisoner and named the priests.
  • Arnim — one of the two Divinity of Two priests aboard The Fortnum, named by Keyes. Went overboard during the previous battle. Not found by Riu's underwater search.
  • Margot — the other priest, a woman, gravely injured during the battle before going overboard. Not found by Riu's underwater search.
  • Jacopa — crew member of The Medallion, stationed aloft. Spotted The Fortnum's sails on the horizon.
  • Tolly — the ship's messenger boy, used as runner between Cosimo below and the command crew above during the communing session.

docs.title: Locations
docs.text:
• The Medallion — the party's ship, hove to within sight of land after the battle. Its capabilities were comprehensively mapped for the first time during this session.
  • At sea, close to shore — the engagement with The Fortnum took place within sight of land; The Medallion hove to in those same waters while the party took stock.

docs.title: Conflicts
docs.text:
• Riu's underwater search — Riu dived to locate the two priests who had gone overboard. Neither could be found by sight or scent.
  • The pigeon incident — Pocket drew attention to a pigeon on the bow railing. Noddy's sleep spell failed; Mani's arbalest shot mortally wounded the bird; Noddy's healing root could not save it. The pigeon died before it could be captured or questioned. A message capsule was recovered from the body.
  • The power transfer gone wrong — Cosimo's attempt to channel power into The Medallion accidentally stripped five power points permanently from Noddy. After a tense standoff — knife drawn, briefly — the matter was resolved when Cosimo surrendered five of his own power points to Noddy in compensation. Noddy pressed to have Cosimo confined to the brig over it, but with no crew witnesses and no formal charge laid, Knick Nab let the matter drop as an accident. Cosimo permanently lost five power points.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• The Medallion's capabilities are now mapped: detects ships and active magic within roughly twenty-five nautical miles; no line of sight required; unaffected by weather; cannot detect sunken ships or treasure; water magic allowing the ship to raise or lower the water level beneath itself on command; a constant fear effect projected by the skulls, requiring line of sight and bounded by some limited range, affecting all; cannot distinguish types of life; cannot detect individual items, including the Diad; cannot steer itself, pump out water, or seal hull breaches; will not answer speculative or evaluative questions; understands spoken orders from whoever holds the wheel without any ritual; and is amenable, in principle, to having a ram or metal reinforcement fitted to its prow at the next port.
  • The ship's ballast includes an odd, faintly blue-sheened stone noticed by Cosimo while communing with The Medallion, later identified as ordinary slag from iron-smelting, commonly used to weigh ships down.
  • The priests Arnim and Margot are not near the ship. Riu's search and The Medallion's own detection both confirm this. Their fate is unknown.
  • The Medallion has articles of agreement — the charter every hand aboard, the party included, signed upon joining — which are traditionally read aloud to all hands, by custom every Sunday.
  • Randolph the Chronicler is almost certainly a prisoner aboard The Fortnum. The carrier pigeon, the Mark of the Three, the initial R, and Keyes's description of a man with pigeons who was confined after initially being a guest of the captain all point to Randolph.
  • How the pigeon reached the ship at all is a mystery. Homing pigeons fly only to a home they already know, and this ship was never that pigeon's home. Noddy suspects its owner shares a bond with it much like his own with Pocket, and worries what the bird's death might mean for him.
  • The Fortnum's orders still stand. "Two gone. Orders stand." — the loss of both priests has not ended the ship's mission. Captain Mason will continue to pursue the party.
  • The Fortnum's starboard side has structural weaknesses from sea serpent damage: the quarter planking and the midship rail. The weakened midship rail would be an advantage in any boarding action.
  • Captain Mason is a professional who would yield to preserve his crew if he believed his duty was fulfilled, per Keyes. He is not a fanatic.
  • The party believes The Fortnum's orders concern recovering the Diad and agreed unanimously they will not surrender it under any circumstance.
  • The party voted unanimously to engage The Fortnum and attempt to rescue the prisoner. No final plan was settled; the session ended with options still being debated.
  • Not all ways of crippling a ship are equal. Cutting steering lines or rigging can be repaired within hours; knocking down a mast or holing the hull cannot be fixed at sea at all. Hot shot — cannonballs heated red-hot before loading — is meant to set an enemy ship ablaze, at the risk of the gun itself if mishandled.

docs.title: Items Gained
docs.text: • A message capsule and its note, recovered from the dead pigeon's leg — signed with the Mark of the Three and believed to have been sent by Randolph the Chronicler, held captive aboard The Fortnum.

docs.title: Items Lost
docs.text: • Cosimo permanently transferred five power points to The Medallion as a result of the channeling accident, compensating Noddy from his own reserves.

docs.title: The Curtain Falls, the Ships Collide
Events and Actions
docs.text:
Hours had passed since the previous clash with The Fortnum — long enough for the crew to repair The Medallion's spar, cracked but not broken in that exchange — when the session opened with the party still planning their boarding action, aware The Fortnum was closing from windward with the wind in its favor. While the crew waited on deck, Noddy was seen eating a raw scrap of the harpooned pigeon in front of several onlookers — most of the bird having been ruined by the harpoon that killed it — a small oddity that drew uneasy looks but no real concern. Rather than shout across the deck himself, Knick Nab sent Tolly, the ship's boy, to fetch Keyes — the former Fortnum crewman now sailing with The Medallion — for questioning. Keyes confirmed that Randolph was being held in the sail storeroom on the Orlop deck — one level below the gun deck — under two guards, with all his luggage, including his carrier pigeons. He described The Fortnum's strength: ten carronades to a side plus two long rifled bow guns, and roughly thirty Marines, somewhat reduced from the previous engagement. The powder room was deep below, served by its own stair up to the gun deck.

A tactical vote settled the question of timing. Rather than evading The Fortnum for five hours until nightfall, the party chose to engage immediately. Cosimo preferred waiting until night when his illusions would be more effective, and Riu agreed — resting and conserving magic was worth the delay. Werner abstained. Knick Nab voted to go now, as did De Torres, the master of sail, and Leopold, the quartermaster, who were keen on prize money and confident after the previous encounter. Three to two, they would fight in daylight. Before the fog could rise, The Fortnum opened fire from extreme range — two shots that sailed wide, but a clear sign the enemy was closing fast and forcing the party's hand.

The plan was shaped around Cosimo. As The Fortnum closed from windward, Cosimo cast a massive wall of fog — a semicircle of static illusion anchored to the bow, roughly 320 feet in radius, set to last fifty minutes. It rose from the water in a vast curtain, and the crew — who had heard about Cosimo's powers but not fully reckoned with their scale — fell silent before breaking into cheers. Knick Nab led three cheers for the "master of fog," and the crew, who had privately thought the title a joke, finally understood why he carried it. The Fortnum vanished into it.

With The Fortnum blind, Knick Nab maneuvered The Medallion to optimal sailing angle. Noddy, aloft, sent Pocket flying some 350 feet above the fog bank — well beyond the height a seagull would normally attempt — to serve as a living sensor, relaying the Fortnum's movements to the deck below. Cosimo then cast a second spell: Fantasm Two, producing a fully moving, visible duplicate of The Medallion — complete with a phantom likeness of Knick Nab at the helm — and positioning it just ahead of the real ship. When he then cancelled the fog — it fell like a curtain, condensing back into the sea in an instant — The Fortnum's crew found themselves looking at two identical vessels.

Before The Fortnum could fire, Cosimo sealed its gun ports with a static illusion of thick black smoke, forcing the gunners half-blind. The Fortnum fired anyway: its cannons went straight through the illusory ship, the shot passing harmlessly through empty air where wood should have been. The real Medallion's three guns returned fire aimed at the rigging: both shots found the upper sails, tearing them badly and compromising The Fortnum's ability to hold speed.

Knick Nab, at the wheel, tried something the crew had never attempted before: ordering The Medallion directly to rise a fathom in the water, hoping to make it easier to board over The Fortnum's taller rail. The ship did not respond, staying at its normal draft. Mani took position at the chains — the point of the hull that would come closest alongside an enemy ship — and laid out grapples, boarding pikes, belaying pins, and four pistols in preparation. Boarding netting was raised along The Medallion's rails to block any counter-boarders, with a single gap left near the port chains for their own boarding party to cross. Riu used a directed spell to deliver a grenade into the cluster of marines and their officer massed at The Fortnum's bow — four devastating shrapnel criticals. Two were killed outright or mortally wounded; two more were knocked down and severely injured. Werner fired the ship's arbalest with a grapple, embedding it near the base of The Fortnum's foremast — though the recoiling line snagged his own foot as it paid out.

Knick Nab drove The Medallion deliberately alongside The Fortnum. The hulls ground together with tremendous force: The Fortnum's hull buckled and bent below the waterline, beginning to take on water, and two upper spars of the main mast came down entangled in The Medallion's rigging. The Medallion took minor structural damage to the port bow but fared considerably better in the exchange. Then, as the ships continued moving in opposite directions, the arbalest rope — still embedded in the foremast — drew taut and snapped loose, whipping back across The Fortnum's deck. Four marines and their officer were caught by it: one killed instantly with a broken neck, one dying from internal heart damage, one flung to the deck with a badly sprung wrist and left reeling in terror, one knocked down by a bruising blow to the shoulder, and their officer struck with a torn muscle in his upper leg.

On the Medallion's side of the rail, five Fortnum Marines had managed to get shots off before the chaos fully engulfed them. Four missed. The fifth did not: Gus, one of the party's Marines stationed near the chains, took a musket ball through the bicep that shattered the bone. He went down screaming, arm useless and bleeding.

With the enemy still reeling from the whipped arbalest rope, Cosimo enhanced his own skill and cast a stun cloud onto The Fortnum's port side, targeting the ship's drummer boy directly. The cloud billowed outward like tear gas, catching the drummer, the lieutenant commanding the Marines, and several of the men still staggering from the rope's blow, stunning and half-blinding all of them at once.

Noddy cast Resilient Invisibility upon himself and winked out of sight, then opened a dimensional portal in the side of The Fortnum — a 3-foot-square aperture straddling the boundary between the gun deck and the Orlop deck, giving access to both from The Medallion's side. The ships were still in motion and the window was brief. Mani went first, leaping from the chains and tumbling through. Leela went second and simply walked through, then reached back and pulled the next person after her. Guy, a brawny southerner recruited to the crew as a boarder for exactly this kind of work, came through on her arm. Knick Nab dove through last with an extraordinary burst of acrobatics, and brought Riu with him.

The portal closed. The ships continued past one another and began to separate — The Fortnum's crew made no attempt to grapple in return, apparently having learned from the previous encounter that closing with The Medallion invited more chaos than advantage. The boarding party — Mani, Leela, Guy, Knick Nab, and Riu — was inside The Fortnum, cut off from The Medallion, in the near-total darkness of the Orlop deck: no gun ports let in daylight here, and only thin cracks between the planks and a distant hatch grating offered enough light to make out shapes. The headroom was barely five feet, forcing everyone into a stooping crouch and close-quarters fighting. The session ended there.

  • The Fortnum — the Northern Navy ship holding Randolph the Chronicler. After the engagement: hull buckled and leaking below the waterline, two upper spars of the main mast lost, upper sails torn, significant Marine casualties along both rails and at the bow.

docs.title: Conflicts
docs.text:
• Naval engagement — The Medallion vs. The Fortnum:
  • The Fortnum's cannons fired blind through Cosimo's illusory duplicate ship, doing no damage to The Medallion.
  • The Medallion's three guns struck The Fortnum's rigging — two critical hits, both tearing upper sails and compromising the ship's sailing speed.
  • Riu's grenade, delivered via a directed spell, struck the Fortnum's bow marines with four shrapnel criticals. Two killed (one immediately, one dying). Two others knocked down, severely wounded.
  • Five Fortnum Marines returned fire at The Medallion's rail: four missed; one shot hit Gus (broken bicep, arm useless, stunned and bleeding).
  • Ship collision: The Fortnum's hull badly buckled below the waterline; two main mast spars entangled and came down; The Medallion took minor port bow damage.
  • Werner's arbalest grapple rope snapped as ships separated, whipping across The Fortnum's deck — four marines hit (one dead with broken neck, one dying from heart damage, one with a sprung wrist and left shaken with fear, one knocked down with a shoulder blow) plus their officer, struck with a torn thigh muscle.
  • Cosimo's stun cloud (tier cloud) rolled across The Fortnum's port side like tear gas, engulfing the drummer, several marines, and the group already reeling from the arbalest rope's whip — stunning and blinding many of them at once.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• Randolph is on the Orlop deck in the sail storeroom, guarded by two sentries at all times, with all his possessions including his carrier pigeons.
  • The Fortnum's complement and armament as confirmed by Keyes: approximately 250 crew, roughly 30 Marines (reduced), 10 carronades per side and 2 long guns at the bow; powder room in the lowest decks, with a dedicated stair running directly up to the gun deck.
  • Without the priests, The Fortnum can no longer magically detect or track The Medallion. Arnim and Margot, who could see through illusions and locate the party, are confirmed gone.
  • The Orlop deck where Randolph is held is below the gun deck with no gun ports — it will be nearly pitch dark for anyone entering from outside, with only lantern light if any is lit.
  • The fear effect from The Medallion's skulls was noted to apply to all who can see them — crew and enemy alike — though The Medallion's own crew have grown accustomed to it.
  • Conditions at the time of engagement: mid-afternoon, wind from windward, weather slightly overcast with the glass dropping — Noddy predicted cloudy skies and an intermittently hidden quarter moon tonight.
  • Riu spoke of Randolph as "my master" while explaining why he wanted to go below decks himself rather than assist Cosimo's illusion from a distance — a personal connection to the chronicler that hasn't yet been explained.
  • Secondary ways to cripple The Fortnum were discussed at length before the engagement: flooding part of the hull, disabling the rudder or its below-deck steering cables, breaking the mainmast, or setting fire to the sail room. All were set aside in favor of the boarding plan, since Randolph's safety came first, but remain options if a future fight calls for them.
  • Handsome Gulliver Gold, Cosimo's illusory ally, was floated as an intimidation tactic for a future boarding action — appearing on the enemy deck after a tier cloud softened it up — though it was not summoned this session.
  • The Medallion's own senses were recapped before the engagement: it perceives out to roughly 25 nautical miles, though it cannot distinguish a person from a shark or other creature at that range, and it detects magic at the same distance — except, curiously, the Diads a couple of officers wear around their necks, one of them the Diad originally recovered on Spider Island, Leela's home island, which the ship's senses cannot pick up at all.
  • The Medallion's water magic is limited to raising itself in the water; it has no other magical actions of its own.
  • Orders to The Medallion must be given by whoever holds the wheel, and only by speaking directly to the skull mounted on the mainmast — the ship's sole command interface.

docs.title: Events and Actions
docs.text:
Before the boarding leap, Mani armed himself for what was to come: four grenades tucked into a satchel, his épée, a pistol, and a slow match he had kept burning since the ship action began. The Medallion had run alongside a large enemy warship in thick fog, with Cosimo maintaining an illusionary decoy vessel that drew the enemy's fire harmlessly to one side as the ships passed. Noddy opened a portal through the enemy ship's hull, giving the boarding party a choice of two openings into different decks. The party chose the lower opening: Mani leaped through first with a spectacular tumble, followed by Leela, who landed just as cleanly and hauled the crewman Boarder through bodily so he would not have to risk the jump himself. Knick Nab went next, landing well enough that he was able to reach back and pull Riu through after him. All five made it onto the enemy's orlop deck without incident, whereupon Noddy sealed the portal behind them and flew off invisibly into the fog, giggling.

Werner — now the ranking officer remaining aboard The Medallion — assumed command of the ship. He had spent the preceding exchange manning the harpoon gun at the bow, where his shot had driven a harpoon into the base of the Fortnum's mainmast; the towline whipped across the enemy weather deck and cut down several of the Marines massed there, and when it finally parted, the fraying strands scythed down several more still — save for one length that stayed fixed to the enemy's mast, dangling within reach. Gus, one of the Medallion's own Marines stationed at the chains, had been shot through the arm in the exchange and was being tended by the surgeon's mate. With that dangling strand the only route back to the boarding party, and one that would have dropped him among some two hundred enemy sailors, Werner chose to stay with his own ship instead, ordering the guns to sweep the enemy weather deck with canister shot while Tyler, the ship's Sergeant-at-Arms, added rifle fire, together suppressing the marines firing down from above. A bank of black smoke, another of Cosimo's illusions, hung over the enemy ship's gun deck, screening the boarding point from view.

The orlop deck was cramped and utterly dark, its ceiling barely five feet high with cannon fire thundering directly overhead on the gun deck — the party quickly judged that longer blades like rapiers would be a liability in such tight quarters. They had landed in the cable room, packed with the ship's heavy anchor cable and rigging. Riu cast a light spell onto a musket ball and gave it to Boarder to carry as a lantern, covering and uncovering it as needed. The light almost immediately drew attention from the corridor outside: a sailor armed with an axe came in to investigate, calling out that he'd seen the light again and wondering aloud if someone had struck a match. The party — having already agreed to fight first and ask questions later, sparing only the enemy captain should the chance arise — took cover to ambush him. Riu cast a shield spell on himself and drew his pistol as they waited; Leela, unable to hold herself back, broke cover early howling like a wild islander, her swing going wide before the fight properly began. Knick Nab's unarmed strike then caught the sailor under the arm and broke it with a sickening sound; as the man turned to flee, Mani lunged with his épée over a barrel and drove it through the sailor's hand, cracking the bone and splattering blood across the door frame. The sailor collapsed in shock, and the party dragged him back into the room. Knick Nab had Boarder search the body for anything useful, particularly keys, and stow it out of sight before they moved on. They debated their approach as they went: content to keep dealing with one or two curious sailors at a time as they had just done, they agreed that if a larger group came at them at once, they would fall back and make their stand in the corridor rather than get cornered inside a room.

The corridor outside ran the length of the ship, partly illuminated by light filtering down through the same grating hatches visible from the weather deck above, marking the main hatchways down through the gun deck. Moving cautiously toward the bow — where they had been told the sail room lay — the party looked into an adjacent compartment and found a damage control party being mustered for battle: a young midshipman driving three sailors to organise wooden plugs, mallets, bales of oakum, and great shaggy patches of sewn sailcloth, all ready to staunch hull damage, shouting at them to go faster. Riu stayed behind in the cable room, using his medicine skill to keep the bleeding sailor alive rather than press on with the others. Knick Nab charged in and bellowed "Surrender or die!" The midshipman called "Repel boarders!" and drew his sword, while his three sailors snatched up a mallet, an axe, and a knife from the workbench. Boarder threw the light fully open to illuminate the room as Leela vaulted onto the table to engage the sailor with the mallet and Mani closed on the one with the knife. The fight was over almost as soon as it began: Knick Nab executed a sweeping hip throw that hurled the midshipman to the deck and broke his elbow with a gut-wrenching crack, knocking him out.

The party pressed forward through the orlop deck to the sail room at the bow of the ship, where they found Randolph the Chronicler being held prisoner. Randolph told them he was honour-bound to remain as a captive, the terms of his captivity being tied somehow to the safety of his writings. He did not elaborate on the precise nature of this arrangement, and no one pressed him for details. His writings, he confirmed, were being held in the captain's cabin. The party began forming plans to recover them, though no definitive approach had been settled on by the time the session ended.

Throughout all of this, Noddy was moving invisibly above the fight, flying directly to the junction of the enemy ship's main mast where it met the lowest and largest yard rather than risk being seen climbing the rigging. He chose the spot deliberately: higher up, near the crow's nest, there would be less wood to catch and sailors posted who might fight the blaze, but nobody was stationed at the base of the main sail. His intention was to cast his Woodfires spell there, igniting the sail along with all the rigging above it, striking at the ship's ability to manoeuvre and fight.

  • Damage control fight: as the midshipman drew his sword and the three sailors armed themselves with a mallet, an axe, and a knife, Knick Nab swept the young midshipman with a hip throw, breaking his elbow and knocking him out (D critical) before the rest of the room could engage. docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
• Randolph the Chronicler is being held prisoner aboard the enemy warship. He is honour-bound to remain in exchange for something that protects his writings, though the exact terms were not explained.
  • His writings are currently held in the captain's cabin.
  • First Lieutenant Montoya is the most notable swordsman on the ship. Second Lieutenant Bush holds some responsibility connected to the gun deck.
  • Aboard ship, "rope" is just raw material; once a length is put to a purpose it takes a specific name, such as "cable" for the heavy line used for anchors, hauling, or careening — the cable room stores exactly this.
  • The orlop deck is a strong insertion point during battle because most of the crew is occupied on the weather deck and gun deck above, leaving the orlop largely unguarded.
  • The orlop deck is primarily a utility and storage deck; the galley normally sits one level up on the gun deck, and specialised stores such as the surgery, powder room, bread room, and spirit room are typically found down here — though on this ship the powder room is a level further down still, since the orlop deck itself sits above the waterline.
  • The enemy ship has a main mast that passes through the orlop deck; Noddy identified the lowest yard junction as the ideal point to ignite, since it was unguarded and would catch both the main sail and the rigging above it.

docs.title: Smoke, Steel, and a Serpent's Wake
Events and Actions
docs.text:
The session opened with a recap of the boarding party's progress through The Fortnum's orlop deck: Knick Nab, Mani, Leela, Boarder, and Riu had fought their way from the bow to the stern, clearing a damage-control party of carpenters and cutting down two musket-armed guards outside the sail room, where they found Randolph the Chronicler held prisoner. Randolph refused rescue, explaining that he had given his word not to attempt escape so long as the captain held his writings — kept, as far as he knew, in a case in the captain's cabin.

With that understood, the party turned toward the stern, where a lone guard stood watch by the aft mast and two routes led up to the gun deck above, alongside a narrow powder-monkey run the ship's boys used to ferry powder charges between decks. Mani closed on the guard playing a wounded marine fresh from the bow — staggering and calling out that a ball had come through — while Knick Nab circled in behind; between the ruse and a sweeping blow that slammed the guard against the wall, the two of them beat him unconscious without raising an alarm. Mani took the man's jacket, hat, and loaded musket to round out his disguise. When a powder monkey came scrambling up the run moments later, Leela's attempt to grab him went wide, but Knick Nab hauled the boy off the ladder by the ankles. A pistol at close range persuaded him to stay quiet; he was then searched for hidden knives, bound, gagged, and hidden behind stores in the cable room alongside the unconscious guard.

While the party regrouped, Noddy — having stayed behind invisible and airborne after opening the boarding portal in the previous session — set fire to the sailyard above the main mast, and the ship's crew began scrambling to fight the blaze. Riu climbed the powder-monkey run, stuck his head above the gun deck, and flung a lit grenade into a distant gun crew, spotting a stunned officer staring aft in the chaos before ducking back down; a second grenade followed shortly after to help clear the way. As two firefighting crews scrambled to answer the blaze, Noddy — still unseen overhead — struck the lead hose-bearer with a spell that sent him stumbling off the rigging; he crashed to the deck twenty feet below, losing both his weapon and his grip on the hose, and setting the firefighting effort back further still.

Under cover of the explosions and the drifting black fog that still clung to the deck, the party split to climb both stairways onto the gun deck at once, emerging onto a deck cleared for battle: bulkheads struck down into a single open space, with gun crews lining both sides for the length of the ship. Mani and Knick Nab emerged near the stern, close by the captain's cabin, while Boarder and Leela came up on the far side, where Leela's charge into an unsuspecting gun crew — screaming and swinging her axe — left no doubt to anyone watching that she was not one of the crew. Riu, still down by the powder-monkey ladder, grabbed a lit grenade, cackled at a nearby gun crew, and threatened them so convincingly that they abandoned their loaded cannon and fled toward the next crew down the line; he then teleported the grenade after them, and the blast tore through both crews at once. Spotting a powder charge the fleeing crew had left behind, Riu set it down further along the deck and dropped a second grenade on it as he withdrew; the blast tore through the ship's midsection just as an unnamed officer near the bow — presumably the gun deck's other lieutenant — was beginning to rally a counter-response, scattering the effort before it could take shape.

A figure carrying two sabers stepped out of the captain's cabin doorway to challenge Mani, demanding to know who dared board his ship; Knick Nab, glimpsing him from a distance, briefly took him for First Lieutenant Montoya, the ship's reputed finest swordsman, but when Mani gave his own name and guessed his opponent's rank, the man confirmed it: Second Lieutenant Bush. He fought with a skill well beyond any sailor or marine the party had faced before. The two duelled at length: Bush opened recklessly with a two-handed slash that landed one serious blow to Mani's shoulder while his second strike went wide, and Mani answered by driving his own blade through Bush's stomach, his cheek, and finally his knee, before finishing with a contemptuous, token slash to the shoulder with the flat of his blade and declaring him defeated. Bush collapsed, alive but bleeding heavily and incapacitated. Knick Nab, meanwhile, caught sight of a commanding figure further down the deck and, looking out past him toward the open sea, spotted something enormous and serpentine slithering slowly toward the ship from a great distance.

With the cabin's defender down, the party pressed inside. They found a locked sea chest, blew its lock open with a pinch of loose powder, and inside found Randolph's writing case — a large, book-crammed cabinet of his chronicles, seemingly matched to the books themselves — along with a second, empty case shaped for a pair of pistols, presumably the ones Captain Mason wore on his person, sitting alongside a shelf of the captain's scrolls and charts. Mani ran the writings down to Randolph in the sail room, telling him bluntly that the captain no longer held them and that he should come now if he wanted to live. Randolph, ever precise, made Mani swear to it formally — that the writings were no longer within Mason's control or command — and only once Mani had done so did he consider the oath discharged. He armed himself with his own blade and pistols, set a lantern to the sail room on his way out, and followed Mani back up through the ship. Along the way, Mani freed the bound powder monkey.

Above, Knick Nab climbed to the weather deck and found Captain Mason himself — pacing the deck with his hands clasped behind his back, coolly directing firefighting and gun crews through the chaos and reassuring wounded sailors without missing a beat — and warned him plainly that a sea serpent was inbound and both crews had bigger problems than each other. When Knick Nab announced himself as the enemy captain, it barely broke Mason's stride; he simply pressed for Knick Nab's actual intent, and on hearing the party meant to leave with the chronicler, flatly refused to allow it. Knick Nab withdrew below regardless. Aboard The Medallion, Werner — acting captain in Knick Nab's absence — ordered the crew, including the lookout Jacopa, to fix their attention solely on The Fortnum and watch for any signal. The party loaded Randolph's writing case and a chest of looted scrolls and charts into the captain's own jolly boat, still hanging from the stern — a boat rated to carry a captain and four rowers safely, but with the case and chest already aboard, there was safe room for barely two more — and gathered by the aft balcony to plan their escape, while out across the water the Medallion held position, watching for the signal to close in and pick them up.

Randolph then strode out onto the weather deck with Knick Nab in tow and, before the assembled crew, formally renounced his oath. Mason reminded him that the bargain had been safe passage in exchange for delivering his writings to the Academy unmolested and unviewed — but Randolph countered that the writings were no longer his to control, so the promise no longer bound either of them, and declared that he and Mason were enemies now rather than men in agreement. Mason simply said, "Understood," and ordered his marines to open fire. The session ended there, with the party caught between a newly hostile crew and an approaching sea serpent, still working out how to reach the boat and get everyone off the ship.

  • Captain Mason — commander of The Fortnum; unshaken by fire, chaos, the news of an approaching sea serpent, or even a stranger announcing himself as the enemy captain, coolly directing firefighting and gun crews throughout, and ultimately ordered his marines to fire on the party once Randolph renounced him.
  • Second Lieutenant Bush — met Mani in a duel outside the captain's cabin, briefly mistaken by Knick Nab at a distance for the more famous First Lieutenant Montoya; fought recklessly with a skill well beyond any ordinary sailor or marine the party had met, and was defeated, badly wounded but left alive.
  • Leela — fought alongside the boarding party, charging a gun crew on the Fortnum's gun deck.
  • Boarder — fought alongside the boarding party on the gun deck.
  • Jacopa — lookout aboard The Medallion, set to watch for the party's signal.

docs.title: Locations
docs.text:
• The Fortnum — the Northern Navy frigate under Captain Mason, the site of the entire boarding action: her orlop deck, gun deck, and captain's cabin.
  • The Fortnum's orlop deck — the utility deck below the guns: cramped, closet-sized officers' cabins near the bow, a sail room where Randolph was held prisoner, and a cable room used to store anchor rope and spare cordage. The party used the cable room to stash a beaten guard and a captured powder monkey, and Randolph put the sail room to the torch with a lantern on his way out.
  • The Fortnum's powder-monkey run — a narrow, steep passage between the hold, the orlop deck, and the gun deck, built ladder-scale for the ship's boys who ferry powder charges between decks; Riu used it to reach the gun deck unseen.
  • The Fortnum's gun deck — cleared to one open firing floor the length of the ship for battle, bulkheads struck down and gun crews packed to both sides; thick with drifting black fog throughout the boarding, which cost the defenders more visibility than it cost the party.
  • The Fortnum's captain's cabin — an unusually spacious, full-height cabin at the stern, its floor space shared with the mast projecting through the middle of the room; furnished with a bookcase and even a chair and table, a rare luxury aboard ship. It opens onto an outside balcony that doubles as a firing position for the stern chasers, and held a locked sea chest containing both Randolph's writing case and the captain's own scrolls and charts.
  • The Medallion — the party's ship, standing off in the fog and awaiting a signal to close in for extraction.

docs.title: Conflicts
docs.text: The party beat the orlop deck's remaining guard unconscious without raising an alarm or taking injury themselves. A captured powder monkey was subdued and bound unharmed. Noddy's fire spread across the Fortnum's main sailyard, drawing firefighting crews; one hose-bearer, struck by a spell that made him stumble, fell roughly twenty feet from the rigging, suffering a knee injury and dropping his weapon, which slowed efforts to fight the blaze. Riu's grenades were the most destructive weapon of the boarding: his first blind throw disrupted a distant gun crew, and later, after intimidating a second crew into abandoning their loaded cannon, he teleported a lit grenade onto them as they retreated, tearing through both that crew and the one they'd fled to; a third blast, made by planting an abandoned powder charge and dropping a grenade on it, scattered a lieutenant further up the deck just as he began rallying a counter-response. Mani's duel with Second Lieutenant Bush was the session's most serious fight: Mani took a solid early hit to the shoulder that left him stunned for a round, but recovered to inflict repeated wounds — through the stomach, the cheek, and finally the knee — before a final, contemptuous slash to the shoulder left Bush alive but incapacitated and bleeding heavily. Leela's charge into a second gun crew left several of its sailors down or scattered, though not all were killed.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text: Randolph confirmed that his oath to Captain Mason was specifically tied to the safekeeping of his writings — once those writings passed out of the captain's control, he considered himself released to act freely, and made a point of saying so publicly and formally before the ship's crew. The captain's cabin was confirmed to hold both Randolph's writing case and a separate stock of the captain's own maps and charts. The party also confirmed what they had been told of The Fortnum's command structure: the gun deck answers to two lieutenants, one stationed fore and one aft, though only the aft lieutenant, Bush, was ever engaged directly — the forward lieutenant was only glimpsed rallying his crew before Riu's explosion scattered the effort. A jolly boat, sized for a captain and four rowers, was confirmed still hanging off The Fortnum's stern as a possible means of escape, though its capacity would be tight once the party's own gear was loaded aboard. Knick Nab's warning to Captain Mason about the approaching sea serpent was heard and acknowledged, but did not stop Mason from ordering his marines to fire once Randolph renounced his captivity — leaving the party's escape plan unresolved as the session ended.

docs.title: The Illusory Beluga and the Wreck of the Fortnum
Events and Actions
docs.text:
The party picked up where the boarding action had left off: Knick Nab and Randolph the Chronicler stood at the top of the stairs leading to the weather deck, in full view of Captain Mason and his crew, while the main deck around them was in controlled chaos — fires being fought with grim efficiency, the enemy still unseen and unhit. Below, at the stern balcony outside the captain's cabin, Mani and Riu had already established a boat: the Fortnum's captain's jolly boat, hanging permanently from davits at the stern, loaded with the sea chest of maps and charts and Randolph's writing case. Its normal complement of six — four rowers, a coxswain, and the captain — was reduced to a safe capacity of four with the cargo aboard. Leela and Boarder, having taken a gun crew completely by surprise and driven off the survivors, were still down by that captured cannon; Noddy, invisible and airborne, was unaccounted for but expected to make his own way back to the Medallion by flying.

Mani called Boarder into the boat to lash down the chest, the writing case, and the two sabers taken earlier from Second Lieutenant Bush, then took up a watch position in the cabin doorway between the balcony and the ship's interior, arming himself with the rifle taken earlier from a downed marine. Riu levitated up past the balcony to examine the mechanism holding the boat aloft, learning that a single windlass on the stern drove both suspension ropes together through a pulley system, held from turning only by a simple loop of rope; freeing it safely would mean cranking the windlass to take the tension off that loop, not simply cutting or pulling on the rope. Riu tried to use telekinesis to lift the loop free, planning to follow up with a resistance spell to ease the rope's controlled descent, but the five pounds of force he could exert wasn't nearly enough to move it, and the plan went no further. Knick Nab, meanwhile, talked Randolph down from wanting to stay and fight, urging him toward the boat instead.

A marine called out from the port side, mistaking Mani in his stolen jacket for the missing Lieutenant Bush; Mani answered in character, ordered the man back to his post, and told him they were launching the captain's jolly boat, which sent him away satisfied. Below, Knick Nab returned to the captain's cabin and found Leela freshly out of combat, bloodied and still keyed up; he coaxed her back toward the boat as the gun deck behind them grew more aware of the commotion. A lieutenant — the same officer Riu had grenaded earlier in the boarding — gathered about four armed sailors and began charging down the deck toward the party. Mani bluffed them off with a shouted counter-order, claiming an inbound sea serpent and ordering the lieutenant to prepare the starboard guns for defense; the lieutenant, suspicious but unwilling to ignore the possibility, halted his men, sent a boy to confirm the story with the captain, and armed his sailors to wait rather than press the attack.

With the charge stalled, the party pulled everyone into the captain's cabin and barricaded the door — a set of keys taken earlier failed to fit the lock — by prying a heavy shelf off the wall and wedging it into place with Leela and Boarder's help. Before leaving, Mani took a moment to loot the captain's own sea chest (its original contents, mostly clothing and a case of pistols, had already been dumped out to make room for the salvaged maps and charts): his good, feathered captain's hat, his gold-brocaded dress coat with its epaulettes, and two small, unidentified pouches. Randolph, still stalling, insisted on staying to help hold a door that no longer needed defending; the others refused and made him get in the boat.

Pounding began on the barricaded door as Mani, Boarder, and Leela climbed into the boat, with one seat still held open for Randolph. Riu came up onto the deck to create a diversion, casting shield over himself and lighting a grenade to throw toward the ship's wheel. Before he could release it, Mason spotted him and fired his double-barreled pistol from across the deck — one shot found him for seven points of damage, the second was turned aside by a deflection spell. Riu threw the grenade anyway; the blast badly wounded both a cabin boy running a message and Captain Mason himself, cracking a finger on his hand and leaving him stunned, and left the wheel damaged though still usable. With the windlass's rope finally worked loose in the chaos, the boat began its descent, and Riu called down to Randolph that this was his last chance before jumping over the side himself, casting a resistance spell mid-fall to help slow the boat's uneven drop as it rode down the ship's side.

Randolph broke from the door at the last moment, released a message pigeon from his coat rather than another grenade, and dove cleanly into the water below, struggling once submerged under the weight of his own coat. Mason reappeared with a second pistol and fired twice more at Riu, but his wounds and the earlier stun spoiled his aim, and both shots missed. Knick Nab, climbing up past Riu as Riu dropped past him, reached the weather deck just long enough to offer Mason a mocking salute and a suggestion that he do something about the approaching sea serpent, then took a showy, well-rolled dive of his own off the stern into the water.

Once down in the water, Riu checked whether the Fortnum's rudder left any gap against the hull he could wedge his last grenade into, but the ship was already pulling away and there was no chance to make use of it. The party then gathered by the boat: Mani, Boarder, and Leela safely aboard with the cargo, Randolph hauled in after struggling with his coat, and Riu and Knick Nab electing to hang off either side of the hull rather than overload it further. Rowing back toward the Medallion, the party got their first clear look at the crippled Fortnum — her main mast and rigging from the mainsail up burned out and unusable, smoke still rising from the forward hold where the sail room fire had taken hold, and her speed badly cut.

Aboard the Medallion, Cosimo tracked the action through a spyglass borrowed from Werner, the acting captain, catching earlier glimpses of Knick Nab and the chronicler on the Fortnum's quarterdeck before they vanished belowdecks. Noddy arrived by air shortly after, reporting that he hadn't managed to breach the enemy hull as intended before he'd run low on range. As the Medallion closed to retrieve the rowboat, lookouts spotted the sea serpent — vastly larger than any encountered before, sinuous and impossibly fast, cresting the water as it overtook the ship — bearing down on a line that could carry it toward either the small boat or the Fortnum beyond. Werner, alerted, handed the wheel to De Torres, the Master of Sail, and ran forward to man the bow arbalest himself, watching the serpent's approach without firing.

Cosimo considered luring the serpent off with an illusion, but held off casting until the creature's presence was confirmed. Once it was, he cast Fantasm, conjuring a giant illusory beluga a hundred feet off, adding a scent effect to make it smell of fresh whale meat, and sent it swimming off at speed in the hope of pulling the serpent's attention toward the enemy ship. The serpent ignored it entirely and kept coming, passing directly beneath the rowboat without attacking — close enough that Knick Nab reached down and ran his hand along its scales in open awe as it slid past. Randolph, questioned about it, admitted he was fairly certain he had called the creature himself, using a rare Academy talent for communicating with birds and beasts that he'd never before tested on anything so large, and that it was meant to attack the Fortnum rather than the party — though he confessed some worry it might be confused given how close the boat now sat to the ship it was hunting. Pressed further as they rowed, he admitted this wasn't his first attempt: smaller serpents had gone after the Fortnum earlier in the voyage and been beaten off, on one occasion alongside a burst of mortar fire from an unexplained source that no one aboard had claimed responsibility for. In the midst of it, he also made a halting, largely unsuccessful attempt at introducing himself to Leela in broken Islander, admitting he'd been practising the language but had little skill in it yet.

The party chose not to interfere further and let the serpent continue on its way. It surfaced against the Fortnum in full view of both crews, weathering musket fire, cannon shot, and thrown weapons before crashing down across the ship's length hard enough to break her in two; ship and serpent both vanished beneath the waves shortly after. With the fight over, the party rowed the rest of the way to the Medallion, keeping the captured jolly boat rather than casting it off, to serve as an extra ship's launch.

Once safely aboard, the party debated their next move. They agreed to sail for the pirate enclave near Drowned Man's Port to retrieve Brother Nicolas, reasoning that the Diad they'd recovered earlier — believed to be the one binding Grantos — was too bound up in the power of the Divinity of Two for any of them to use safely, and that Nicolas was needed to command it. Concerned that the Divinity might be able to track the Diad if it lingered too long in one place, they agreed to make the stop brief and keep moving afterward rather than making camp at the pirate cove. They also voted, three to one, to keep Randolph confined below decks during the stop, both to keep the location of the pirate enclave out of his writings and to avoid drawing any attention to the Diad's whereabouts — Randolph, for his part, insisted he knew nothing of any hidden pirate base in these waters beyond the general rumor that local piracy had to come from somewhere, and noted that his recent months as a captive had left him further out of touch with naval gossip than usual. Along the way, they planned a side trip near Grantos's wreck to retrieve a magic item known to be resting in a shallow underwater cavern beneath a giant sea turtle, and intended to spend the sailing time questioning Randolph about the last three years: the fate of the war, why the party had been declared heretics, what became of their old ship and captain, what is known of the Shatters and the two priests who had served aboard the Fortnum, the Fortnum's original mission, and the nature of Randolph's own facility for calling beasts. Asked separately why his surrender to Captain Mason had seemed so formal, Randolph explained it as a simple matter of honor rather than anything magical: he had given Mason his word not to attempt escape, in exchange for a promise that his writings would be delivered safely to the Academy rather than confiscated, and considered that word void the moment the party carried the writing case off the ship themselves.

docs.text:
• Randolph the Chronicler — escaped the Fortnum with the party, struggling to swim in his heavy coat; revealed he had likely called the giant sea serpent himself using a rare Academy talent for communicating with birds and beasts, intending it to attack the Fortnum, and admitted surprise at its scale. Explained his oddly formal surrender to Captain Mason as an honor-bound bargain — his word not to escape in exchange for his writings being spared and delivered to the Academy — voided the moment the party took the writing case; also professed no knowledge of the hidden pirate enclave the party means to visit.
  • Captain Mason — wounded by Riu's grenade near the wheel (a broken finger, stunned) but kept fighting, firing a double-barreled pistol at Riu twice more before his ship was destroyed by the sea serpent; had earlier held Randolph captive under an honor-bound promise not to confiscate his writings, a bargain the party's escape with the writing case rendered moot; his fate after the serpent's attack is unknown.
  • Second Lieutenant Bush — not seen this session; his two sabers, taken after his defeat the session before, were recovered and stowed aboard the escape boat.
  • First Lieutenant Montoya — led a group of about four armed sailors in a charge toward the party's escape route; halted and held back after Mani bluffed him with a false order about an inbound sea serpent.
  • An unnamed cabin boy — critically wounded by the blast of Riu's diversionary grenade near the ship's wheel while relaying a message.
  • Leela — found freshly out of combat with a gun crew, bloodied and keyed up; coaxed back to the boat and rowed for the Medallion.
  • Boarder — helped secure the sea chest, writing case, and sabers in the jolly boat before the escape.
  • De Torres — took the wheel of the Medallion as Master of Sail when Werner ran forward to man the bow arbalest as the sea serpent approached.
  • The giant sea serpent — far larger than any previously encountered, fast and serpentine with no visible fins or limbs; passed directly beneath the party's boat without attacking before crashing down on and destroying the Fortnum.

docs.title: Locations
docs.text:
• The Fortnum — the boarding action's final stage: the weather deck in disarray from firefighting, the captain's cabin (looted and barricaded), and the stern balcony where the captain's jolly boat hung from its davits.
  • The open sea between the Fortnum and the Medallion — where the party swam and rowed to safety, and where the sea serpent passed beneath their boat.
  • The Medallion — the party's own ship, which closed in to recover the escaping party while directing its own response to the approaching serpent.

docs.title: Conflicts
docs.text: Riu's attempt to free the jolly boat's winch by force failed outright — five pounds of telekinetic force was nowhere near enough to overcome the mechanism. Riu's diversionary grenade near the ship's wheel fared better as a weapon than a distraction: before he could throw it, Mason spotted him and hit him once with a double-barreled pistol for seven points of damage, the second shot deflected; Riu threw the grenade anyway, and its blast critically wounded both a passing cabin boy and Captain Mason (a broken finger, stunned) and dented the wheel itself. Mason then fired twice more with a second pistol as Riu made his escape, both shots spoiled by his wounds and stun. No one else in the party was harmed reaching the boat. The session's decisive conflict was the sea serpent's assault on the Fortnum itself: after ignoring Cosimo's illusory beluga and passing peacefully beneath the party's boat, it surfaced against the enemy ship under a hail of musket fire, cannon shot, and thrown weapons, then crashed down across her length, breaking the ship in two before both vanished beneath the waves.

docs.title: Learnings and Discussions
docs.text:
The jolly boat's suspension mechanism was a single windlass driving both ropes together through a pulley, held from spinning only by a rope loop that had to be cranked loose rather than cut or pulled free by hand — a detail that cost the party valuable time under fire. Randolph confirmed, when asked, that he was very likely responsible for summoning the sea serpent using a facility with birds and beasts taught at the Academy — a broader skill than the one he and his fellow Chroniclers most often put to use for message-bird work — and admitted he'd had no expectation the talent could produce a beast of this size; he was visibly startled by the result and remarked that even after three years in the west he was still continually amazed by its wonders. The mortar fire that had inexplicably supported one of his earlier, smaller summonings against the Fortnum remains unaccounted for.

Pressed on why his surrender aboard the Fortnum had seemed so oddly formal, Randolph explained there had been nothing magical to it: he had simply given Captain Mason his word, as a matter of honor, not to attempt escape, and in exchange Mason had agreed not to confiscate his writings but to see them delivered safely to the Academy. Once the party took possession of the writing case, Mason no longer held anything to hold him to that bargain, and Randolph considered himself free to break his word without loss of honor. He also professed to know nothing of any hidden pirate enclave in these waters — only the general rumor that piracy in the region must have some base — noting that his recent months as a captive had left him less privy to naval gossip than before.

The party confirmed their belief that the Diad recovered earlier is the one binding Grantos, but that its power, being tied to the Divinity of Two, is incompatible with any of them — Brother Nicolas will be needed to command it and free Grantos. They resolved to sail for the pirate enclave near Drowned Man's Port to collect Nicolas, keep the visit brief to avoid the Divinity tracking the Diad, and keep Randolph confined below decks during the stop by a three-to-one vote, both to protect the pirates' location and to keep the Diad's whereabouts out of his writings. Riu, who now wears the Diad, recalled a past incident with a submerged clam that had seemed to resist his sensing it, and hoped that keeping the Diad on his own person might create similar interference against anyone trying to track it — though the party admitted they had no real certainty how, or whether, such tracking would actually work. They also planned a side trip to recover a magic item resting in a shallow cavern beneath a giant sea turtle near Grantos's wreck, and agreed to spend the voyage debriefing Randolph on developments of the last three years: the state of the war, the party's heretic status, the fate of their old ship and captain, the nature of the Shatters, the two priests who served aboard the Fortnum, the Fortnum's original mission, and what Randolph might know of magic beyond what the Divinity of Two itself teaches.

  • Two small, unidentified pouches taken from the captain's cabin.
  • Second Lieutenant Bush's two sabers, recovered and stowed in the escape boat.
  • The Fortnum's captain's jolly boat, kept as an additional launch for the Medallion.
